projects.name: Call.md
projects.tagline: Turn meetings into live agent loops
projects.taglineZh: 把会议变成实时智能体闭环
projects.description: Call.md is a desktop AI meeting assistant that records calls, transcribes microphone and system audio on separate channels, and provides live suggestions, conversation metrics, MCP tool automation, and three-part post-meeting summaries.
projects.descriptionZh: Call.md 是一款桌面 AI 会议助手，可录制、转录并分析会议，覆盖会前、会中与会后：分别转录麦克风与系统音频，实时生成建议和对话指标，按语境自动调用 MCP 工具，并在会后生成包含概览、要点和行动项的三段式摘要。
projects.content:
## Overview

Call\.md is a real\-time AI meeting assistant that works before, during, and after calls\. It captures microphone and system audio separately, generates live suggestions and conversation metrics, triggers configured MCP tools from conversation context, and produces three\-part summaries after the meeting\.

## Key Features

- Dual\-channel transcription captures microphone audio labeled as you and system audio labeled as them separately\.
- Live assist generates contextual suggestions and questions every 20 seconds based on recent conversation context\.
- Conversation metrics track talk ratio, speaking pace, questions asked, engagement score, and monologue detection\.
- MCP auto\-triggering scans conversations for information needs and calls configured MCP tools, displaying results inline\.
- Post\-meeting three\-part summaries provide an overview, key points by topic, and action items\.
- Workflow webhooks send structured meeting data to n8n, Zapier, or CRMs when a meeting ends\.

## Use Cases

- Sales calls where the assistant can fetch pricing or CRM information inline from conversation context\.
- Customer support calls where the assistant retrieves knowledge base documentation for reported errors\.
- Meeting preparation using AI\-generated probing questions and a dynamic discussion checklist\.
- Post\-meeting follow\-up by sending summaries and action items to workflow automation tools\.

## Getting Started

- Prerequisite: macOS 12\+ or Windows 10\+, plus a VideoDB API key\.
- Install Call\.md on macOS using the provided install script, then launch it from Applications or Spotlight\.
- Enter your VideoDB API key and grant requested system permissions\.
- Configure microphone capture, system audio capture, optional screen recording, and optional Google Calendar connection\.
- Click New Meeting, optionally run the Meeting Setup wizard, then click Start Recording\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs on macOS 12\+ (Monterey or later) or Windows 10\+; Linux support is coming soon\.
- Requires a VideoDB API key, with a free tier available\.
- AI features require internet connectivity\.
- On macOS, grant Microphone and Screen Recording permissions\.

## Before You Adopt

- No recognizable license was detected; verify permission to use, modify, and distribute the project before adoption\.
- Call\.md is currently available for macOS and Windows, with Linux support not yet available\.
- Its AI transcription and analysis depend on internet connectivity through VideoDB\.
- MCP tool automation relies on MCP servers and tools that users configure\.
- API keys are stored with encryption, and credentials are protected\.

projects.description: Open-source AI job search agent that scans job boards, scores each job 1–5 against your CV, tailors an ATS-friendly resume and cover letter, provides interview prep and an application tracker, and runs locally in AI coding CLIs.
projects.descriptionZh: career-ops 是开源 AI 求职搜索代理，可扫描招聘网站，按你的简历为职位打 1–5 分，定制 ATS 友好的简历与求职信，提供面试准备和申请跟踪；它协助填写申请，最终由你提交，并在本地 AI 编程 CLI 中运行，支持 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 等。
projects.content:
## Overview

career\-ops is an open\-source AI job search agent and job finder\. It scans job boards, scores jobs from 1 to 5 against your CV before you apply, tailors an ATS\-friendly resume and cover letter, offers interview preparation, and tracks applications\. It helps fill in each application while the user presses Submit, and runs locally in AI coding CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode\.

## Key Features

- Scans job boards for opportunities\.
- Scores each job from 1 to 5 against your CV before you apply\.
- Tailors an ATS\-friendly resume and cover letter\.
- Provides interview preparation and a job application tracker\.
- Helps fill in each application while you retain the final Submit action\.
- Runs locally in AI coding CLIs including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode\.

## Use Cases

- Scanning job boards and evaluating job fit before applying\.
- Tailoring resumes and cover letters for ATS\-friendly applications\.
- Preparing for interviews and tracking job applications in one workflow\.
- Filling in applications while keeping final submission under user control\.

## Getting Started

projects.content:
## Overview

Caveman is an open\-source project for coding agents with two main parts: a response skill that makes agent answers shorter and a local proxy that compresses what the agent reads\. The skill follows a controlled, answer\-first style while preserving negations, numbers, units, code, commands, paths, and error messages\. The proxy runs on the user's machine with the user's keys and keeps every original on disk so the agent can retrieve it\.

## Key Features

- Response skill shortens agent answers with an answer\-first style and preserves negations, numbers, units, code, commands, paths, and error messages\.
- Local CLI proxy compresses logs, JSON, CSV, YAML, and test output before the model reads them; the benchmark reports 33\.2% fewer input tokens across whole sessions\.
- Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot, and 30\+ more agents\.
- Provides /caveman, /ultracave, and /megacave modes plus commands for commit messages, code review, memory\-file compression, stats, and help\.
- Includes optional Auto model and effort routing, Blocks code mode, browse compression, and middleware for TypeScript or Python applications\.
- Runs locally, uses the user's keys and Claude Pro/Max login, and keeps original files on disk for retrieval\.

## Use Cases

- Reduce input and output token usage in coding\-agent sessions without changing code payloads\.
- Compress noisy command output, logs, test results, JSON, CSV, YAML, or web pages before an agent reads them\.
- Shorten responses in supported assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and Copilot using caveman response modes\.
- Shrink memory files such as CLAUDE\.md while keeping headings, code blocks, and paths intact\.

## Getting Started

- Install the full tool with npx @caveman\-ai/cli@latest, then start an agent with caveman claude or another supported command\. For the response skill alone, run npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman \-g and type /caveman if it does not start automatically\. The CLI requires Node\.js

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 22\.13 or newer\.
- Mac, Linux, or Windows\.
- Runs locally with your keys and Claude Pro/Max login; no hosted account is needed for local use\.
- Auto requires a free account\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The CLI requires Node\.js 22\.13 or newer\.
- HTML currently has no compressor, so that file type may not benefit and can incur overhead\.
- Blocks is pre\-release, Python\-only, and does not yet include a sandbox\.
- Auto routing requires an account, though the account is free\.
- Per\-request billing can make shorter answers offer no cost saving\.

## Overview

CC Workflow Studio provides a visual canvas for building and editing workflows for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and other AI agents\. Workflows are stored as JSON and can be exported as Markdown slash commands or agent skills, then run in supported AI coding agents\. The same workflow file can also be used through a CLI and an MCP server\.

## Key Features

- Visual drag\-and\-drop canvas for designing AI agent orchestrations without code
- Agentic engineering support with Sub\-Agent orchestration, Agent Skills, and MCP tool integration
- Edit with AI through natural\-language conversation, with native MCP server editing starting automatically
- One\-click export to ready\-to\-use formats and direct workflow runs from the editor
- Export support for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot Chat and CLI, OpenAI Codex CLI, Zoo Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Cursor
- The same workflow JSON can be used through the VS Code extension, CLI, and MCP server

## Use Cases

- Design multi\-agent workflows for AI coding agents on a visual canvas
- Export workflows as Markdown slash commands or agent skills for supported tools
- Refine workflows with natural\-language AI\-assisted editing
- Preview or run workflows outside VS Code through the CLI and MCP server

## Getting Started

- Install the VS Code extension with code \-\-install\-extension breaking\-brake\.cc\-wf\-studio
- Open the editor from the top\-right icon or run CC Workflow Studio: Open Editor from the Command Palette
- Add nodes from the palette and configure them, or use Edit with AI to create a workflow
- Save workflows as \.vscode/workflows/\*\.json and use the toolbar to export or run them
- Use the CLI with npx @cc\-wf\-studio/cli \-\-help or run the MCP server with npx @cc\-wf\-studio/mcp \-\-file \<workflow\.json\>

## Deployment & Requirements

- The VS Code extension lists compatibility with VS Code ^1\.80\.0
- The supported agent table lists required tools for each export target, including Claude Code, Copilot Chat, Copilot CLI, Codex CLI, Zoo Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Cursor

- The CLI and MCP server are available through npx packages

## Before You Adopt

projects.content:
## Overview

ccstatusline is a status line formatter for Claude Code CLI that displays model information, Git branch, token usage, session cost, usage metrics, timers, and other session data in the terminal\. It includes a TUI for configuring widgets, layouts, colors, themes, and Powerline\-style separators\.

## Key Features

- Powerline mode with arrow separators, customizable caps, built\-in themes, and auto\-alignment across multiple status lines\.
- Widgets covering model info, Git and JJ status, branches, worktrees, pull requests, CI checks, token and context metrics, usage windows, reset timers, session cost, memory, voice status, vim mode, sandbox status, and more\.
- TUI configuration for widget selection, labels, symbols, colors, gradients, separators, padding, flex modes, and line layouts\.
- Support for multiple status lines, full\-width layouts, raw\-value mode, global minimalist mode, custom commands, custom text, links, and configurable number formatting\.
- Config import/export to JSON with validation and preview, plus version pinning for global installs\.
- Cross\-platform terminal support including Windows\-specific handling and macOS usage lookup improvements\.

## Use Cases

- Customize the Claude Code CLI status line to show model, branch, token usage, and session metrics at a glance\.
- Build Powerline\-styled terminal status lines with themes and aligned multi\-line layouts\.
- Monitor Git or JJ repository state, pull requests, CI checks, and worktree details from the status line\.
- Track usage windows, reset timers, costs, cache metrics, and context usage during Claude Code sessions\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Moving from an auto\-updating install requires uninstalling through the TUI before reinstalling with the version pinning flow\.
- Cached Git commands are bounded by a five\-second timeout so stalled Git invocations cannot block the status line indefinitely\.
- Invalid settings files are not overwritten; defaults render in memory and an invalid\-config warning is shown\.
- Uninstalling preserves ccstatusline settings\.

projects.descriptionZh: Chatterbox 是 Resemble AI 推出的开源文本转语音模型系列，包含多语言、低延迟以及面向设备端和 CPU 的变体，支持语音克隆与语音生成。
projects.content:
## Overview

Chatterbox is a family of state\-of\-the\-art, open\-source text\-to\-speech models by Resemble AI\. The README describes Chatterbox Multilingual V3 as the latest general\-purpose multilingual TTS model, alongside Turbo and Nano variants for low\-latency and resource\-constrained deployments\. The project is described as retired research as of August 2026 and no longer maintained, with code kept public as an archive under the MIT license\.

## Key Features

- Chatterbox Multilingual V3 is a 0\.5B\-parameter general\-purpose multilingual TTS model with improved speaker similarity and reduced hallucinations across languages\.
- Chatterbox\-Turbo is a 350M\-parameter English model for low\-latency voice agents, using a distilled speech\-token\-to\-mel decoder that reduces generation from 10 steps to one\.
- Turbo and Nano natively support paralinguistic tags such as \[cough\], \[laugh\], and \[chuckle\]\.
- Chatterbox\-Nano is a 110M\-parameter model sharing Turbo’s architecture, targeting on\-device and CPU inference and claimed to run 3x faster than realtime on 8 CPU cores\.
- The Single Language Pack provides dedicated finetunes for priority languages and regional variants, including Chinese, Latam Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Spain Spanish, Portugal Portuguese, and Hindi\.
- Generated audio includes Perth neural watermarking intended to survive compression and editing while maintaining detection accuracy\.

## Use Cases

- Cross\-language voice cloning and multilingual speech generation for global applications and localization\.
- Low\-latency English voice agents and production speech interfaces\.
- On\-device or CPU inference where memory and latency budgets are tight\.
- Narration and creative workflows using paralinguistic tags for realism\.

## Getting Started

- Install from PyPI with pip install chatterbox\-tts\.
- Alternatively, clone the repository, enter the chatterbox directory, and install from source with pip install \-e \.
- Python examples load ChatterboxTurboTTS, ChatterboxTTS, or ChatterboxMultilingualTTS from pretrained checkpoints and generate audio; voice cloning examples use a reference audio clip\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The project was developed and tested on Python 3\.11 on Debian 11, with dependency versions pinned in pyproject\.toml\.
- Examples can run on cuda, cpu, or mps devices; Nano targets CPU and on\-device inference\.
- Turbo is described as using less compute and VRAM than previous models; Nano targets tight memory and latency budgets\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is retired and no longer maintained\.
- The repository is an archive with no support, updates, or paid tier\.
- Resemble AI states it does not sell TTS or voice cloning and that this repository is not a product\.
- Voice cloning output can inherit the reference clip’s accent if the reference language does not match the language tag\.

Chatterbox 是 Resemble AI 推出的一系列先进开源文本转语音模型。README 将 Chatterbox Multilingual V3 描述为最新的通用多语言 TTS 模型，并与面向低延迟和资源受限部署的 Turbo、Nano 变体并列。项目说明指出，截至 2026 年 8 月，Chatterbox 已退役研究且不再维护，代码以 MIT 许可证作为存档公开保留。

## 核心功能

- Chatterbox Multilingual V3 是 0\.5B 参数的通用多语言 TTS 模型，提升跨语言说话人相似度并减少幻觉。Chatterbox\-Turbo 是 350M 参数的英语模型，面向低延迟语音代理，使用蒸馏的语音 token 到 mel 解码器，将生成从 10 步降至 1 步。Turbo 与 Nano 原生支持 \[cough\]、\[laugh\]、\[chuckle\] 等副语言标签。Chatterbox\-Nano 是 110M 参数模型，沿用 Turbo 架构，面向设备端与 CPU 推理，README 称其在 8 个 CPU

## 适用场景

- 跨语言语音克隆与多语言语音生成，适用于全球应用和本地化。低延迟英语语音代理与生产级语音界面。内存和延迟预算紧张时的设备端或 CPU 推理。使用副语言标签增强真实感的旁白与创意工作流。

## 快速开始

- 可通过 pip install chatterbox\-tts 从 PyPI 安装。也可克隆仓库，进入 chatterbox 目录后执行 pip install \-e \. 从源码安装。Python 示例通过 ChatterboxTurboTTS、ChatterboxTTS 或 ChatterboxMultilingualTTS 从预训练检查点加载模型并生成音频；语音克隆示例使用参考音频片段。

## 部署与要求

- 项目在 Debian 11 上使用 Python 3\.11 开发和测试，依赖版本固定在 pyproject\.toml 中。示例可运行于 cuda、cpu 或 mps 设备；Nano 面向 CPU 与设备端推理。Turbo 使用更少计算和显存；Nano 面向紧张的内存与延迟预算。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

Checkmate is an open\-source, self\-hosted uptime and infrastructure monitoring application\. It regularly checks whether servers and websites are accessible and performing as expected, then provides real\-time alerts and reports on availability, downtime, and response time\. The repository includes both the frontend and backend, and an optional Capture agent adds CPU, RAM, disk, and temperature insights from remote servers\.

## Key Features

- Uptime and response\-time checks for servers and websites, with real\-time alerts and reports on availability, downtime, and response time\.
- Self\-hosted application with frontend and backend included in the repository\.
- Optional Capture agent for CPU, RAM, disk, and temperature data on remote servers; it runs on Linux, Windows, Mac, Raspberry Pi, or any device that can run Go\.
- Used in production to monitor 1,600\+ servers on a single deployment, with no reported performance bottlenecks or significant operational issues\.
- Horizontal scaling through dedicated worker nodes that share check load via MongoDB, documented for more than 5,000 servers\.
- Heartbeat monitors for cron jobs, backups, and scheduled tasks through ping URLs\.

## Use Cases

- Monitor server and website uptime and response times before users notice outages\.
- Track hardware metrics such as CPU, RAM, disk, and temperature with the optional Capture agent\.
- Monitor cron jobs, backups, and scheduled tasks using passive heartbeat monitors\.
- Run a self\-hosted monitoring setup where infrastructure data remains under your control\.

## Getting Started

- Ensure Docker with Docker Compose is installed; Git is only needed if you want to build the image yourself\.
- Download the reference Docker Compose file, generate a JWT secret, and start the services with Docker Compose\.
- Open the app on the default port 52345; set CLIENT\_HOST if the app is reached at another origin\.
- Optionally deploy Capture on servers where you want hardware metrics\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker with Docker Compose installed\.
- MongoDB is required; the reference Compose file starts it, or configure DB\_CONNECTION\_STRING to use an external MongoDB instance\.
- Required configuration includes DB\_CONNECTION\_STRING, JWT\_SECRET, and CLIENT\_HOST\.
- Docker TLS monitors and Checkmate Connect enrollment require ENCRYPTION\_KEY\.
- For TLS, place a reverse proxy such as Caddy, Traefik, or nginx in front of port 52345\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- MongoDB is an external required dependency even when using the all\-in\-one Checkmate image\.
- Checkmate sends a small anonymous telemetry report once per installation per day\.
- The Kubernetes Helm chart has not yet migrated to the all\-in\-one image\.
- Capture\-backed Docker monitors do not provide restart counts, mounts, published host\-port bindings, or container logs\.
- The Docker daemon does not enable TLS by default, so remote daemon monitoring requires TLS setup\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Chili3D is an open\-source browser\-based 3D CAD application built with TypeScript\. It compiles OpenCascade (OCCT) to WebAssembly and renders through Three\.js, while AI\-assisted, parametric, and direct modeling share one document, viewport, and undo stack\.

## Key Features

- A built\-in AI assistant runs in the browser and reads and writes the same document, selection, feature tree, and undo stack as regular commands\.
- Parametric modeling provides an ordered feature list, editable 2D sketches with constraints, document variables, and stable references\.
- Direct modeling supports basic shapes, booleans, extrusions, revolutions, sweeps, lofts, shelling, editing operations, and transformations\.
- OpenCascade is compiled to WebAssembly for the geometry kernel and rendered through Three\.js\.
- Documents support transaction\-based undo/redo and import/export of STEP, IGES, BREP, and STL\.
- Runtime plugins can be loaded with a plugin URL parameter, including a macro editor and a Rete\.js visual\-programming editor\.

## Use Cases

- Build and edit parametric parts in the browser without installing desktop CAD software\.
- Use the chat assistant to create or modify models, measure geometry, set materials, manage variables, and export results\.
- Edit imported geometry directly with push/pull and other direct modeling operations\.
- Use the project as a reference for integrating OCCT with WebAssembly or for AI\-assisted CAD architecture\.

## Getting Started

- Use the hosted version by configuring an LLM provider and supplying your own API key in the assistant settings\.
- For local development, clone the repository, run npm install, then run npm run dev; the development server launches on port 8080\.
- Build the application with npm run build\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Running the app requires a modern browser with WebAssembly and WebGL 2 support\.
- Local development uses Node\.js and npm; CI builds with Node 24\.
- Docker deployment is available with docker compose up \-d, serving the app on port 8080\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The AI assistant depends on a user\-supplied LLM provider API key and calls the chosen endpoint directly from the browser\.
- The source recommends evaluating the project against your own workflows if you need production CAD today\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Chroma is an open\-source search infrastructure for AI\. It offers fast, serverless, and scalable infrastructure supporting vector, full\-text, regex, and metadata search, built on object storage and used by millions of developers\.

## Key Features

- Vector search for semantic similarity search\.
- Sparse vector search for lexical search with BM25 and SPLADE\.
- Full\-text search with trigram and regex search\.
- Metadata search with filtering and faceted search\.
- Forking for dataset versioning, A/B testing, and roll\-outs\.
- Command\-line tools for development\.

## Use Cases

- AI applications and agents that need search, retrieval, and context engineering\.
- Knowledge bases and question\-answering workflows\.
- Multi\-tenant search over billions of indexes\.
- Dataset versioning, A/B testing, and roll\-outs using forking\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Python client with pip install chromadb\.
- Install the JavaScript/TypeScript client with npm install chromadb\.
- Start client\-server mode with chroma run \-\-path /chroma\_db\_path\.
- Start free on Chroma Cloud with $5 in free credits, or read the docs\.
- Get up and running in 30 seconds or less\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Run Chroma OSS on your own infrastructure using open\-source deployment guides\.
- Use client\-server mode with chroma run \-\-path /chroma\_db\_path\.
- Chroma Cloud provides a hosted serverless deployment option\.
- Enterprise deployment supports BYOC in your VPC, multi\-cloud/multi\-region replication, and point\-in\-time recovery\.
- Built on object storage with automatic data tiering and caching\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Chroma Cloud became generally available in August 2025\.
- The project is described as rapidly developing and welcomes contributions\.
- Chroma Cloud offers customer\-managed encryption keys to encrypt data with users' own keys\.
- Chroma Cloud supports private networking through AWS PrivateLink\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Chrome DevTools for agents, published as chrome\-devtools\-mcp, is a Model\-Context\-Protocol server and CLI for coding agents\. It lets agents control and inspect a live Chrome browser to automate interactions, debug pages, collect performance insights, and run checks before shipping\.

## Key Features

- Performance insights from Chrome DevTools traces with actionable findings\.
- Advanced browser debugging, including network requests, screenshots, console messages, and source\-mapped stack traces\.
- Reliable automation through Puppeteer with automatic waiting for action results\.
- Live Chrome session connection for inspecting, pausing, and troubleshooting in real time\.
- Proactive QA with Lighthouse audits for accessibility, SEO, and performance\.
- User experience emulation for responsive designs, geolocations, and real user flows\.

## Use Cases

- Testing responsive designs and emulating locations or real user flows in a managed browser\.
- Debugging a live Chrome session by inspecting network activity, console output, and screenshots\.
- Running Lighthouse accessibility, SEO, and performance audits to catch issues before production\.
- Using a coding agent to navigate sites, click controls, and verify page behavior through prompts\.

## Getting Started

- Add the chrome\-devtools MCP server to your MCP client using npx \-y chrome\-devtools\-mcp@latest\.
- For basic browser tasks, use slim mode with the \-\-slim and \-\-headless flags\.
- Run a first prompt to check performance and confirm the browser opens and records a trace\.
- Client\-specific setup guidance is available for editors and agents such as Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Copilot, and OpenCode\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js LTS version\.
- Google Chrome current stable version or newer\.
- npm\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Official browser support is limited to Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing; other Chromium\-based browsers may produce unexpected behavior\.
- Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API for real\-user experience data, and this can be disabled with a flag\.
- Google collects usage statistics to improve reliability and performance, with opt\-out controls available\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Chrome DevTools for agents（发布名为 chrome\-devtools\-mcp）是面向编码代理的 Model\-Context\-Protocol 服务器与 CLI。它让代理控制并检查实时 Chrome 浏览器，以自动执行交互、调试页面、收集性能洞察，并在发布前运行检查。

## 核心功能

- 基于 Chrome DevTools 跟踪记录提供可操作的性能洞察。
- 高级浏览器调试：分析网络请求、截图、查看控制台消息（含源映射堆栈跟踪）。
- 通过 Puppeteer 实现可靠自动化，并自动等待操作结果。
- 可连接实时 Chrome 会话，实时检查、暂停和排查问题。
- 使用 Lighthouse 对无障碍、SEO 和性能进行主动 QA 审计。
- 模拟响应式设计、地理位置和真实用户流程。

## 适用场景

- 在受管浏览器中测试响应式设计，模拟地理位置或真实用户流程。
- 通过检查网络活动、控制台输出和截图调试实时 Chrome 会话。
- 运行 Lighthouse 无障碍、SEO 和性能审计，在生产前发现问题。
- 使用编码代理通过提示导航网站、点击控件并验证页面行为。

## 快速开始

- 在 MCP 客户端中添加 chrome\-devtools MCP 服务器，使用 npx \-y chrome\-devtools\-mcp@latest。
- 对于基础浏览器任务，使用带 \-\-slim 和 \-\-headless 标志的 slim 模式。
- 运行首个提示以检查性能，并确认浏览器打开且记录跟踪。
- 针对 Antigravity、Claude Code、Cursor、VS Code、Codex、Copilot 和 OpenCode 等编辑器或代理，可查看客户端专用设置指南。

## 部署与要求

- Node\.js LTS 版本。
- Google Chrome 当前稳定版或更新版本。
- npm。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：Apache\-2\.0。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

知了 Cicada 是免费开源的跨平台会议与直播助手，可直接读取电脑系统声音，为线上会议、直播、线下会议室和混合会议提供实时字幕、同声传译与 AI 会议纪要。它不向会议中派入机器人，对方无需安装客户端；在 Apple 芯片 Mac 上语音识别在本机完成，录音与会议记录只存本机。

## 核心功能

- 实时字幕：自动识别说话语言并翻译为系统语言，字幕只在有人说话时出现；Apple 芯片 Mac 可在本机完成语音转文字。
- 同声传译：按住右 Option（Windows 为右 Ctrl）说中文，松手后自动翻译，并通过虚拟麦克风把译文说进会议；对方无需安装任何软件。
- AI 会议纪要：边开会边整理要点、结论、待办和鱼骨图，按声音区分说话人，可点击结论或待办跳回原话。
- 会议记录与导入导出：双语记录、纪要和原始录音保存在本机，支持导入录音或视频生成纪要，并导出 Markdown、Word 和 SRT。
- 线下与混合会议：Mac、Windows、Linux 可通过麦克风听会议室，也能同时听线上和现场声音并去重标注。
- 隐私与权限：Mac 上声音、录音和会议记录可留在本机，权限按功能申请；项目代码开源且无统计埋点。

## 适用场景

- 在 Zoom、Microsoft Teams、飞书、腾讯会议、Google Meet 等线上会议中显示双语字幕并生成会议纪要。
- 为 X Spaces、YouTube 直播、Twitch、Discord、B 站直播和播客等电脑播放的声音提供实时字幕与翻译。
- 在会议室或线上线下混合会议中，用麦克风听现场发言并与线上声音合并记录。
- 在需要发言的线上会议或 X Space 连麦中，按住按键说中文，让参会者听到翻译后的语音。

## 快速开始

- 从官网下载页或 GitHub Releases 下载对应平台安装包，可用 checksums\.txt 核对 SHA\-256。
- Mac 下载 DMG 后拖入应用程序文件夹；Windows 双击安装包；Linux 解压后运行 cicada\-linux/install\.sh；Android 安装 APK。
- 按首次引导授予所需权限，并在需要时于设置中的 AI 服务填入 key 或选择兼容服务。

## 部署与要求

- Mac：macOS 14\.4\+，Apple 芯片或 Intel。
- Windows：Windows 10（2004）\+，x64 或 ARM64。
- Linux：Ubuntu 22\.04 或 24\.04 桌面版。
- Android：Android 10\+。
- Windows、Linux、Android 需配置 AI 服务 key；Mac 的 AI 纪要需 key，Intel Mac 的语音识别需 Ling key。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：Apache\-2\.0。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。
- Windows、Linux 和 Android 版的语音识别依赖用户配置的 AI 服务，必须接入 Ling、OpenRouter、ZenMux 或自建兼容服务。
- Mac 上录音和会议记录只存本机，但识别文字会发送到翻译或 AI 服务；将语音识别交给自建服务时，会议声音会发到那台机器。
- Linux 共享屏幕时纪要窗口可能被他人看到。
- 当前安装包尚未完成苹果公证和 Windows 代码签名，首次打开可能被系统拦截，需要手动允许。
- 同声传译需要虚拟麦克风：Mac 安装 BlackHole，Windows 安装 VB\-Cable，Linux 自动创建。

projects.description: Cindy is an open-source AI agent that works out of the box, bringing multiple harnesses, models, and tools into one agent to finish real work in your projects and apps. Ready from day one and yours to shape over time.
projects.descriptionZh: Cindy 是开箱即用的开源 AI Agent，将多种 harness、模型与工具整合为一个智能体，在你的项目和应用中完成实际工作。第一天即可使用，并可随你的需要持续塑造。想到，就能做到。
projects.content:
## Overview

Cindy is an open\-source AI agent and local\-first client for desktop and mobile\. She runs on your own machine with your real files and logged\-in apps, supports multiple harnesses such as Claude Code and Codex, and lets supported models run across supported harnesses\. Harnesses and models can switch mid\-task while workspace, memory, skills, and tools stay continuous\. The repository contains the open\-source client, including desktop and mobile apps and shared packages; the backend service lives in a separate repository\.

## Key Features

- Multiple agent harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, and Pi are supported, with more harnesses on the way and a native Cindy harness in development\.
- Harness and model routing: every supported model runs across every supported harness, and users can switch harnesses or models mid\-task without restarting the work\.
- Multi\-agent orchestration: a task can be planned, executed in parallel by workers, and independently reviewed using different harness and model combinations while Cindy holds context and acceptance criteria\.
- Ready\-to\-work model access: use the managed Cindy service, an existing Coding Plan, your own API key, or local models, with 20\+ tools and sensible defaults\.
- Local workspace and integrations: work with projects, files, apps, terminal, Slack, Feishu, GitHub, Jira, SSH, servers, Android, MCP, skills, and voice\.
- Control and safety: ask\-first behavior at critical moments, isolated workspaces, line\-by\-line review, rollback checkpoints, local workspace retention, and visible work and cost\.

## Use Cases

- Individual developers delegating coding and project tasks on their own computer while reusing existing model subscriptions or API keys\.
- Teams using Slack or Feishu to @ Cindy, run tasks on a member's computer, return results to the thread, and schedule recurring work\.
- Advanced multi\-agent workflows that plan, execute in parallel, and review work across different harness and model combinations\.
- Team and enterprise administration with centralized model access, credit and daily limits, distributed team skills, SSO, and optional self\-hosted Gateway\.

## Getting Started

- Install Node\.js 22\.x, pnpm 10\.x, and Git LFS\.
- Clone the repository, run git lfs pull, and then run pnpm install\.
- Contributor setup, validation, and submission workflow are documented in CONTRIBUTING\.en\.md\.
- For remote development, use pnpm restart:desktop:remote \-\-region=cn for Mainland China Cindy accounts or \-\-region=global for global accounts\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 22\.x, pnpm 10\.x (v11 is not yet supported), and Git LFS are required for the repository\.
- The client is organized as a pnpm monorepo with an Electron desktop app, an Expo/React Native mobile client, and shared packages; the backend service is in a separate repository\.
- Official distribution builds connect to Cindy's official cloud services by default; desktop auto\-updates also come from the official CDN\.
- Linux users have an installation guide for Ubuntu, Arch Linux, and Omarchy covering installation, updates, keyring setup, and migration from a manual install\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Some advertised capabilities are still in development, including the public marketplace and plugin system\.
- Proactive briefs and work suggestions are not yet available and are being developed\.
- Using Skip Sign\-In runs local agents without a Cindy account, but server\-backed capabilities are unavailable in that state\.

projects.content:
## Overview

cinecode is a skill for Claude Code and Cursor that makes films from code\. It supports short films, long YouTube videos, ads, explainers, and music videos; the agent writes the script, builds frames in code, designs sound, and delivers an MP4\.

## Key Features

- An AI coding agent writes the script, builds every frame in code, designs the sound, and hands over a finished MP4\.
- Covers short films, long YouTube videos, ads and product films, social explainers, and music videos\.
- Offers Quick mode with a single self\-contained film\.html using Canvas 2D or three\.js/WebGL, and Film mode for longer multi\-scene productions\.
- Includes named camera moves, typography references, eight look presets, sound design, mastering, and quality checks\.
- Can use open\-licensed archival or stock media and optional external TTS voices; licenses are recorded for downloaded assets\.

## Use Cases

- Making short films and animations from a one\-sentence idea\.
- Producing long YouTube documentaries, explainers, and video essays with researched scripts and narration\.
- Creating ads and product films in 9:16, 1:1, and 16:9 formats\.
- Building vertical social explainers and music videos synchronized to a song's beat grid\.

## Getting Started

- Open Claude Code or Cursor in an empty folder and ask the agent to install the cinecode skill from its GitHub repository, then open a new chat\.
- Tell the agent what film you want; only the idea is required, and it will ask for duration, format, sound, look, and references if omitted\.
- Review and approve the plan, two preview scenes, draft, revisions, and final render; the finished film is delivered as an MP4 in the film folder\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A tool\-running AI coding agent: Claude Code (desktop app, VS Code extension, or terminal) or Cursor\.
- Node\.js 22\+, Python 3\.9\+, ffmpeg, and Google Chrome or Chromium/Edge; the agent can install missing items with approval\.
- A Chrome\-usable GPU and disk space: a few hundred MB for Quick mode and several GB per film during Film mode renders\.
- Optional external speech uses your own Gemini key, ElevenLabs, or free Turkish voice models, which the kit does not install\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- It requires a local tool\-running coding agent; a regular claude\.ai chat cannot run the tools needed to make a film\.
- A full end\-to\-end film on Windows has not yet been tried\.
- On older Claude Code versions, guard hooks may not engage; the film can still work\.
- Free Turkish voice models are optional and not installed by the kit; narration otherwise uses your Gemini key or a temporary system voice\.
- Film mode needs several GB of disk space per film during rendering\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Claude Code is an AI\-powered coding assistant that helps you build features, fix bugs, and automate development tasks\. It understands your entire codebase and can work across multiple files and tools to get things done\. It is available in the terminal, IDE extensions, desktop app, and web\.

## Key Features

- Agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools\.
- Available in terminal, IDE extensions, desktop app, and browser\.
- Executes routine tasks, explains complex code, and handles git workflows through natural language commands\.
- Connects to external data sources and tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP)\.
- Customizable with CLAUDE\.md instructions, skills, hooks, and auto memory\.
- Supports parallel agents and custom agent workflows, including the Agent SDK\.

## Use Cases

- Automate tedious tasks such as writing tests, fixing lint errors, resolving merge conflicts, updating dependencies, and writing release notes\.
- Build features and fix bugs by describing what you want in plain language; Claude Code plans the approach, writes code across multiple files, and verifies it works\.
- Create commits and pull requests, including staging changes, writing commit messages, creating branches, and opening pull requests\.
- Connect external tools through MCP to read design docs in Google Drive, update tickets in Jira, or pull data from Slack\.

## Getting Started

- Install on macOS, Linux, or WSL with the native install script: curl \-fsSL https://claude\.ai/install\.sh \| bash
- Install on Windows PowerShell with: irm https://claude\.ai/install\.ps1 \| iex
- Alternatively install with Homebrew: brew install \-\-cask claude\-code
- Alternatively install with WinGet: winget install Anthropic\.ClaudeCode
- After installation, navigate to your project directory and run claude\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Most surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account\.
- The Terminal CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains also support third\-party providers\.
- The desktop app requires a paid subscription\.
- The JetBrains plugin requires the Claude Code CLI, installed separately\.
- Teleport and the /desktop handoff require a claude\.ai subscription\.

## Before You Adopt

- No recognizable license was detected; verify permission to use, modify, and distribute the project before adoption\.
- Installing via npm is deprecated in favor of recommended installation methods\.
- Most Claude Code surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account, though some CLI and IDE surfaces support third\-party providers\.
- Homebrew installations do not auto\-update, so users must manually upgrade to get the latest features and security fixes\.
- WinGet installations do not auto\-update, so periodic upgrades are required for the latest features and security fixes\.
- The desktop app is in beta on Ubuntu and Debian\.

- 通过自然语言命令执行常规任务、解释复杂代码并处理 git 工作流。
- 通过模型上下文协议（MCP）连接外部数据源和工具。
- 可使用 CLAUDE\.md 指令、技能、钩子和自动记忆进行自定义。
- 支持并行智能体和自定义智能体工作流，包括 Agent SDK。

## 适用场景

- 自动化繁琐任务，例如编写测试、修复 lint 错误、解决合并冲突、更新依赖项和编写发布说明。
- 用自然语言描述需求来构建功能和修复缺陷；Claude Code 会规划方案、跨多个文件编写代码并验证其工作正常。
- 创建提交和拉取请求，包括暂存更改、编写提交信息、创建分支和打开拉取请求。
- 通过 MCP 连接外部工具，以读取 Google Drive 中的设计文档、更新 Jira 中的工单或从 Slack 拉取数据。

## 快速开始

- 在 macOS、Linux 或 WSL 上，使用原生安装脚本安装：curl \-fsSL https://claude\.ai/install\.sh \| bash
- 在 Windows PowerShell 上安装：irm https://claude\.ai/install\.ps1 \| iex
- 或者使用 Homebrew 安装：brew install \-\-cask claude\-code
- 或者使用 WinGet 安装：winget install Anthropic\.ClaudeCode
- 安装后，进入你的项目目录并运行 claude。

## 部署与要求

- 大多数使用界面需要 Claude 订阅或 Anthropic Console 账户。
- 终端 CLI、VS Code 和 JetBrains 还支持第三方提供商。
- 桌面应用需要付费订阅。
- JetBrains 插件需要单独安装 Claude Code CLI。
- Teleport 和 /desktop 交接需要 claude\.ai 订阅。

## 采用前须知

- 未检测到可识别的许可证；采用前请核实项目的使用、修改和分发权限。

projects.content:
## Overview

Claude Code Action is a general\-purpose GitHub action for pull requests and issues\. It can answer questions and implement code changes, activating based on workflow context such as @claude mentions, issue assignments, or explicit automation prompts\. It supports Anthropic direct API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry authentication\.

## Key Features

- Intelligent mode detection selects the appropriate execution mode from workflow context without configuration\.
- Interactive code assistant answers questions about code, architecture, and programming\.
- Code review analyzes pull request changes and suggests improvements\.
- Code implementation supports simple fixes, refactoring, and new features\.
- PR and issue integration works with GitHub comments and pull request reviews\.
- Flexible tool access includes GitHub APIs and file operations, with additional tools configurable\.

## Use Cases

- Automatic pull request code review
- Path\-specific reviews triggered by critical file changes
- Issue triage and labeling
- Security\-focused reviews

## Getting Started

- Open Claude Code in the terminal, run /install\-github\-app, and follow the guided setup for the GitHub app and required secrets\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The action executes entirely on your own GitHub runner; Anthropic API calls go to your chosen provider\.
- Installing the GitHub app and adding secrets requires repository admin access\.
- The quickstart method is only available for direct Anthropic API users; AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry setups are covered separately\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Installing the GitHub app and adding secrets requires repository administrator access\.
- The terminal quickstart path is limited to direct Anthropic API users\.
- Users upgrading from v0\.x should follow the migration guide for workflow updates to v1\.0\.

projects.content:
## Overview

claude\-desktop\-debian is an unofficial repackaging project for running Claude Desktop on Linux\. Since v3\.0\.0 it repackages Anthropic's official Linux \.deb rather than the Windows installer, and builds additional formats Anthropic does not ship: RPM for Fedora/RHEL, distribution\-agnostic AppImages, and a Nix flake for NixOS\. It also adds a launcher and \-\-doctor diagnostics for Linux\-specific environment issues\.

## Key Features

- Repackages Anthropic's official Linux \.deb into RPM and AppImage builds, with a Nix flake for NixOS\.
- MCP support, with configuration stored at ~/\.config/Claude/claude\_desktop\_config\.json\.
- Launcher adds opt\-in native Wayland via CLAUDE\_USE\_WAYLAND=1, GPU\-crash auto\-recovery, XRDP detection, IM\-module override, and autostart\-entry healing\.
- \-doctor diagnostics check the display server, sandbox permissions, MCP config, stale locks, KVM/Cowork stack, and official\-version drift\.
- Cowork on Linux runs when KVM hardware virtualization is available, and the doctor reports readiness\.
- System integration includes a global hotkey (Ctrl\+Alt\+Space) on X11 and Wayland, a system tray, and desktop\-environment integration\.

## Use Cases

- Running Claude Desktop on Fedora or RHEL using the project's RPM package\.
- Running Claude Desktop on distributions without official packages using an AppImage\.
- Installing Claude Desktop on NixOS from the Nix flake\.
- Diagnosing Linux\-specific launch, display, sandbox, MCP, lock, and Cowork issues with \-\-doctor\.

## Getting Started

- On Debian or Ubuntu, add the project's APT repository and install claude\-desktop\-unofficial for automatic updates\.
- On Fedora or RHEL, add the project's DNF repository and install claude\-desktop\-unofficial\.
- On NixOS, install from the GitHub flake, optionally using the claude\-desktop\-fhs variant for MCP server support\.
- Pre\-built \.deb, \.rpm, and \.AppImage files are available on the Releases page\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Linux is required; builds target Debian/Ubuntu via APT, Fedora/RHEL via RPM/DNF, any distribution via AppImage, and NixOS via the Nix flake\.
- Cowork on Linux requires a KVM\-backed VM and depends on KVM, QEMU, OVMF firmware, vhost\-vsock, and virtiofsd\.
- The unofficial package can be installed alongside Anthropic's official package, but the two share ~/\.config/Claude and only one can run at a time\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- This is an unofficial repackaging project, so official support should be sought from Anthropic for the Claude Desktop application\.
- The project no longer publishes to the AUR, and its former claude\-desktop\-appimage package was deleted\.
- Cowork depends on a KVM\-backed VM and related components; the doctor can report which dependencies are installed or missing\.
- Issue reports are sent to Anthropic's API by an automated triage bot, so users should avoid including credentials, tokens, personal data, or other sensitive content\.

projects.descriptionZh: 开源持久记忆引擎，捕获代理会话中的工具使用观察，经 AI 压缩后把相关上下文注入后续会话，支持 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini、OpenCode 等工具。
projects.content:
## Overview

claude\-mem is an open\-source persistent memory compression system for Claude Code and other coding agents\. It captures tool usage observations during sessions, generates semantic summaries, and injects relevant context into future sessions so work can continue across session boundaries and machines\. The local engine stores memory on the user's machine, while optional CMEM Pro adds hosted observation, cloud sync, and private MCP recall\.

## Key Features

- Persistent memory keeps context available across sessions\.
- Progressive recall lets an agent find a relevant note before reading its details\.
- MCP search workflow uses search, timeline, and get\_observations for token\-efficient retrieval\.
- Cloud sync keeps captured project memory available across connected computers\.
- Privacy control supports private tags to exclude sensitive content from storage\.
- TeamBrain provides an optional shared workspace with team work lists, member attribution, and linked findings\.

## Use Cases

- Resume work with prior decisions, discoveries, and fixes available in later sessions\.
- Search project history for past bug fixes and architectural decisions\.
- Recall synced memory from MCP clients, including ChatGPT when the account supports custom connectors\.
- Share a project's history across supported tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT\.

## Getting Started

- Run npx claude\-mem install for the default setup\.
- Target specific environments with IDE flags, such as npx claude\-mem install \-\-ide opencode or npx claude\-mem install \-\-ide grok\-bot\.
- Restart the host tool after installation so previous\-session context can appear in new sessions\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 20\.0\.0 or higher\.
- Claude Code latest version with plugin support for Claude Code integration\.
- Bun JavaScript runtime and process manager, auto\-installed if missing\.
- uv Python package manager for vector search, auto\-installed if missing\.
- SQLite 3 for persistent storage, bundled with the system\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Capture is limited to the tools and integrations installed; MCP recall does not imply automatic capture from every client\.
- Memory is stored locally by the open\-source engine; enabling cloud sync also stores synced data with CMEM, so privacy policy review is advised before connecting\.
- Hosted observation and cloud sync are provided by the paid CMEM Pro service rather than the free open\-source engine\.
- Token\-use effects vary by workload and provider, and CMEM Pro does not alter another subscription's price or limits\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Claude Code Plugins is Anthropic's official marketplace and directory for Claude Code plugins\. A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit; most plugins come from a marketplace, and the directory lists both Anthropic\-maintained internal plugins and third\-party plugins from partners and the community\.

## Key Features

- Packages skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and other components into a single installable plugin\.
- Lists internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic alongside external third\-party plugins from partners and the community\.
- Supports installing from the official marketplace with /plugin install \{plugin\-name\}@claude\-plugins\-official or browsing plugins in /plugin \> Discover\.
- Defines a standard plugin structure with a required \.claude\-plugin/plugin\.json manifest and optional MCP configuration, commands, agents, skills, and README documentation\.
- Supports skill\-bundle marketplace entries for repositories that ship SKILL\.md files without a plugin manifest, using strict false and an explicit skills array\.

## Use Cases

- Install curated plugins from Anthropic's official marketplace to extend Claude Code with skills, agents, hooks, or MCP servers\.
- Browse internal and third\-party plugins in the Discover tab to find a setup someone else built\.
- Submit third\-party plugins for inclusion in the official marketplace through the plugin directory submission form\.
- Package several skills, subagents, hooks, or MCP servers as one unit for teammates or multiple projects\.

## Getting Started

- Run /plugin in a Claude Code terminal session to open the plugin interface\.
- Browse the Discover tab to see plugins from your marketplaces, or install a plugin from the official marketplace with /plugin install \{plugin\-name\}@claude\-plugins\-official\.
- For plugin development without a marketplace, load the plugin directly from its folder with \-\-plugin\-dir\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Plugins may include MCP servers, files, or other software that Anthropic does not control or verify, so users should confirm trust before installing, updating, or using a plugin\.
- Installing a plugin can run code with the user's own privileges, regardless of marketplace tier\.
- An enabled plugin is active across every session, not only sessions where it is used\.

projects.content:
## Overview

CleanYourTV is a free and open\-source approach for removing ads and debloating Android TV and Google TV\. It uses an AI coding assistant over Wi\-Fi to remove unwanted packages and set up an Apple TV\-style home screen, without root and without uninstalling anything\.

## Key Features

- Uses an AI coding assistant to remove ads from Android TV and Google TV over Wi\-Fi\.
- Debloats supported TVs by removing unwanted packages, with an example citing 25 Xiaomi packages removed\.
- Writes a new launcher to provide an Apple TV\-style home screen\.
- Requires no root and uninstalls nothing; one line restores it\.
- Free and open source\.

## Use Cases

- Removing sponsored ads that appear before reaching apps such as Netflix on an Android TV or Google TV\.
- Debloating a smart TV without root and without uninstalling apps\.
- Giving an Android TV an Apple TV\-style home screen experience\.

## Getting Started

- Copy the prompt\.
- On the TV, open Settings, Device Preferences, About and press OK on Build seven times\.
- Go back to Developer options\.
- Turn on USB debugging, and Network or ADB debugging if your TV shows it\.
- Keep the TV on and on the same Wi\-Fi as your computer\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Android TV or Google TV\.
- A computer on the same Wi\-Fi network as the TV\.
- The TV kept on during setup\.
- Developer options enabled, with USB debugging and Network or ADB debugging if shown\.
- An AI coding assistant to run the prompt\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The TV must stay on and remain on the same Wi\-Fi network as the computer during setup\.
- Community launchers, ports, add\-ons, and themes are not reviewed by the repository; review each project's README before sideloading\.

CleanYourTV 是一套免费开源的方案，用于移除 Android TV 和 Google TV 上的广告并进行精简。它通过 Wi\-Fi 借助 AI 编程助手移除不需要的软件包，并搭建 Apple TV 风格的主屏幕，无需 root，也不卸载任何内容。

- 通过 Wi\-Fi 使用 AI 编程助手移除 Android TV 和 Google TV 上的广告。为受支持的电视精简系统，移除不需要的软件包，示例提到移除 25 个小米软件包。编写新的启动器，提供 Apple TV 风格的主屏幕。无需 root，不卸载任何内容；一行命令即可恢复。免费且开源。

## 适用场景

- 移除 Android TV 或 Google TV 上进入 Netflix 等应用前出现的赞助广告。在不 root、不卸载应用的情况下精简智能电视。为 Android TV 提供 Apple TV 风格的主屏幕体验。

- 复制提示词。在电视上打开设置、设备偏好设置、关于，连续按 OK 键七次进入开发者选项。返回开发者选项。开启 USB 调试；如果电视显示网络或 ADB 调试选项，也一并开启。保持电视开机，并与电脑连接到同一 Wi\-Fi。

projects.content:
## Overview

CLI\-Anything is a project that makes software agent\-native\. It generates an agent\-native CLI for any software, codebase, or Web API so AI agents can operate it, with installation through a single command\. It is backed by CLI\-Hub, a registry of generated CLIs that can be browsed, searched, installed, updated, and removed from the command line\.

## Key Features

- Generates an agent\-native CLI for any software, codebase, or Web API so AI agents can operate it\.
- CLI\-Hub registry currently lists 656 CLIs across 279 categories, with browsing via cli\-hub list and keyword lookup via cli\-hub search\.
- One\-command agent skill installation through npx skills add HKUDS/CLI\-Anything \-\-skill cli\-hub\-meta\-skill \-g \-y\.
- A pip\-installed toolkit (pip install cli\-anything\-hub) providing cli\-hub list, search, install, info, update, and uninstall commands\.
- Matrices bundle curated intents mapped to provider CLIs, with 5 matrices and 62 capabilities listed\.
- Real\-world demos show agents driving generated CLIs to produce CAD models, 3D scenes, diagrams, gameplay, captioned video, and live GIS without a GUI\.

## Use Cases

- Prompting an agent to find appropriate CLI software in CLI\-Hub and complete a task through the generated CLI\.
- Bringing any application with a GUI or an API to the hub, including desktop apps, dev tools, cloud services, SaaS APIs, and creative suites\.
- Producing finished artifacts such as 3D CAD models, diagrams, gameplay, captioned video, and live GIS entirely through CLI automation\.

## Getting Started

- Add the agent skill: npx skills add HKUDS/CLI\-Anything \-\-skill cli\-hub\-meta\-skill \-g \-y
- Install the CLI toolkit: pip install cli\-anything\-hub
- Use cli\-hub list to browse the registry, cli\-hub search for keywords, cli\-hub install to install, cli\-hub info to inspect one CLI, cli\-hub update to update an install, and cli\-hub uninstall to remove an install\.
- Then prompt your agent: "Find appropriate CLI software in CLI\-Hub and complete the task: \.\.\."

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Cline is an open\-source AI coding agent that runs as a VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, CLI, desktop app, and SDK\. It helps developers understand codebases, refactor large projects, and automate workflows with human\-in\-the\-loop approval\. It supports Plan and Act modes, runs bash commands, and works with any model provider including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and local models via Ollama\.

## Key Features

- Plan and Act modes: toggle between planning and execution with approval on every step\.
- Edits across your project: coordinated multi\-file changes with linter\-aware fixes, diffs, checkpoints, and one\-click undo\.
- Runs bash commands: executes in your terminal and reacts to output in real time\.
- Rules and Skills: define \.clinerules to teach the agent your coding standards and conventions\.
- Works with every model: Claude, GPT, Gemini, local Ollama, or any OpenAI\-compatible endpoint\.
- Extend with MCP and plugins: register custom tools and lifecycle hooks via the SDK\.

## Use Cases

- Understand your codebase: ask questions about files, dependencies, and behavior\.
- Refactor large codebases: make coordinated changes while keeping imports, types, and behavior consistent\.
- Automate with Cline CLI: use in scripts, cron jobs, and CI pipelines for recurring checks and updates\.
- Multi\-agent teams: coordinate specialist agents for complex tasks\.

## Getting Started

- Install the CLI with \`npm i \-g cline\`, the SDK with \`npm install @cline/sdk\`, or download the desktop app for macOS and Windows\. For VS Code, install from the Marketplace; for JetBrains, install from the JetBrains Marketplace\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Cline runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux\. The desktop app is available for macOS and Windows\. The CLI and SDK require Node\.js\. It can connect to various model providers, including cloud and local endpoints\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Clypra is a free, open\-source video editor for desktop with a native Rust/Tauri v2 core and React 19 frontend\. It provides a multi\-track, frame\-accurate timeline, GPU\-native rendering, hardware\-accelerated playback, and an integrated Web Studio for authoring shaders, transitions, and text effects\. The project emphasizes local file processing, zero PII telemetry, and open standards such as WGSL and OpenTimelineIO\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-track timeline with frame\-accurate trimming, multi\-layer track arrangement, and complete undo/redo history\.
- Hardware\-accelerated engine with sub\-10ms decoding via native Rust, GPU decoding through VideoToolbox, D3D11VA, and VAAPI, and FFmpeg\.
- High\-fidelity audio and waveform rendering with frame\-accurate AV sync and clip volume controls\.
- Text and visual compositing with custom styling, animated overlays, filters, and real\-time canvas previews\.
- Multi\-format import and export including MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, MP3, WAV, PNG, and high\-quality ProRes/H\.264 export\.
- Integrated Web Studio for authoring shaders, transitions, and text effects against WGSL and OpenTimelineIO contracts\.

## Use Cases

- Editing vlogs and tutorial videos with a multi\-track timeline and waveform\-based audio timing\.
- Working with large local 4K ProRes and RAW assets without cloud uploads\.
- Authoring and validating shaders, transitions, and text effects in Web Studio for parity with the native desktop editor\.
- Local video editing on macOS, Windows, or Linux desktop systems\.

## Getting Started

- Download a prebuilt release for macOS, Windows, or Linux\. On macOS, install with Homebrew using brew install AIEraDev/tap/clypra or use the universal DMG\. On Windows, download and run the x64 MSI\. On Linux, download the AppImage, make it executable with chmod \+x, and run it\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Prebuilt desktop binaries target macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows 10/11, and Linux, with release assets listed for macOS, Windows x64 and ARM64, and Linux x64 and ARM64\. Building from source requires Node\.js 18\+, npm, Rust 1\.70\+, and FFmpeg 6\.0\+ with development headers\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- On first launch, macOS Gatekeeper, Windows SmartScreen, or Linux permissions may require explicit user authorization\.
- The README states Clypra includes a lightweight telemetry collector for performance diagnostics, while also stating that media content, project details, file paths, and personal identities are not accessed or sent\.
- Building from source requires FFmpeg 6\.0\+ with development headers as an external dependency\.

projects.content:
## Overview

cmux is a free and open source native macOS terminal built on Ghostty for multitasking, organization, and programmability\. It is designed for developers running coding agents, with vertical tabs, notification rings, split panes, an in\-app browser, and a CLI\.

## Key Features

- Vertical tabs show git branch, working directory, listening ports, and latest notification text\.
- Notification rings and sidebar badges alert when coding agents need attention\.
- Split panes support horizontal and vertical splits within each tab\.
- The in\-app browser can be split alongside the terminal and controlled through a scriptable API\.
- A CLI and Unix socket API enable automation, scripting, and workspace control\.
- The native Swift and AppKit app uses libghostty for GPU\-accelerated rendering\.

## Use Cases

- Running multiple coding agents in parallel and seeing which pane needs attention\.
- Orchestrating subagents or teammates as native panes and splits instead of hidden background processes\.
- Verifying web changes with the in\-app browser while agents work in the terminal\.
- Working with remote machines by opening workspaces over SSH and attaching to remote tmux sessions\.

## Getting Started

- Download the macOS DMG, open it, and drag cmux to the Applications folder; cmux auto\-updates via Sparkle\.
- Alternatively, install with Homebrew by running brew tap manaflow\-ai/cmux and brew install \-\-cask cmux\.
- On first launch, macOS may ask you to confirm opening an app from an identified developer; click Open to proceed\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires macOS to run the native cmux terminal app\.
- Available platform builds are listed in the Download menu; platforms not yet released have a waitlist\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The iOS companion app is in beta\.
- The iOS companion is distributed through TestFlight as cmux BETA\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Codebase Memory (CBM) is an open\-source Model Context Protocol server that gives AI coding agents a persistent local knowledge graph of source code, documentation, and infrastructure\. It supports structural, full\-text, and local semantic search, relationship tracing, source evidence retrieval, index coverage checks, and optional visual exploration through CBM Lens\.

## Key Features

- Provides 17 MCP tools for indexing repositories, searching symbols and text, querying graphs, tracing paths, retrieving code snippets, comparing graphs, and checking index coverage\.
- Builds a connected graph across code, documentation, and infrastructure, including call relationships, documentation references, architecture decisions, container and deployment configuration, and supported CI steps\.
- Uses tree\-sitter parsing and Hybrid LSP type resolution for supported languages, with language and framework coverage varying by the support matrix\.
- Includes native CLI access, persistent indexes, and optional CBM Lens open beta for source navigation, architecture maps, and graph exploration\.
- Adds experimental Smart CI test selection that uses change impact, changed tests, and admitted coverage to explain which tests a change reaches\.
- Runs source analysis and graph storage locally, with native releases requiring no Docker or language runtime and indexing and graph queries requiring no API key\.

## Use Cases

- Give AI coding agents persistent repository context so they can find relevant symbols and source snippets without repeatedly reading whole files\.
- Trace call paths, dependencies, routes, documentation references, and deployment paths across files, services, and indexed repositories\.
- Review changes by mapping diffs to affected symbols, comparing graph snapshots, inspecting related tests, and focusing CI runs with Smart CI\.
- Explore architecture and source evidence visually in CBM Lens while checking index coverage and architecture decisions\.

## Getting Started

- Install the native release and agent integrations on macOS or Linux with the provided install script, restart your coding agent, then ask it to index the project\.
- On Windows, use the PowerShell installation path or another documented installation method\.
- Optionally start CBM Lens with codebase\-memory\-mcp daemon start \-\-open\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Native releases run on macOS, Linux, and Windows without Docker or a language runtime for the native runtime\.
- Indexing and graph queries require no API key\.
- Native packages or npm, PyPI, and Go wrappers are available; package wrappers use their respective runtimes\.
- Source analysis and graph storage run locally, and CBM Lens is served on loopback\.
- Lens browser AI may download an optional model after it is enabled\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Codewhale is an open\-source coding agent and terminal client built on a local Rust agent engine\. It can read a project, edit files, run commands, and check its work, while using hosted provider APIs or local and self\-hosted models\.

## Key Features

- Provider choice across more than 40 built\-in provider routes, OpenAI\-compatible endpoints, and local models through Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang\.
- Plan, Work, and Operate modes with approval postures, workspace recovery through /undo and /restore, and session activity listed by /receipts\.
- Interactive terminal, headless exec, local browser client, and a local HTTP runtime API for threads, events, and approvals\.
- Extensibility through MCP servers, skills, plugins, hooks, and compatibility with existing Claude Code plugins\.
- Multi\-agent workflows with sub\-agents, supervised agent teams, Fleet setup and status, and checked\-in workflows\.
- Computer Use plugin for observing and operating other applications, with access granted by the user\.

## Use Cases

- Build an app, add a feature, or write a script, then run the code and test what it builds\.
- Automate repeated workflows from the terminal, scripts, or CI, including headless turns with codewhale exec\.
- Connect tools through plugins and MCP servers, or use APIs from your own scripts\.
- Split a larger job across agents with different roles and models using Fleet\.

## Getting Started

- Install Codewhale on macOS or Linux with the install script, follow any PATH instruction it prints, then open a project folder\.
- Connect a model with codewhale auth set \-\-provider deepseek, use /provider or F3, and switch models with /model\.
- Run codewhale and describe a concrete task, then choose permissions and review its work\.
- Optionally save a multi\-agent team with /fleet setup and check runs with /fleet status\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows; Android on Termux is a preview\.
- Install routes include the install script, npm, Cargo, Docker, Nix, Homebrew on Linux, and manual downloads\.
- Model access can use provider accounts, an OpenAI\-compatible endpoint, or local and self\-hosted inference through Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang\.
- Connected services require their own setup and authentication\.
- The terminal, local browser, and VS Code GUI need no Codewhale account; hosted web and desktop use an account\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The hosted web app is a development preview, and hosted task execution is still being qualified\.
- The native desktop app is in development and has no public download yet\.
- Connected services require separate setup and authentication\.
- On Linux, bubblewrap sandboxing depends on bubblewrap being installed and working\.

## Overview

Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer\. It provides a lightweight terminal\-based coding agent experience and can also be used through IDE integrations, a desktop app, and the cloud\-based Codex Web\.

## Key Features

- Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
- Runs locally on your computer
- Can be installed via standalone installer, npm, or Homebrew
- Supports signing in with a ChatGPT account or an API key
- Available as an IDE integration, desktop app, and cloud\-based Codex Web

## Use Cases

- Terminal\-based coding assistance
- Local coding agent workflows
- Use with IDE integrations, desktop app, or Codex Web

## Getting Started

- On Mac or Linux, run the install script: curl \-fsSL https://chatgpt\.com/codex/install\.sh \| sh
- On Windows, run the PowerShell install script: powershell \-ExecutionPolicy ByPass \-c "irm https://chatgpt\.com/codex/install\.ps1 \| iex"
- Install with npm: npm install \-g @openai/codex
- Install with Homebrew: brew install \-\-cask codex
- Run codex to get started and select Sign in with ChatGPT

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supported platforms include macOS, Linux, and Windows\.
- macOS binaries are available for Apple Silicon/arm64 and x86\_64; Linux binaries are available for x86\_64 and arm64\.
- Standalone installers download from https://releases\.openai\.com/codex by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable\.
- Using an API key requires additional setup\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Standalone installers have a default download source and fall back to GitHub Releases if metadata or asset downloads are unavailable\.
- Using Codex with a ChatGPT plan depends on signing in with a ChatGPT account and is associated with Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plans\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Codex Security is OpenAI's security tooling for scanning application code, investigating findings, and reviewing fixes\. It reports evidence to support vulnerability investigation and remediation, and can be used through Codex workflows or automated with the CLI and TypeScript SDK\.

## Key Features

- Scans repositories, selected paths, or Git changes, with deep scans repeating standard scans and returning deduplicated findings\.
- Validates candidate findings, generates patches, and verifies existing fixes\.
- Drafts SECURITY\.md policies and saves threat models for later review\.
- Browses saved scans and findings, identifies duplicates, assesses severity against a custom rubric, and suggests owners from source and Git history\.
- Imports third\-party scanner findings and supports export as SARIF, JSON, and CSV, with tracking in Linear, Jira, or GitHub\.
- Automates scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and containers\.

## Use Cases

- Scan a local repository interactively in Codex and work through findings\.
- Run repeatable terminal scans or add security checks to CI\.
- Run scans and handle results inside an application or developer tool with the TypeScript SDK\.
- Scan connected GitHub repositories in Codex cloud or monitor new commits with Codex Security Cloud\.

## Getting Started

- For a first local scan, use the Codex Security plugin in the ChatGPT desktop app or Codex CLI\.
- Install the CLI globally with npm install \-\-global @openai/codex\-security, sign in with cs login, then run cs scan \. from the repository directory\.
- When the scan completes, open the Markdown report at the REPORT path shown in the terminal\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- CLI requires Node\.js 22\.13\.0\+ within 22\.x, or Node\.js 24\.x or 26\.x, and Python 3\.10\+; Python 3\.10 also requires tomli\.
- Scans using OpenAI inference require Codex Security access; CI scans need OPENAI\_API\_KEY or CODEX\_API\_KEY set in the scan process environment\.
- Codex Security Cloud requires workspace access, a GitHub connection, and a compatible Codex cloud environment\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Cognee is an open\-source agent memory platform for LLM agents\. It builds persistent memory across sessions from documents, code, and conversations, turning them into a self\-hosted knowledge graph that agents can search and reuse\. It supports graph, vector, and relational retrieval and can run locally, in Docker, on\-prem, or on Cognee Cloud\.

## Key Features

- Persistent long\-term memory across sessions for AI agents
- Graph, vector, and relational retrieval
- Self\-hosted knowledge graph engine
- First\-party integrations for Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, OpenClaw, and more, plus an MCP server
- Custom ontologies, custom data models, and permissions control
- Local use without an OpenAI or Anthropic API key

## Use Cases

- Build a Company Brain by bringing documentation, conversations, tickets, code, and agent work into shared memory\.
- Give agents memory across runs so they retain project context, past decisions, fixes, and learned rules\.
- Ground agents in your domain by structuring memory around entities and relationships with custom data models and ontologies\.
- Support customer\-facing agents that retrieve cited facts, follow domain rules, and improve from real usage\.

## Getting Started

- Requires Python 3\.10–3\.14\.
- Install with uv pip install "cognee\[gliner\]" or another Python package manager\.
- Optionally configure the LLM by setting LLM\_API\_KEY or creating a \.env file from the template\.
- Run locally without an LLM by saving the quickstart script and running python quickstart\.py, or use cognee\-cli remember and cognee\-cli recall\.
- Explore the bundled demo with cognee\-cli demo\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Python 3\.10–3\.14\.
- Can run self\-hosted, in Docker, on\-prem, or on Cognee Cloud\.
- Cognee can be deployed BYOC in your own cloud\.
- Cognee Cloud is a managed service option\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Default processing uses OpenAI for language models and embeddings, and processing plus generated answers make provider calls\.
- Generated answers and media processing that requires vision or transcription models need additional LLM configuration\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Colibri is an open\-source inference engine for running large language and other models on hardware you already own\. It places model weights across GPU memory, system RAM, and storage, keeping dense parts in memory and streaming routed mixture\-of\-experts weights from disk when the router requests them\. The project includes a dashboard, model catalog, APIs, MCP support, and a CLI\.

## Key Features

- Hierarchical placement of model weights across GPU memory, system RAM, and storage, with routed experts streamed from disk when needed\.
- Mixture\-of\-experts routing activates only a subset of experts per token, allowing very large models to run on machines where the whole model does not fit in fast memory\.
- CPU inference with optional GPU acceleration through CUDA, Vulkan, and Metal across Windows, Linux, and macOS\.
- A dashboard for local chat, expert routing, activity, and structured decisions, with real timing and throughput from the engine\.
- Compatibility with OpenAI\-compatible and Anthropic\-compatible APIs, MCP, and a CLI named coli for agent and tool workflows\.
- Support for 21 catalogue entries and 13 engines, including language, vision, image\-generation, and decision models, plus published GGUF files read as\-is\.

## Use Cases

- Running large open mixture\-of\-experts language models locally on owned hardware, including models that stream experts from disk\.
- Using local models from chat, coding agents, and automation tools through OpenAI\-compatible, Anthropic\-compatible, MCP, or CLI interfaces\.
- Making structured choices with probabilities, such as routing a request, picking an action, or scoring a signal\.
- Researching and measuring inference optimizations through the dashboard and reproducible end\-to\-end benchmarks\.

## Getting Started

- On Windows, download the project ZIP, unzip it, and run START\-HERE\.bat\.
- On Ubuntu or Debian, install git, python3, and build\-essential, clone the Colibri repository, and run \./start\-here\.sh\.
- On macOS with Homebrew, install the Xcode command line tools plus libomp, git, and python, clone the repository, and run \./start\-here\.sh\.
- The setup checks RAM, disk, CPU, and GPUs; recommends a fitting model; builds or downloads the engine; downloads the model with resume; and opens the dashboard\.
- On later runs, START\-HERE\.bat or \./start\-here\.sh starts Colibri without downloading or building again\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- At least 8 GB of RAM; 16 GB or more is better\.
- 22 GB free disk for the smallest model, plus model\-specific download and cache space\.
- An internet connection for setup and model download; a graphics card is optional\.
- Supported platforms include Windows, Linux, and macOS; RAM, disk, and backend needs depend on the chosen model\.
- Setup can use a compiler to build the engine or download a prebuilt engine when no compiler is present\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Model files carry their own licences, separate from the engine\.
- Disk speed is a practical performance factor for large models that stream experts from storage\.
- Some supported models require a conversion or preparation step after download before use\.

projects.content:
## Overview

ComfyUI is an AI creation engine for visual professionals, centered on a modular node\-graph interface for building and reusing image, video, audio, 3D, and text workflows\. It offers local and cloud options, an API, App Mode, and Comfy Agent, which can plan, build, and run workflows from natural\-language descriptions inside ComfyUI\.

## Key Features

- Visual node graph for building and reusing image, video, audio, 3D, and text workflows without code, with visible and adjustable models, parameters, and processing steps\.
- Comfy Agent lets users describe what they want inside ComfyUI; it plans, builds, and runs workflows while editing the canvas alongside the user\.
- Efficient local execution with asynchronous queueing, partial graph re\-execution, smart VRAM and RAM management, model offloading, and quantized model support\.
- Broad native model support spanning image generation and editing, video generation, audio and music, 3D and vision, and text generation\.
- Reusable subgraphs, workflow templates, App Mode, a local API, and JSON workflow save/load with workflow and seed recovery from supported generated media\.
- Runs fully offline for built\-in functionality; the core does not download anything unless requested, and optional API nodes can be disabled\.

## Use Cases

- Creating product scenes and video ads from base compositions, product references, keyframes, and motion references\.
- Generating and editing images with models such as Stable Diffusion, SDXL, SD3\.5, Flux\.1, and Flux\.2\.
- Generating video with models such as Wan, LTX\-Video, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, and Mochi\.
- Running 3D, vision, and media processing tasks such as depth estimation, segmentation, upscaling, frame interpolation, and inpainting or outpainting\.

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop application or try Comfy Cloud for free\.
- Load a workflow from a community template or build one from scratch\.
- Generate and iterate by running and adjusting workflows, then scale when ready\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Available locally on Windows, Linux, and macOS through the desktop application, portable install, or manual install, and available in the cloud via Comfy Cloud\.
- Manual install supports all operating systems and GPU types, including NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, and Ascend\.
- With asynchronous weight streaming, the biggest open\-source models can run on as low as 4GB VRAM plus 8GB RAM relatively quickly\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Commits outside stable release tags may be very unstable and can break many custom nodes\.
