projects.content:
## Overview

Gemini CLI is an open\-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into the terminal, providing lightweight access from your prompt to the model\.

## Key Features

- Free tier with 60 requests per minute and 1,000 requests per day when using a personal Google account\.
- Access to powerful Gemini 3 models with improved reasoning and a 1M token context window\.
- Built\-in tools including Google Search grounding, file operations, shell commands, and web fetching\.
- Extensibility through MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for custom integrations\.
- Terminal\-first design for developers who live in the command line\.
- GitHub integration for pull request reviews, issue triage, on\-demand assistance, and custom workflows\.

## Use Cases

- Query and edit large codebases, generate new apps from PDFs, images, or sketches, and debug issues with natural language\.
- Automate operational tasks such as querying pull requests or handling complex rebases, and run non\-interactively in scripts\.
- Integrate with GitHub workflows for pull request reviews, issue triage, on\-demand assistance, and custom automation\.
- Ground queries with built\-in Google Search for real\-time information and use MCP servers for custom capabilities including media generation\.

## Getting Started

- Run instantly with npx @google/gemini\-cli without installation\.
- Install globally with npm using npm install \-g @google/gemini\-cli, Homebrew using brew install gemini\-cli, or MacPorts using sudo port install gemini\-cli\.
- Start in the current directory with gemini, include multiple directories with gemini \-\-include\-directories \.\./lib,\.\./docs, choose a model with gemini \-m gemini\-2\.5\-flash, and run non\-interactively with gemini \-p\.
- Authenticate by signing in with Google, using a Gemini API key, or using Vertex AI\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Preview releases are published weekly but are not fully vetted and may contain regressions or outstanding issues\.
- Organizations using a paid Code Assist License must set the Google Cloud Project\.

- 查询和编辑大型代码库，使用多模态能力从 PDF、图像或草图生成新应用，并用自然语言调试问题；自动化运维任务，例如查询拉取请求或处理复杂 rebase，并在脚本中以非交互方式运行；集成 GitHub 工作流，用于拉取请求审查、议题分类、按需协助和自定义自动化；使用内置 Google Search 为查询提供实时信息接地，并使用 MCP 服务器获得自定义能力，包括媒体生成。

projects.content:
## Overview

GenOffice is a free, open\-source desktop office suite for macOS, Windows and Linux\. It provides Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDF, HTML and Markdown editors with a built\-in AI agent that can edit documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDFs\. Files open, edit, save and convert locally; AI features use Genspark credits or your own API key\.

## Key Features

- Docs opens and saves real \.docx files with byte\-preserving editing, so only the content you change is rewritten\.
- Sheets uses an in\-house \.xlsx engine with charts, pivot tables, slicers, conditional formatting and formula tracing\.
- Slides creates and edits native \.pptx decks with masters, layouts and smart guides\.
- PDF supports in\-place text and image editing, annotations and forms, plus local conversion to Word, Excel or PowerPoint\.
- HTML and Markdown editors generate and edit self\-contained pages and plain Markdown, with local export to Word\.
- Local file search indexes names, folders and extracted text in an on\-device SQLite full\-text index, with optional TypeSafe Jev reranking\.

## Use Cases

- Drafting and revising Word documents, reports and proposals with AI\-assisted rewrites and tracked changes\.
- Building budgets, summaries and charts in Excel\-compatible spreadsheets with live formulas\.
- Turning a topic into an editable PowerPoint deck, or editing existing decks\.
- Editing PDF text and images, converting PDFs to editable Office formats, and generating HTML or Markdown documents\.

## Getting Started

- Download GenOffice for macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel), Windows (x64 or ARM64) or Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, AppImage, Fedora/RHEL) from genoffice\.ai or GitHub releases\.
- Open, edit, save and convert files locally; sign in with Genspark or add your own provider API key to use AI features\.
- For coding agents, install the genoffice skill from Settings → Integrations, download the skill as a zip, or run npx skills add genspark\-ai/genoffice; then use the genoffice CLI or genoffice mcp server\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 11\+; Windows 10\+ (x64) or Windows 11\+ (ARM64); Linux x86\_64 with glibc 2\.34\+\.
- Desktop app with local opening, editing, saving and PDF\-to\-Office conversion\.
- AI features require Genspark credits or your own API key; supported providers include Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and any OpenAI\-compatible endpoint, local servers included\.
- Scanned\-page OCR is supported on macOS and Windows\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- AI features are not fully bundled; they depend on Genspark credits or a user\-supplied API key, and provider usage charges may apply\.
- Formatting fidelity may vary for complex files, so important documents should be checked before sharing\.
- PDF conversion output should be reviewed for tables and formatting\.
- Online AI features send requests to the chosen provider when used, while core file operations stay local\.
- Official builds collect limited usage statistics by default, with an opt\-out in settings\.

projects.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken using OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view, then returns a camera position, heading and evidence image.
projects.descriptionZh: geo-sleuth 是一个 Agent Skill，可利用 OpenStreetMap 几何、高程天际线、卫星影像和街景查找照片拍摄地点，并返回带误差半径的坐标、相机朝向、证据图和分级置信度；支持 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 和 GitHub Copilot。
projects.content:
## Overview

geo\-sleuth is an Agent Skill for photo geolocation\. It uses OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view, and can solve photos with no text, plates or landmarks\. It returns coordinates with an error radius, camera heading, an evidence image and graded confidence, with every conclusion tied to a command and file produced in the session\.

## Key Features

- One photo and a short request return the camera position, facing direction, satellite evidence image and graded confidence\.
- Uses OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite tiles and street view, so it can work without readable signs, plates or landmarks\.
- Twenty\-odd single\-purpose scripts search, score and rank candidates; the model judges only among the top few\.
- Every conclusion must point to a command that ran in the session and the file it produced\.
- Answers carry coordinates with an error radius, camera heading, evidence image and confidence grade\.
- A standard SKILL\.md plus Python scripts package works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot\.

## Use Cases

- Geolocate a phone photo whose EXIF data has been stripped and whose frame contains no text\.
- Narrow a search with OSM railway or power\-line features and elevation\-based skyline matching\.
- Check candidate locations against satellite imagery and historical street view\.
- Produce an evidence image showing the inferred camera position, field of view and nearby features\.

## Getting Started

- Install with npx skills add Oldcircle/geo\-sleuth, selecting the agents when prompted\.
- Give the installed agent a photo and ask it to find where the photo was taken\.
- On first use, ask the agent to run doctor\.py from the installed skill's scripts folder and address any failed checks\.
- Alternatively, clone the repository and copy the skill folder into the agent's skills directory\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10\+, uv, curl, and an agent that can run shell commands\.
- Keep the complete skill folder, including data and helper modules in scripts\.
- Reverse image search requires Google Chrome or Playwright Chromium; the scripts fall back from Chrome to Chromium\.
- match\.py and sat\_scan\.py use CUDA when supported, then MPS, then CPU, and print the selected device\.
- On Windows, the default uv run install uses a CPU\-only torch; an NVIDIA GPU requires a CUDA build supported by the driver\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Reverse image search depends on an installed Chrome or Chromium browser\.
- Case results reflect one model's decisions, so another model or different decisions may not reproduce them\.
- Published blind re\-runs are regression checks on previously solved photos, not measurements on unseen photos\.
- Some runs can spend substantial time waiting on computation\.

projects.descriptionZh: GEOInflow 是一套面向生成式引擎优化（GEO）的自托管网站与 AI 爬虫分析系统，将网站访客、AI 搜索引荐、服务器抓取日志、内容目录与转化数据放入同一网站上下文，用于观察 AI 爬虫访问、页面抓取覆盖、请求问题以及 AI 搜索带来的访客与转化。项目由猎看科技与北京日报社智源GEO联合发布，采用 MIT 协议。
projects.content:
## Overview

GEOInflow is a self\-hosted system for web and AI crawler analytics focused on Generative Engine Optimization\. It brings website visitors, AI search referrals, server crawl logs, and content inventories into a shared website context so teams can inspect crawler activity, content coverage, access problems, and AI referral outcomes\.

## Key Features

- Built\-in catalog covers AI crawler identities and request purposes from providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, Google, ByteDance, Baidu, Kimi, and Tencent Hunyuan\.
- Crawl activity analytics include requested\-page rankings, repeated requests, directory distribution, leading crawlers, recent activity, and content freshness\.
- Content inventories imported from sitemap, CSV, or JSON can be compared with observed crawl logs to measure coverage and AI blind spots\.
- Website analytics cover pageviews, visitors, events, goals, funnels, visitor paths, attribution, search engines, UTM, heatmaps, retention, and audiences\.
- AI referral sessions can be combined with landing pages, events, goals, and conversions while remaining separate from crawler requests\.
- Operational features include ingestion checks, historical data repair, analytics acceleration, and source and rule versioning\.

## Use Cases

- Company websites, content sites, media publishers, developer documentation teams, and GEO teams managing multiple sites can use GEOInflow\.
- Teams can identify which AI crawlers visit a site, which pages they request, and which important pages have no observed crawl activity\.
- Operators can investigate blocked or failing requests using HTTP status, caching, latency, errors, and risk signals\.
- Analysts can observe how AI search contributes visitors and conversions alongside standard website analytics\.

## Getting Started

- Start Docker Engine or Docker Desktop and Docker Compose V2, then run sh scripts/liekan\-deploy\.sh from the project root\.
- The default address after deployment is http://127\.0\.0\.1:3002\.
- For a fresh installation, the initial username is admin and the initial password is liekan; change the password after signing in\.
- To try the bundled example, run docker compose \-f docker\-compose\.liekan\.yml exec app node scripts/liekan\-seed\-demo\.mjs\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker Engine or Docker Desktop and Docker Compose V2 are required\.
- Image and dependency download sources must be reachable\.
- Production access requires a domain, HTTPS, and a trusted reverse proxy\.
- Automatic server collection requires public HTTPS, an ingestion secret, and signed installation assets\.
- Cloudflare integration also requires OAuth, permissions, and the relevant provider capabilities\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- GEO Weight is marked beta and uses a fixed 30\-day calculation policy with documented evidence and limitations\.
- AI analysis is optional and disabled by default; enabling it requires choosing model connections and website materials\.
- Automatic server collection and Cloudflare integration require additional external configuration and permissions\.
- Some GEO\-related outcomes require additional data beyond the system's observations\.

projects.description: GhidraMCP is a Model Context Protocol server that exposes Ghidra tools to MCP clients, enabling LLMs to autonomously decompile and analyze binaries, rename methods and data, and list methods, classes, imports, and exports.
projects.descriptionZh: GhidraMCP 是面向 Ghidra 的模型上下文协议服务器，把核心 Ghidra 能力以工具形式暴露给 MCP 客户端，让 LLM 可自动反编译和分析二进制、重命名方法与数据，并列出方法、类、导入和导出。
projects.content:
## Overview

GhidraMCP is a Model Context Protocol server and Ghidra plugin that lets LLMs autonomously reverse engineer applications\. It exposes numerous tools from core Ghidra functionality to MCP clients\.

## Key Features

- Decompile and analyze binaries in Ghidra\.
- Automatically rename methods and data\.
- List methods, classes, imports, and exports\.
- Expose core Ghidra functionality as MCP tools\.
- Support optional headless analysis without the Ghidra GUI\.

## Use Cases

- Ask an LLM to decompile a function and explain it in plain language\.
- Map functions, imports, strings, and cross\-references in a binary\.
- Analyze malware samples, old firmware, or your own builds\.
- Automatically rename methods and data during reverse engineering\.

## Getting Started

- Install Ghidra 12\.1\.4 and uv, or use Python 3\.10\+ with the package installed\.
- Download the latest release, import the extension zip into Ghidra through File \> Install Extensions, restart Ghidra, and enable GhidraMCPPlugin\.
- Configure an MCP client to launch ghidra\-mcp and point it at the Ghidra server, which defaults to localhost:8080\.
- For clients that connect to a URL, run the MCP server with streamable HTTP transport and add its MCP endpoint as a remote server\.
- For headless analysis, run ghidra\-mcp with headless and binary options, using Python 3\.10–3\.13 and GHIDRA\_INSTALL\_DIR set to the Ghidra 12\.1\.4 directory\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Ghidra 12\.1\.4 is required\.
- uv is recommended; Python 3\.10\+ can be used with a pip installation\.
- Headless mode requires Python 3\.10–3\.13, the GhidraMCP extension installed or available as a jar, and GHIDRA\_INSTALL\_DIR set to the Ghidra 12\.1\.4 directory\.
- The MCP server and Ghidra HTTP server default to localhost:8080 and can be configured\.
- On macOS, headless use requires building Ghidra's decompiler once\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The documented setup explicitly requires Ghidra 12\.1\.4\.
- Headless mode narrows the Python requirement to versions 3\.10 through 3\.13\.
- Headless use on macOS requires an additional decompiler build step\.
- When server host and port are not set, they default to localhost:8080\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

GhidraMCP 是一个 MCP 服务器与 Ghidra 插件，旨在让 LLM 自主进行应用逆向工程。它把 Ghidra 核心功能中的大量工具暴露给 MCP 客户端。

## 核心功能

- 可在 Ghidra 中反编译和分析二进制。可自动重命名方法和数据。可列出方法、类、导入和导出。可将核心 Ghidra 功能作为 MCP 工具暴露。支持在无 Ghidra 图形界面的情况下进行可选的 Headless 分析。

projects.content:
## Overview

GitLab MCP Server connects MCP\-compatible AI clients to GitLab through the Model Context Protocol\. It provides tools for projects, merge requests, issues, pipelines, wikis, releases, tags, milestones, and related GitLab workflows, starting with 40 default tools and expanding through discover\_tools to 288 total tools\.

## Key Features

- Broad GitLab coverage across projects, repository browsing, merge requests, issues, pipelines, wiki, releases, tags, labels, and milestones\.
- Flexible authentication options include Personal Access Token, local OAuth2 browser flow, MCP OAuth proxy, and per\-request remote authorization\.
- Supports stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP transports for local, legacy, and remote deployments\.
- Starts with a lean default toolset of 40 tools; discover\_tools can activate additional toolsets for the session, with 288 tools total\.
- JMESPath result filtering and compact results help reduce oversized tool replies\.
- Self\-hosted ready with custom GitLab instances, proxy settings, and dynamic API URL routing\.

## Use Cases

- Review merge requests by listing changed files and fetching batched file diffs from an MCP\-compatible AI client\.
- Inspect pipelines and retrieve paginated job logs without hunting through the GitLab UI\.
- Manage GitLab issues, projects, wikis, releases, tags, labels, and milestones through AI client workflows\.
- Run a hosted or self\-hosted MCP endpoint for team or remote AI clients using Streamable HTTP\.

## Getting Started

- Install the zereight\-mcp\-gitlab binary with npm or Homebrew, or use the npx one\-liner\.
- Configure an MCP client with a GitLab Personal Access Token or OAuth2 settings\.
- Use the skill plus CLI path for workflows without MCP registration\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 20 or later is required\.
- A GitLab API URL and Personal Access Token or OAuth configuration must be supplied for the server to access GitLab\.
- Remote Claude\.ai connections require public HTTPS and GITLAB\_MCP\_OAUTH on the server\.
- Shared HTTP deployments can expose a Streamable HTTP endpoint for remote clients\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The api toolset bypasses group/project allowlists, other tool filters, and per\-tool safety checks, and prompt injection can drive it\.
- The @next npm build is a pre\-release and is not intended for production use\.

projects.content:
## Overview

God's Eye View is a browser\-based spy\-satellite simulator that pulls public sensor data into a single picture\. It combines satellite imagery, flights, ships, weather, and public cameras on a 3D globe, and lets users click objects to track them\. The project also includes voice queries, a rendered cockpit view, recent Sentinel\-2 imagery retrieval, transit tracking, SDR/RF visualization, world radio, an MCP server, and Director Mode annotation tools\.

## Key Features

- Interactive 3D globe for tracking satellites, planes, ships, and public cameras\.
- Voice queries that annotate the globe with natural\-language answers\.
- Toggle satellite layers including GPS and Starlink\.
- Weather layers such as clouds, rain radar, lightning density, and cyclone tracks with forecast cones, plus time scrubbing for cloud imagery\.
- Recent Sentinel\-2 imagery retrieval by drawing a bounding box, draped on 3D terrain\.
- MCP server access so agents can query the same picture and add findings to a shared canvas\.

## Use Cases

- Explore public data across flights, ships, satellites, weather, and cameras on one map\.
- Visualize a flight in cockpit view or follow a bus in transit with a trailing path\.
- Use voice or MCP\-enabled agents to ask questions and annotate a shared 3D globe\.
- Retrieve recent Sentinel\-2 imagery for an area such as a fire\.

## Getting Started

- Get it on GitHub, join the hosted version waitlist, or use the one\-click Pinokio install\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Traffic and camera\-pose layers are estimates rather than exact observations\.
- Not all layers are keyless; the site notes that 18 of 20 layers need no key\.
- RF and SDR visualization depends on connecting your own SDR\.

projects.content:
## Overview

goose is a general\-purpose, open source AI agent that runs on your machine\. It is available as a native desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows, a CLI for terminal workflows, and an API for embedding\. Built in Rust, it supports code, research, writing, automation, data analysis, and other tasks\.

## Key Features

- Native desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows, plus a CLI and an API\.
- Connect to 70\+ extensions such as databases, APIs, browsers, GitHub, and Google Drive via the Model Context Protocol open standard\.
- Works with 15\+ model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, and Bedrock, using API keys or existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP\.
- Recipes capture workflows as portable YAML configs for sharing with teams and running in CI\.
- Subagents can handle tasks in parallel, including code review, research, and file processing\.
- Security features include prompt injection detection, tool permission controls, sandbox mode, and an adversary reviewer that watches for unsafe actions\.

## Use Cases

- Code\-related tasks such as installing, executing, editing, and testing with supported LLMs\.
- Research, writing, automation, and data analysis\.
- Sharing portable workflows with a team or running them in CI using recipes\.
- Using extensions to connect goose to databases, APIs, browsers, GitHub, Google Drive, and more\.

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop app for macOS, Linux, or Windows\.
- Install the CLI using the provided shell script\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- goose depends on external model providers; the source lists 15\+ providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, and Bedrock\.
- goose can use community\-built MCP extensions, an external extension ecosystem users can browse and add to\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Graphic Walker is an open\-source alternative to Tableau designed as a lightweight, embeddable React component rather than a heavy BI platform\. It lets users explore datasets by dragging fields onto axes and building visualizations, with computation handled by web workers so it can run as a pure front\-end app\. The visual analytics interface is based on a grammar of graphics foundation, and it also provides a general query interface for routing data queries to your own computation service\.

## Key Features

- Drag\-and\-drop interface for exploratory data analysis and visualization building\.
- Data Explainer that explains why some patterns occur or what may cause them\.
- Web workers handle computation, allowing use as a pure front\-end app\.
- General query interface for submitting data queries to your own computation service\.
- Natural language/chat interface for asking questions about data\.
- Spatial visualization with GeoJSON and TopoJSON support\.

## Use Cases

- Embedding exploratory charting inside an existing React application\.
- Adding data exploration to internal tools or product features without adopting a full BI platform\.
- Letting users explore CSV or JSON datasets and build charts in the browser\.
- Routing data queries through an existing computation service when backend computation is available\.

## Getting Started

- Open the online playground, create a dataset by dropping in a CSV or JSON file or choosing a sample, review the preview, and click Use This Dataset\. Then open Visualization and drag fields onto axes\. To embed it, install @kanaries/graphic\-walker and import the GraphicWalker

## Deployment & Requirements

- Graphic Walker can run as a pure front\-end app with client\-side computation handled by web workers\. For server\-side computation, provide the computation function and also provide fields\. It is published on npm as @kanaries/graphic\-walker for embedding in React apps\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The uiTheme customization API is labeled beta and may change\.
- The visualization specification prop is internal and should not be provided directly\.
- TerseSpec is intended for authoring; persistence and export/import continue using the canonical format\.

projects.taglineZh: 编码助手查询知识图谱，而非逐文件搜索；可托管或本地开源运行
projects.description: Graphify turns codebases, docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph that AI coding assistants query over MCP instead of grepping, with local deterministic AST parsing and no vector store.
projects.descriptionZh: Graphify 将代码库及其文档、SQL 模式、配置和 PDF 转换为可查询的知识图谱，AI 编码助手可通过 MCP 查询，而不是逐个文件搜索。代码解析在本地以确定性的 AST 方式完成，不使用向量存储。
projects.content:
## Overview

Graphify builds a persistent, typed knowledge graph from code and related materials so AI coding assistants can query source\-linked context instead of searching files\. It works across repositories and can run as a hosted product or through the open\-source engine on your own machine\.

## Key Features

- Builds a queryable knowledge graph from code, docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs\.
- Parses code locally with tree\-sitter grammars, without uploading code or sending telemetry in the open\-source tool\.
- Serves graph context to assistants over MCP, including Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, and others\.
- Traverses a persistent cross\-repo graph so answers can include file:line citations and evidence paths\.
- Supports incremental updates by re\-parsing changed files and can rebuild on commits with a git hook\.
- Includes PR review triage and formal verification features, with coverage depending on workflow and language\.

## Use Cases

- Give coding assistants source\-linked context for architecture questions and code navigation across repositories\.
- Assess change impact and merge risk before merging, including CI, review, and conflict signals\.
- Recover and share repository knowledge across teams without relearning the codebase by hand\.
- Support audited or regulated work with graph paths and provenance for answers\.

## Getting Started

- Install the open\-source CLI with uv tool install graphifyy\.
- For Graphify Cloud, connect an MCP client to the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint and complete OAuth sign\-in\.
- A Graphify Cloud setup requires a Graphify account, workspace access, and an indexed repository\.
- Running graphify install registers the /graphify skill with the assistants it detects\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Choose between the hosted Graphify Cloud service or the open\-source engine on your own machine\.
- The open\-source engine can be served over stdio or HTTP on infrastructure you own\.
- Enterprise can run the whole system on your own infrastructure, including air\-gapped deployment\.
- For fully offline use, point the semantic pass at a local model such as Ollama or any OpenAI\-compatible server like vLLM\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The open\-source tool is designed not to send code anywhere; the hosted product is an optional alternative\.
- Local parsing keeps code on the machine, but the non\-code semantic pass may leave the machine if pointed at a hosted model\.
- The hosted product keeps the graph in the cloud on connected repositories, so using Cloud involves a hosted service and connected repositories\.
- The enterprise layer is described as early access, so teams should account for that maturity status\.
- Formal verification coverage is not universal and depends on the workflow and language\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Graphify 从代码及相关材料构建持久、带类型的知识图谱，让 AI 编码助手查询带来源链接的上下文，而不是搜索文件。图谱可跨仓库使用，既可部署为托管产品，也可通过开源引擎在自有机器上运行。

## 核心功能

- 从代码、文档、SQL 模式、配置和 PDF 构建可查询的知识图谱。开源工具使用 tree\-sitter 语法在本地解析代码，不上传代码，也不发送遥测。通过 MCP 向 Claude Code、Cursor、Copilot、Codex、Gemini CLI 等助手提供图谱上下文。遍历持久化跨仓库图谱，使答案可包含 file:line 引用和证据路径。通过仅重新解析变更文件实现增量更新，并可用 git hook 在提交时重建。包含 PR 评审分流和形式化验证功能，覆盖范围取决于工作流和语言。

## 适用场景

- 为编码助手提供带来源链接的上下文，用于跨仓库的架构问答和代码导航。在合并前评估变更影响和合并风险，包括 CI、评审和冲突信号。帮助团队恢复并共享仓库知识，无需手工重新学习代码库。以图谱路径和来源信息支持审计或受监管工作。

## 快速开始

- 使用 uv tool install graphifyy 安装开源 CLI。使用 Graphify Cloud 时，将 MCP 客户端连接到 Streamable HTTP MCP 端点并完成 OAuth 登录。Graphify Cloud 设置需要 Graphify 账户、工作区访问权限和已索引的仓库。运行 graphify install 会向检测到的助手注册 /graphify 技能。

## 部署与要求

projects.description: Graphiti is an open-source framework for building and querying temporal knowledge graphs for AI agents. It tracks how facts change over time, maintains provenance to source data, and supports hybrid retrieval for evolving real-world data.
projects.descriptionZh: Graphiti 是一个开源框架，用于构建和查询面向 AI 代理的时序知识图谱。它跟踪事实随时间的变化，维护对源数据的溯源，并支持针对不断演变的现实数据的混合检索。
projects.content:
## Overview

Graphiti is a framework for building and querying temporal context graphs for AI agents\. Unlike static knowledge graphs, it tracks how facts change over time, maintains provenance to source data, and supports both prescribed and learned ontology\. It continuously integrates user interactions, structured and unstructured enterprise data, and external information into a coherent, queryable graph\.

## Key Features

- Temporal Fact Management: Facts have validity windows; old facts are invalidated not deleted\. Episodes & Provenance: Every entity and relationship traces back to raw episodes\. Prescribed & Learned Ontology: Define entity and edge types via Pydantic models or let structure

## Use Cases

- Build temporal knowledge graphs that evolve with every interaction\. Represent rich, structured context instead of flat document chunks\. Query across time, meaning, and relationships with hybrid retrieval\.

## Getting Started

- Install with pip install graphiti\-core\. Requires Python 3\.10\+, a graph database (Neo4j, FalkorDB, Amazon Neptune, or Kuzu), and an OpenAI API key\. See the Quickstart example for connecting, initializing indices, adding episodes, and searching\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10 or higher; Neo4j 5\.26 / FalkorDB 1\.1\.2 / Amazon Neptune Database Cluster or Neptune Analytics Graph \+ Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection / Kuzu 0\.11\.2 (deprecated); OpenAI API key (defaults to OpenAI for LLM inference and embedding)\. Optional: Google Gemini,

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Graphiti works best with LLM services that support structured output; other services may cause incorrect schemas and ingestion failures\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Graphiti 是一个用于构建和查询面向 AI 代理的时序上下文图的框架。与静态知识图谱不同，它跟踪事实随时间的变化，维护对源数据的溯源，并支持预设和习得的本体。它持续将用户交互、结构化和非结构化企业数据以及外部信息整合到一个连贯、可查询的图中。

## 核心功能

- 时序事实管理：事实具有有效性窗口；旧事实被失效而非删除。
- 事件与溯源：每个实体和关系都追溯到原始事件。
- 预设与习得本体：通过 Pydantic 模型定义实体和边类型，或让结构从数据中涌现。

## 适用场景

- 构建随每次交互演化的时序知识图谱。
- 表示丰富的结构化上下文，而非扁平文档块。
- 通过混合检索跨时间、语义和关系进行查询。

## 快速开始

- 使用 pip install graphiti\-core 安装。需要 Python 3\.10\+、图数据库（Neo4j、FalkorDB、Amazon Neptune 或 Kuzu）以及 OpenAI API 密钥。参见快速入门示例以了解连接、初始化索引、添加事件和搜索。

## 部署与要求

- Python 3\.10 或更高版本；Neo4j 5\.26 / FalkorDB 1\.1\.2 / Amazon Neptune Database Cluster 或 Neptune Analytics Graph \+ Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection / Kuzu 0\.11\.2（已弃用）；OpenAI API 密钥（Graphiti 默认使用 OpenAI 进行 LLM 推理和嵌入）。可选：Google Gemini、Anthropic 或 Groq API 密钥（用于替代 LLM 提供商）。

projects.content:
## Overview

GraphRAG is a structured, hierarchical approach to Retrieval Augmented Generation\. It extracts a knowledge graph from raw text, builds a community hierarchy, generates summaries for these communities, and leverages these structures for RAG\-based tasks\.

## Key Features

- Extracts entities, relationships, and key claims from TextUnits\.
- Builds a hierarchical community structure using the Leiden technique\.
- Generates bottom\-up summaries of each community and its constituents\.
- Supports Global, Local, DRIFT, and Basic query modes\.
- Provides prompt tuning guidance for fine\-tuning prompts to your data\.
- Offers CLI and Indexer/Query packages for working with the system\.

## Use Cases

- Reasoning over private datasets such as enterprise proprietary research, business documents, or communications\.
- Answering holistic questions over large data collections or singular large documents\.
- Connecting disparate pieces of information through shared attributes to synthesize new insights\.
- Question answering about specific entities by fanning out to their neighbors and associated concepts\.

## Getting Started

- Check out the Get Started guide\.
- Try the command line quickstart\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- GraphRAG is described as a research project that is largely in maintenance mode and will not accept new PRs or implement new features\.
- The provided code is a demonstration and is not an officially supported Microsoft offering\.
- Indexing can be expensive, so users should read the documentation to understand costs and start small\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Grok Build is SpaceXAI's terminal\-based AI coding agent\. It runs as a full\-screen TUI that understands your codebase, edits files, executes shell commands, searches the web, and manages long\-running tasks\. It supports interactive use, headless operation for scripting and CI, and embedding in editors via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP)\. The project is written in Rust and synced periodically from the SpaceXAI monorepo\.

## Key Features

- Full\-screen TUI with mouse interaction; Extensible via plugins, skills, and MCP servers; Understands codebase and edits files; Executes shell commands and searches the web; Manages long\-running tasks; Supports headless mode for scripting/CI and ACP for editor embedding\.

## Use Cases

- Interactive coding assistance in the terminal; Headless automation for scripting and CI pipelines; Embedded in editors via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP)\.

## Getting Started

- Install the released binary via curl \-fsSL https://x\.ai/cli/install\.sh \| bash (macOS/Linux/Git Bash) or irm https://x\.ai/cli/install\.ps1 \| iex (Windows PowerShell), then run grok \-\-version\. Alternatively, build from source with Rust and DotSlash; see the repository for details\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Prebuilt binaries are available for macOS, Linux, and Windows\. Building from source requires Rust, DotSlash, and protoc\. macOS and Linux are supported build hosts; Windows builds are best\-effort and not currently tested\. First launch opens the browser for authentication\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- External contributions are not accepted\.

projects.content:
## Overview

HA\-MCP is a standalone Model Context Protocol server for Home Assistant\. It is designed for configuring, building, and debugging a smart home, not only controlling it, and works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, and 15\+ AI clients\. It provides 87 tools across search, control, management, monitoring, system, and safety categories\.

## Key Features

- 87 tools across search, control, management, monitoring, system, and safety categories\.
- Natural\-language device control, service calls, bulk operations, and real\-time state tracking\.
- Management of automations, scripts, helpers, dashboards, areas, zones, groups, calendars, and blueprints\.
- Monitoring through history, statistics, camera snapshots, automation traces, and ZHA devices\.
- System capabilities including backup and restore, updates, apps, device registry, and HACS management\.
- Safety features such as Read Only Mode, per\-tool enable/disable, tool security policies, and automatic edit backups\.

## Use Cases

- Create an automation that turns on the porch light at sunset\.
- Add a weather card to a Lovelace dashboard\.
- Debug a motion sensor automation by analyzing execution traces and suggesting fixes\.
- Create a reusable movie\-mode script that dims lights, closes blinds, and turns on the TV\.

## Getting Started

- Install the HA\-MCP integration through HACS, or through Settings → Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026\.11 or newer\.
- Restart Home Assistant\.
- Choose an administrator account: use a long\-lived access token, or create a dedicated administrator account with local access only\.
- Add the HA\-MCP Server integration and choose remote access through Home Assistant and/or local network access\.
- Copy the connect URL from the Configure screen and paste it into your AI client\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The HA\-MCP integration requires Home Assistant 2026\.8\.0 or newer\.
- The in\-process server works on Home Assistant OS, Supervised, Container, and Core with full feature parity\.
- The app (add\-on) is available on Home Assistant OS and Supervised installs\.
- Docker, PyPI/uvx, and local stdio run the server outside Home Assistant and are useful for Container or Core installs or a separate host\.
- Setup requires an administrator access token or a dedicated administrator account\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Run only one ha\-mcp installation method; the in\-process server replaces the app, Docker, and uvx/PyPI methods\.
- Configure exactly one install method per client to avoid connection hangs\.
- The stdio transport has known connection problems that streamable HTTP does not\.
- OIDC authentication makes all authenticated users share the server's Home Assistant credentials\.
- The File & YAML services entry is optional and only needed when opt\-in file and YAML editing tools are enabled\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Hallmark is an anti\-AI\-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex\. It selects a macrostructure and theme for a brief, applies a rule set, and runs slop\-test gates before returning UI; it also supports auditing, redesigning, and studying existing designs\.

## Key Features

- Default build mode picks a macrostructure first, dresses it in a theme, and refuses to repeat the last three macrostructures\.
- Twenty\-one themes and twenty\-one macrostructures provide structural variety across briefs\.
- Fifty\-seven slop\-test gates plus a pre\-emit self\-critique run before output is returned\.
- Audit scores existing code against anti\-patterns and returns a punch list without edits\.
- Redesign keeps copy, information architecture, and brand while rebuilding with a different structural fingerprint\.
- Study extracts design DNA from a screenshot or URL, refuses pixel clones, and can optionally emit a portable design\.md for handoff\.

## Use Cases

- Building landing pages, product pages, and other web UI from a brief with an AI coding agent\.
- Auditing existing UI code for common AI\-generated design anti\-patterns without making edits\.
- Redesigning a page while preserving its copy, information architecture, and brand\.
- Extracting structural design DNA from a screenshot or URL for handoff to another AI tool\.

## Getting Started

- Run npx skills add nutlope/hallmark, then ask your agent for a UI\. Re\-run the command to update, or copy SKILL\.md and references into the tool\-specific directory for Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex as the agent environment\. Installation uses the npx skills command, or manual copying of skill files into the agent's skills or rules directory\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Hallmark is built for specific AI coding environments, so adoption depends on using Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex\.
- The documented install path uses the npx skills command\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Handy is a free, open source, and extensible speech\-to\-text desktop application that works completely offline\. Press a configurable keyboard shortcut, speak, and release; Handy processes the speech locally and pastes the transcribed text into the text field you are using\.

## Key Features

- Press a configurable keyboard shortcut, speak, and release to paste transcribed text into any text field\.
- Processes speech entirely on your computer, so audio does not need to be sent to the cloud\.
- Supports push\-to\-talk, toggle, hold\-only, and toggle\-only recording modes with configurable keybindings\.
- Uses Silero VAD for silence filtering and offers Whisper models with GPU acceleration when available\.
- Includes Parakeet V3, a CPU\-optimized model with automatic language detection\.
- Runs as a cross\-platform desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux; the project is free, open source, and extensible\.

## Use Cases

- Dictating text directly into any application or text field using a keyboard shortcut\.
- Transcribing speech locally when privacy requires keeping audio on the computer\.
- Writing longer text or replying to messages without switching to a separate transcription service\.

## Getting Started

- Download the latest release from the Handy releases page or the website\.
- On macOS, Handy is also available via Homebrew cask using brew install \-\-cask handy; on Windows, via winget using winget install cjpais\.Handy\.
- On Debian or Ubuntu, install the downloaded \.deb with APT, for example sudo apt install \./Handy\_\*\.deb\.
- Install the application, launch Handy, and grant necessary system permissions such as microphone and accessibility\.
- Configure preferred keyboard shortcuts in Settings, then start transcribing\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux as a desktop application\.
- Requires microphone and accessibility permissions after launch\.
- On Linux with X11, install xdotool for reliable text input; on Wayland, install wtype or dotool\.
- Linux installations depend on the gtk\-layer\-shell runtime library; package names vary by distribution\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- On Linux, reliable text input depends on display\-server\-specific tools; without them Handy falls back to enigo, which may have limited compatibility\.
- The Homebrew cask and winget packages are external packages not maintained by the Handy developers\.
- Using a Bluetooth headset microphone on macOS can temporarily reduce playback quality or volume while recording\.
- Shortcuts that include the fn or Globe key work only on Apple keyboards and never trigger on third\-party keyboards\.
- Wayland support on Linux is limited\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Happy is an open\-source remote control for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex that run on your own computers\. It lets you start, steer, approve, and review agent sessions from iOS, Android, or the web, then continue the same session in your terminal\. Session data is end\-to\-end encrypted: your code, agent, and encryption keys stay on your devices, and only encrypted session data passes through the Happy backend\. The project is built by a small team and publishes the app, CLI, and server as open source\.

## Key Features

- Mobile access to Claude Code and Codex sessions from iOS, Android, or the web
- Push notifications when an agent needs permission or encounters errors
- Instant switching between phone, desktop, and terminal with a single keypress
- End\-to\-end encryption, with keys held on your own devices and only ciphertext relayed
- Open source app, CLI, and server with no telemetry or tracking
- Realtime voice support alongside the mobile and web clients

## Use Cases

- Checking on a long\-running agent task while away from your desk
- Answering an agent's permission request or question from your phone
- Reviewing diffs and live session output remotely before continuing work
- Starting at your desk and continuing the same session from another device

## Getting Started

- Download the iOS or Android app\.
- Install the CLI on your computer with: npm install \-g happy
- Start your agent through the wrapper: happy claude or happy codex
- Optionally download the native macOS desktop app from its releases page\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A computer on which your code and coding agent keep running
- Node\.js/npm to install the happy CLI globally via npm install \-g happy
- A paired iOS or Android device, or a web browser, for remote control
- Claude Code or Codex installed to be launched through the happy wrapper

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Session data is end\-to\-end encrypted: the backend stores and relays only opaque ciphertext and never receives the decryption key\.
- The CLI was migrated from the earlier happy\-coder npm package\.
- The project states that it is open source with no telemetry or tracking\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Harbor is a framework from the creators of Terminal\-Bench for specifying sandboxed agent tasks for evaluation and optimization\. It can evaluate arbitrary agents such as Claude Code, OpenHands, and Codex CLI, build and share benchmarks and environments, run experiments in parallel across thousands of environments, and generate rollouts for RL optimization\.

## Key Features

- Evaluate arbitrary agents like Claude Code, OpenHands, Codex CLI, and more\.
- Build and share your own benchmarks and environments\.
- Conduct experiments in thousands of environments in parallel through providers like Daytona, Modal, LangSmith, Blaxel, Novita Sandbox, Tensorlake, and Runta\.
- Generate rollouts for RL optimization\.
- Serves as the official harness for Terminal\-Bench\-2\.0\.

## Use Cases

- Running benchmarks such as Terminal\-Bench\-2\.0 locally with Docker or on cloud providers\.
- Evaluating arbitrary agents and language models on supported datasets\.
- Exploring third\-party benchmarks like SWE\-Bench and Aider Polyglot\.
- Generating rollouts for RL optimization\.

## Getting Started

- Install Harbor with uv tool install harbor or pip install harbor\.
- Run a benchmark such as: harbor run \-\-dataset terminal\-bench@2\.0 \-\-agent claude\-code \-\-model anthropic/claude\-opus\-4\-1 \-\-n\-concurrent 4\.
- Set ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY before running the Anthropic example\.
- Use harbor run \-\-help to see supported agents and options\.
- Use harbor datasets list to explore supported third\-party benchmarks\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Local benchmark runs use Docker\.
- Cloud runs can use providers such as Daytona via the \-\-env flag\.
- Set ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY for Anthropic models and DAYTONA\_API\_KEY for Daytona cloud runs\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Local benchmark runs require Docker\.
- Cloud\-parallel experiments depend on third\-party providers such as Daytona, Modal, LangSmith, Blaxel, Novita Sandbox, Tensorlake, and Runta\.
- The Anthropic example requires an ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY environment variable\.
- Cloud runs on Daytona require a DAYTONA\_API\_KEY environment variable\.

projects.name: HarnessRouter
projects.tagline: The unified interface for agent harnesses.
projects.taglineZh: 智能体运行框架的统一接口
projects.description: Open-source infrastructure that runs harnesses like Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes as pluggable agent backends, letting products run tasks, retrieve results, and switch harnesses through one API.
projects.descriptionZh: 开源基础设施，将 Codex、Claude Code、Hermes 等运行框架作为可插拔的智能体后端运行，让产品通过一个 API 执行任务、获取结果并切换运行框架。
projects.content:
## Overview

HarnessRouter is the execution and runtime layer between a product and supported agent harnesses\. An LLM returns tokens, while a harness gives it a sandbox, tools, and a loop so it returns actual work; HarnessRouter turns existing harnesses such as Codex and Claude Code into plug\-and\-play agent backends\. Applications send a task and receive progress, files, artifacts, final state, and trace through one interface, implemented as the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) with an OpenAI Responses\-compatible API\. It is available as a self\-hosted Apache 2\.0 Community Edition and as managed HarnessRouter Cloud\.

## Key Features

- One API contract across every supported agent harness, so a product keeps a single integration as harnesses are added
- Implements the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP), an open standard, and exposes an OpenAI Responses\-compatible API
- Handles the agent execution lifecycle: sessions, tools, files, artifacts, streaming progress, cancellation, errors, resume, and traces
- Community Edition is Apache 2\.0 and runs on infrastructure you control with your own keys, state, and files
- Cloud provisions and operates one isolated sandbox per task, scaling workloads without infrastructure work
- Harness × model routing lets teams benchmark combinations by quality, latency, and cost before changing production traffic

## Use Cases

- Build a new agent product on top of Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, or another supported harness
- Migrate an existing managed agent backend to HarnessRouter
- Run a task across harnesses and compare time, cost, and accuracy in the Harness Arena
- Start from open\-source starter kits such as Slides, Sheets, Dashboards, and Videos

## Getting Started

- Run the container: docker run \-d \-\-name harnessrouter \-p 127\.0\.0\.1:3000:3000 \-v harnessrouter:/data harnessrouter/harnessrouter
- Wait for the first launch by following docker logs until the logs show "\[harnessrouter\] ready on :3000"
- Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with username harnessrouter and password harnessrouter
- Connect a model provider under Bring Your Own Key and add its API key so its supported models become available
- Open Agent harnesses, choose a harness, select New task, pick a model, and follow live progress and produced files

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker with about 4 GB of disk and a provider API key; no HarnessRouter account or bundled trial key is required for Community Edition
- Do not add \-\-user: the entrypoint and Runner need root to manage per\-session users, while the Console and Gateway run unprivileged and agent processes run as their session's user
- Keep the loopback binding while using the initial credentials
- Use a named volume such as harnessrouter:/data to preserve the database, files, installed harness CLIs, and workspaces between restarts

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Migrating an existing agent workflow requires adopting the API or UHP contract, mapping existing behavior to it, and verifying product\-specific behavior on your side\.
- Harness capabilities differ, so combinations should be benchmarked before production traffic is switched\.
- Model access depends on the third\-party provider and the credentials you choose to supply\.
- Long exact values such as tokens should be attached as files or passed through the harness environment rather than written into the prompt\.

## 项目简介

HarnessRouter 是产品与受支持智能体运行框架之间的执行和运行时层。LLM 只返回 token，而运行框架为它提供沙箱、工具和循环，使其真正完成工作；HarnessRouter 将 Codex、Claude Code 等现有运行框架变成即插即用的智能体后端。应用通过一个接口发送任务，并接收进度、文件、产物、最终状态和追踪信息，该接口以统一运行框架协议（UHP）实现，并提供兼容 OpenAI Responses 的 API。它既有自托管的 Apache 2\.0 社区版，也有托管的 HarnessRouter Cloud。

## 核心功能

- 所有受支持智能体运行框架共用一套 API 契约，因此产品在新增运行框架时仍只需维护一个集成。实现统一运行框架协议（UHP）这一开放标准，并暴露兼容 OpenAI Responses 的 API。处理智能体执行生命周期：会话、工具、文件、产物、流式进度、取消、错误、恢复和追踪。社区版采用 Apache 2\.0，运行在你自己控制的基础设施上，使用你自己的密钥、状态和文件。Cloud 为每个任务预置并运行一个隔离沙箱，无需基础设施运维即可扩展工作负载。运行框架 × 模型路由让团队在切换生产流量前按质量、延迟和成本对组合进行基准测试。

## 适用场景

- 在 Codex、Claude Code、Hermes 或其他受支持运行框架之上构建新的智能体产品。将现有托管智能体后端迁移到 HarnessRouter。在 Harness Arena 中跨运行框架运行同一任务，比较时间、成本和准确性。从 Slides、Sheets、Dashboards、Videos 等开源入门套件开始。

## 快速开始

- 运行容器：docker run \-d \-\-name harnessrouter \-p 127\.0\.0\.1:3000:3000 \-v harnessrouter:/data harnessrouter/harnessrouter。通过跟踪 docker logs 等待首次启动，直到日志显示 \[harnessrouter\] ready on :3000。打开 http://localhost:3000，使用用户名 harnessrouter 和密码 harnessrouter 登录。在 Bring Your Own Key 下连接模型提供商并添加其 API

## 部署与要求

- 需要 Docker、约 4 GB 磁盘和提供商 API 密钥；社区版不需要 HarnessRouter 账户或捆绑试用密钥。不要添加 \-\-user：入口点和 Runner 需要 root 来管理每会话用户，而 Console 和 Gateway 以非特权运行，智能体进程以其会话用户身份运行。使用初始凭据时保持回环绑定。使用 harnessrouter:/data 这样的命名卷，在重启之间保留数据库、文件、已安装的运行框架 CLI 和工作区。

## 采用前须知

projects.description: Headroom is a context optimization layer for LLM applications. It compresses tool outputs, database results, file reads, logs, RAG results, and API responses before they reach the model, reducing tokens while keeping the same answers.
projects.descriptionZh: Headroom 是面向 LLM 应用的上下文优化层，可在工具输出、数据库结果、文件读取、日志、RAG 检索结果和 API 响应到达模型前进行压缩，在保持回答质量的同时减少 token；可作为库、代理或 MCP 服务器使用，压缩在本地运行并支持可逆恢复。
projects.content:
## Overview

Headroom is a context optimization layer for LLM applications\. It compresses tool outputs, database results, file reads, RAG retrievals, API responses, logs, and conversation history before they reach the model, so the model sees less noise\. Compression runs locally, and compressed content is reversible through a local CCR store\.

## Key Features

- Reversible compression (CCR) stores originals locally and gives the model a headroom\_retrieve tool for full details\.
- Smart content detection routes JSON, source code, logs, text, diffs, and HTML to the best compressor with zero configuration\.
- SmartCrusher preserves errors, anomalies, and first and last boundaries in JSON tool outputs through statistical analysis\.
- Works as a transparent proxy, Python or TypeScript library, agent wrapper, or MCP server\.
- Cache optimization stabilizes prefixes to help provider KV caches hit and tracks frozen messages to preserve cache read discounts\.
- Persistent memory uses hierarchical user, session, agent, and turn scopes with SQLite and HNSW backends\.

## Use Cases

- Reduce tokens from tool outputs, logs, database reads, RAG results, file reads, and API responses before sending them to an LLM\.
- Preserve critical errors during SRE incident debugging while compressing large, mostly routine tool output\.
- Compress context during codebase exploration and GitHub issue triage\.
- Share compressed context between agents across frameworks with SharedContext\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Python package with uv tool install \-\-python 3\.13 "headroom\-ai\[all\]" or pip install "headroom\-ai\[all\]"; install the TypeScript SDK with npm install headroom\-ai\.
- Choose a mode: headroom deploy for turnkey local deployment, headroom wrap claude to wrap a coding agent, headroom proxy \-\-port 8787 for a drop\-in proxy, or use the inline Python library\.
- Run headroom doctor to confirm routing works, then headroom perf or headroom dashboard to view savings\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Compression runs locally on your machine; no prompt or file content is sent anywhere to be compressed\.
- The headroom CLI ships only in the PyPI package; the npm headroom\-ai package is the TypeScript SDK and provides no headroom command\.
- Docker\-native installation is documented as an install option\.
- A local proxy can be run on port 8787\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Compression savings depend on how repetitive the input is, so benchmark figures should be treated as workload\-specific\.
- Source code compression is optional and off by default\.
- Prose and already\-dense outputs may compress very little\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Helicone is an AI Gateway and LLM observability platform for AI engineers\. It routes, debugs, and analyzes AI applications, offering one\-line integration to log requests from providers and frameworks\. It supports monitoring, evaluation, experimentation, prompt management, and self\-hosting\.

## Key Features

- AI Gateway: access 100\+ AI models with one API key through the OpenAI API, with intelligent routing and automatic fallbacks\.
- Quick integration: one line of code logs requests from OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, Gemini, Vercel AI SDK, and more\.
- Observability: inspect and debug traces and sessions for agents, chatbots, document processing pipelines, and more\.
- Analytics: track cost, latency, quality, and more, and export to PostHog in one line for custom dashboards\.
- Prompt management: version prompts using production data and deploy prompts through the AI Gateway without code changes\.
- Playground and fine\-tuning: rapidly test and iterate on prompts, sessions, and traces, and fine\-tune with OpenPipe or Autonomi\.

## Use Cases

- Debugging and monitoring agents, chatbots, and document processing pipelines\.
- Tracking cost, latency, and quality across AI applications\.
- Testing and iterating on prompts, sessions, and traces in a playground\.
- Versioning and deploying prompts using production data\.

## Getting Started

- Get an API key by signing up and add credits\.
- Update the baseURL in your code to the Helicone AI Gateway and add your API key\.
- Use a supported model such as gpt\-4o\-mini, claude\-sonnet\-4, or gemini\-2\.0\-flash, or any model from the Helicone models list\.
- View your logs in the Helicone dashboard and access 100\+ models through one API\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Helicone can be used through its hosted service or self\-hosted\.
- For self\-hosting, use the Docker Compose setup; clone the repository, enter the docker directory, copy \.env\.example to \.env, and start services with the compose script\.
- For Enterprise workloads, a production\-ready Helm chart is available by contacting enterprise@helicone\.ai\.
- Manual deployment is not recommended; Docker or Helm should be used\.
- Helicone comprises Web, Worker, Jawn, Supabase, ClickHouse, and Minio services\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Manual deployment is discouraged; Docker or Helm are the recommended self\-hosting paths\.
- The listed integrations may be outdated, so users should check current documentation for provider or framework support\.
- The production\-ready Helm chart for Enterprise workloads requires contacting Helicone for access\.
- Helicone states SOC 2 and GDPR compliance for enterprise readiness\.

projects.tagline: The runtime your coding agents live on.
projects.taglineZh: 编码 agent 所依托的运行时
projects.description: Herdr is a runtime for coding agents that keeps terminals running in a background server, so multiple agents across projects can continue when you disconnect and be reached again from any machine.
projects.descriptionZh: Herdr 是编码 agent 的运行时：终端在后台服务器中持续运行，断开连接也不中断工作，并可跨本地与 SSH 机器重新接入多个项目的 agent。
projects.content:
## Overview

Herdr is a runtime for coding agents\. It runs terminals inside a background server, keeps multiple agents and projects organized, and lets you detach without stopping work\. It supports local and SSH\-connected machines and marks agents as working, blocked, or idle so waiting agents are visible\.

## Key Features

- Detach without stopping work: terminals continue in a background server when the client closes or an SSH connection drops\.
- Several machines, one window: local work and saved SSH machines appear together with a combined agent list and independent reconnects\.
- Agent status tracking: panes are marked working, blocked, or idle, and Herdr flags an agent that stops and needs an answer\.
- Agent\-native control: agents can drive Herdr through the CLI and socket API to split panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is blocked\.
- Works with existing agent CLIs: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, Grok, and others run in Herdr\-owned terminals rather than being wrapped or replaced\.
- Keyboard and mouse first\-class: tmux\-style prefix keys plus click, drag, and split interactions; plugins extend panes and workflows\.

## Use Cases

- Running several coding agents across projects without keeping a terminal client open\.
- Returning to the same agent workspaces from another machine and reattaching to running terminals\.
- Monitoring a group of agents to find one that is blocked and needs input\.
- Automating agent\-to\-agent workflows through the CLI and socket API\.

## Getting Started

- Install with the curl install script, Homebrew via brew install herdr, mise via mise use \-g herdr, the Windows PowerShell install script, or published binaries\.
- Start Herdr with the herdr command where the work lives, run agents and split panes, then use ctrl\+b q to detach and herdr to reattach\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supported operating systems are macOS, Linux, and Windows\.
- Herdr runs as a single Rust binary and does not use Electron; it runs in the terminal you already use\.
- A background Herdr server owns the terminals, allowing clients to detach and reconnect\.
- Windows has an endpoint\-protected install option, and installation is also available through Homebrew, mise, install scripts, and released binaries\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- After a server or machine restart, Herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported agent sessions, but the original processes do not survive\.
- Connecting additional machines currently relies on SSH\.

projects.tagline: Training-free language model modification
projects.taglineZh: 无需训练的语言模型修改工具
projects.description: Heretic is a training-free language model modification tool. It uses mathematical techniques and configurable scorers to steer model behavior, including removing censorship, suppressing refusals, reducing slop or sycophancy, and more.
projects.descriptionZh: Heretic 是一款无需训练即可修改语言模型的工具。它基于对比示例提示与匹配评分器，用数学方法引导模型行为，可移除审查、抑制拒答，并减少废话或迎合倾向。
projects.content:
## Overview

Heretic is a tool for training\-free language model modification\. It lets users modify language models they can run on their hardware without expensive training, using mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting example prompts and matching scorers\. Refusal suppression is the default action\.

## Key Features

- Training\-free modification of language models that can run on local hardware, with support for most dense models, many multimodal models, several MoE architectures, and many modern hybrid models\.
- Default censorship removal and refusal suppression, with configuration options to reduce slop, reduce humor, reduce sycophancy, or alter emotional alignment\.
- Configurable scorer plugins, including refusal rate and KL divergence by default, with support for custom scorers and co\-optimization of multiple scores\.
- Two built\-in modifiers: Arbitrary\-Rank Ablation (default) and directional ablation, also known as abliteration\.
- Optional on\-the\-fly 4\-bit quantization using bitsandbytes to reduce VRAM requirements at a slight accuracy cost\.
- Reproducible model manifests and the Heretic Grimoire for cataloguing and reproducing published models\.

## Use Cases

- Removing censorship or suppressing refusals in a language model as the default processing action\.
- Reducing slop, humor, or sycophancy, or altering emotional alignment, by selecting different configuration files\.
- Writing custom scorer plugins to control and co\-optimize multiple behavioral objectives\.
- Saving, uploading to Hugging Face, chatting with, or benchmarking a processed model after a run\.

## Getting Started

- Prepare a Python 3\.10\+ environment with PyTorch 2\.6\+ installed as appropriate for your hardware\.
- Run pip install \-U heretic\-llm\.
- Run heretic Qwen/Qwen3\-4B\-Instruct\-2507, replacing the model identifier with the model you want to process\.
- By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression); choose another configuration file or write your own to do something else\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10\+ environment with PyTorch 2\.6\+ installed as appropriate for your hardware\.
- A language model that can run on your hardware\.
- Optional 4\-bit quantization with bitsandbytes can reduce VRAM requirements at a slight accuracy cost\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Optional 4\-bit quantization with bitsandbytes can lower VRAM requirements but may introduce a slight accuracy cost\.
- Byte\-for\-byte reproduction of a processed model depends on an environment perfectly identical to the original, including hardware, drivers, operating system, and all package versions\.

## 项目简介

Heretic 是一款无需训练即可修改语言模型的工具。用户可以在自己的硬件上运行并修改模型，无需昂贵训练；它通过对比示例提示与匹配评分器，用一系列数学方法引导模型行为。默认操作是抑制拒答、移除审查。

## 核心功能

- 可在本地硬件上运行的语言模型进行无需训练的修改，支持大多数稠密模型、许多多模态模型、若干 MoE 架构以及许多现代混合模型；默认移除审查、抑制拒答，并可通过配置减少废话、减少幽默、减少迎合倾向或改变情绪对齐；可配置评分器插件，默认包含拒答率和 KL 散度，并支持自定义评分器及多评分协同优化；内置两种修改器：任意秩消融（默认）与方向消融，也称 abliteration；可使用 bitsandbytes 进行可选的即时 4 位量化，以降低显存需求，但会带来轻微精度损失；提供可复现模型清单，以及用于编目和复现已发布模型的 Heretic Grimoire。

## 适用场景

- 默认对语言模型执行移除审查或抑制拒答；通过选择不同配置文件减少废话、幽默或迎合倾向，或改变情绪对齐；编写自定义评分器插件，以控制和协同优化多个行为目标；在一次运行后保存模型、上传至 Hugging Face、与模型对话或对其进行基准测试。

## 快速开始

- 准备 Python 3\.10\+ 环境，并根据硬件安装 PyTorch 2\.6\+；运行 pip install \-U heretic\-llm；运行 heretic Qwen/Qwen3\-4B\-Instruct\-2507，并将模型标识替换为要处理的模型；默认执行移除审查（抑制拒答），如要做其他修改，可选择其他配置文件或自行编写。

projects.content:
## Overview

Hermes Agent is a self\-improving AI agent built by Nous Research\. It features a built\-in learning loop that creates skills from experience, improves them during use, and builds a deepening model of the user across sessions\. It runs on various infrastructures and integrates with multiple messaging platforms\.

## Key Features

- Real terminal interface with full TUI, multiline editing, slash\-command autocomplete, and streaming tool output\.
- Lives where you do: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI from a single gateway process\.
- Closed learning loop: agent\-curated memory, autonomous skill creation, self\-improving skills, FTS5 session search, and Honcho dialectic user modeling\.
- Scheduled automations with built\-in cron scheduler and delivery to any platform\.
- Delegates and parallelizes: spawn isolated subagents for parallel workstreams and write Python scripts that call tools via RPC\.
- Runs anywhere: seven terminal backends including local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox\.

## Use Cases

- Scheduled tasks like daily reports, nightly backups, and weekly audits in natural language\.
- Research: batch trajectory generation and trajectory compression for training tool\-calling models\.
- Personal assistant accessible from messaging platforms while running on a cloud VM\.

## Getting Started

- Install with curl \-fsSL https://hermes\-agent\.nousresearch\.com/install\.sh \| bash on Linux/macOS/WSL2, or use the PowerShell one\-liner for Windows\. Then run 'hermes' to start chatting\. Use 'hermes model' to choose your LLM provider and 'hermes setup' for full configuration\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs on a $5 VPS, GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure\. Supports terminal backends: local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox\. Native Windows and WSL2 supported\. Android/Termux via APT repository\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Windows Defender or antivirus may flag uv\.exe as malware; this is a false positive\.

## 核心功能

- 真正的终端界面：完整 TUI，支持多行编辑、斜杠命令自动补全、对话历史、中断与重定向以及流式工具输出。随处可用：通过单一网关进程支持 Telegram、Discord、Slack、WhatsApp、Signal 和 CLI，包括语音备忘录转录和跨平台对话连续性。闭环学习：智能体策展记忆并定期提醒，复杂任务后自主创建技能，技能在使用中自我改进，FTS5 会话搜索配合 LLM 摘要实现跨会话回忆，Honcho 辩证用户建模，兼容 agentskills\.io 开放标准。定时自动化：内置 cron

## 适用场景

projects.content:
## Overview

Hex is a local\-first voice dictation application built in Rust\. It lets users hold a shortcut, speak, and paste transcribed text into the foreground app\. The macOS app is available now, with Windows and Linux betas\. Ordinary dictation uses on\-device speech recognition; optional OpenCode\-backed features can rewrite or process transcripts when an OpenCode service is already running\.

## Key Features

- On\-device speech transcription using downloadable local models; ordinary dictation does not require OpenCode or a cloud transcription service\.
- Configurable shortcut, microphone, language, local model, recording behavior, feedback volume, launch\-at\-login behavior, and Dock visibility\.
- Modes provide corrections, application\-specific behavior, and optional text processing or rewriting\.
- Annotate records screen drawing and speech, then offers paste or send\-to\-OpenCode actions on macOS and Linux, not Windows\.
- CLI queries expose dictation history and meeting transcripts, while custom TypeScript or JavaScript transformations run in an embedded engine\.
- The TypeScript SDK lets other applications use Hex for local transcription when supplied a compatible Hex executable\.

## Use Cases

- Dictating text into any focused application with a hold\-to\-talk shortcut\.
- Fixing names and preferred spellings before paste with Modes corrections\.
- Capturing annotated screen recordings with voice explanation for review or sending to an agent\.
- Reading recent dictation history or meeting transcripts from the terminal on supported builds\.

## Getting Started

- macOS: install with Homebrew using brew install \-\-cask anomalyco/tap/hex, or download the signed DMG, drag Hex\.app into Applications, launch it, and complete microphone, Accessibility, and transcription model setup\.
- Windows: download the x64 or ARM64 installer and run it; it installs for the current user without administrator rights\.
- Linux: use the Linux install script, Debian or Fedora packages, or a binary, then follow the Linux guide for shortcuts and compositor setup\.
- Optional OpenCode features require an OpenCode service that is already running and a configured model provider\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS requires Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later\.
- Windows beta runs on Windows 10 or 11 on x64 or ARM64; x64 needs a 2013 or newer processor with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or later)\.
- Linux beta targets x86\_64 Linux on i3/X11 and compatible wlroots Wayland compositors; x86\_64 needs a 2013 or newer processor with AVX2\.
- Native Wayland requires compositor support for clipboard and layer\-shell protocols; paste uses wtype with the virtual keyboard protocol or the desktop's RemoteDesktop portal\.
- Network access is required for model installation and software updates; local model setup also needs huggingface\.co and its model download CDN\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Windows support is a beta and runs on Windows 10 and 11 for x64 and ARM64\.
- Linux support is a beta with processor and compositor requirements\.
- History retention stores pasted dictation text and limited metadata for seven days by default, but does not store audio, full browser URLs, or window titles\.
- Model installation and software updates require network access\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Hindsight is an agent memory system designed for AI agents that need long\-term memory across sessions\. It extracts conversations into typed facts, consolidates them into observations, and supports recall and reflective reasoning over memory banks\.

## Key Features

- Typed memory extraction turns conversations into world facts, experience facts, observations, mental models, and knowledge pages rather than storing raw transcripts\.
- Multi\-strategy recall runs semantic, keyword BM25, graph, and temporal searches in parallel, fuses results by rank, reranks with a cross\-encoder, and cuts to a token budget\.
- Observation consolidation deduplicates overlapping facts, grounds observations in evidence, keeps a history of refinements, and treats affected observations as stale when new memories are not yet consolidated\.
- Reflect runs an agentic loop over the bank, gathers its own evidence, checks mental models and knowledge pages before raw facts, and cites retrieved sources\.
- Memory banks are isolated per user or agent and can be configured with mission, directives, and disposition to shape reflect behavior\.
- Integrations include Python, TypeScript, Go, CLI, MCP, personal agents, and 20\+ coding\-agent harnesses\.

## Use Cases

- Coding agents can use one install to wire 20\+ harnesses to a per\-repo memory bank\.
- Personal agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw can use Hindsight as their memory provider\.
- AI agents can use Hindsight to recall context across sessions, reason over time expressions, and consolidate beliefs from many facts\.
- Teams can run Hindsight Cloud or self\-host it for production memory needs\.

## Getting Started

- Install and get running in 60 seconds via the Quick Start\.
- Start a server using Docker Compose, Helm, or pip, then connect a client\.
- Use Python, TypeScript, Go, CLI, MCP, or plain HTTP clients\.
- Use the Python embedded option when no server is required\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Hindsight Cloud is a fully managed option\.
- Embedded deployment has zero setup and runs locally\.
- Self\-hosted deployment supports Docker Compose, Helm/Kubernetes, and bare\-metal pip\.
- Memory banks use Postgres with pgvector, and users can bring their own cluster connection string\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Homelable is a self\-hosted infrastructure visualization and documentation solution for homelabs\. It scans local networks and Zigbee/Z\-Wave devices, builds device documents from scan results, and adds live healthchecks so the diagram reflects what is actually running\. A markdown Library stores runbooks, incidents, and network notes alongside the visual map\.

## Key Features

- Network scanning with nmap populates a Pending Devices queue that can be approved, hidden, or ignored\.
- Automatically generated per\-device documents plus a markdown Library for runbooks, incidents, and network overview pages\.
- Live node healthchecks using ping, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP, SSH, Prometheus, and /health methods\.
- Imports from Proxmox VE, Zigbee2MQTT, and Z\-Wave JS UI via MQTT or REST API sources\.
- Rack canvases with U\-height, faceplates, port\-to\-port patching, floor plans, and per\-device design customization\.
- Read\-only Live View and Documentation View, a documented REST API, and an optional MCP server for AI clients\.

## Use Cases

- Keep homelab documentation synchronized with the devices and services actually present on the network\.
- Map network topology and see online/offline status directly on an interactive canvas\.
- Import existing Proxmox VE virtualization inventory or Zigbee/Z\-Wave device topology instead of re\-entering devices manually\.
- Share a read\-only canvas or documentation space on the LAN, or connect scripts and AI assistants through the REST API and MCP server\.

## Getting Started

- Download the latest release or use the pre\-built GHCR Docker images\.
- Follow the installation documentation for Docker, Proxmox LXC, bare\-metal systemd/nginx, or build\-from\-source setup\.
- Run a network scan, then approve discovered devices to add them to the canvas\.
- Optionally import from Proxmox VE, Zigbee2MQTT, or Z\-Wave JS UI, configure healthchecks, and add Library pages\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker deployment uses pre\-built GHCR images; Proxmox LXC and bare\-metal Debian/Ubuntu installs with systemd and nginx are also documented\.
- Zigbee2MQTT and Z\-Wave JS UI imports require a reachable MQTT broker, such as Mosquitto\.
- Proxmox VE import requires a reachable Proxmox host and an API token with the read\-only PVEAuditor role\.
- The gethomepage widget requires backend port 8000 to be reachable from the gethomepage container\.
- Network scans may require root or NET\_RAW capabilities for certain nmap scan types\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is described as young and still evolving, so users should expect rough edges\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Homer is a static homepage for a server, designed to keep self\-hosted services and links in one place\. It is a full static HTML/JS dashboard configured by a simple YAML file, with no database or backend, and it is intended to be served over HTTP\.

## Key Features

- Static HTML/JS dashboard with no database or backend to maintain\.
- Configured through a single YAML file at assets/config\.yml\.
- Lightweight and fast with low or no maintenance\.
- Installable as a PWA\.
- Supports smart cards, fuzzy search, multi\-page layouts, item grouping, and theme customization\.
- Keyboard shortcuts include / for search, Escape to stop, Enter to open the first match, and Alt/Option\+Enter to open in a new tab\.

## Use Cases

- Provide a single homepage for self\-hosted services, home lab links, and internal tools\.
- Organize larger collections of services into multiple pages and groups\.
- Install as a PWA for quick access from a home screen or app launcher\.

## Getting Started

- Use Docker with image b4bz/homer:latest, bind\-mount a config directory to /www/assets, expose port 8080, and restart unless stopped\.
- With Docker Compose, set the image, container name, volume mapping, port, user, INIT\_ASSETS environment variable, and restart policy\.
- Alternatively download and extract the latest release homer\.zip, rename assets/config\.yml\.dist to assets/config\.yml, and serve it behind a web server\.
- For a manual build, run pnpm install and pnpm build; the dashboard is ready in /dist\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Homer must be served by an HTTP server; opening index\.html directly over file:// will not work\.
- The Docker container runs as UID/GID 1000 by default; adjust with \-\-user if assets directory permissions require it\.
- INIT\_ASSETS defaults to 1 and installs example config and assets, so the config directory must be writable by the container user\.
- Environment variables include INIT\_ASSETS, SUBFOLDER, PORT, and IPV6\_DISABLE\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Homer is static by design, so it does not provide live status indicators or dynamic data\.
- Homer must be served over HTTP; opening index\.html directly with file:// will not work\.
- The Docker container uses UID/GID 1000 by default, so directory permissions may need adjustment\.
- INIT\_ASSETS defaults to 1 and requires the config directory to be writable by the container user\.
