projects.content:
## Overview

mcp\-ssh\-manager is a standard stdio MCP server for SSH\. It lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex, or any MCP client run commands, move files, query databases, create backups, check health, open tunnels, and manage servers, while a control plane can show live output and hold requests for approval\.

## Key Features

- Runs as an MCP server for SSH, usable by Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex, and other MCP clients\.
- Provides 37 SSH tools for command execution, file upload/download and rsync sync, database dumps/import/query, backups, health checks, service and process management, deployments, sessions, tunnels, groups, aliases, hooks, and profiles\.
- Offers per\-server modes: unrestricted, readonly, and restricted with allow/deny command patterns\.
- Includes an encrypted vault using AES\-256\-GCM, with the master key in the OS keychain where available, and a local audit trail\.
- Adds an opt\-in control plane and desktop application for approval, live terminal output, file browsing, health checks, shells, saved commands, groups, and host keys\.
- Supports approval per server for never, destructive, or always, stored in the vault; approval timeouts or an unreachable control plane deny pending requests\.

## Use Cases

- Ask an MCP client to diagnose production load, memory, disk, or top processes\.
- Create compressed, timestamped MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or file backups with retention\.
- Deploy files to a remote server with ownership, permissions, backup, and restart handled\.
- Run a command across a group of tagged servers, or open a tunnel to a production database\.

## Getting Started

- npm install \-g mcp\-ssh\-manager
- ssh\-manager server add
- claude mcp add ssh\-manager mcp\-ssh\-manager
- Restart Claude Code and ask it something\.
- For OpenAI Codex, configure the MCP server in ~/\.codex/config\.toml and define servers in ~/\.codex/ssh\-config\.toml\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node 18 or later for npm/CLI usage on Linux, macOS, or Windows\.
- rsync is required for ssh\_sync\.
- sshpass is required only when syncing with password authentication\.
- The desktop application carries its own runtime and engine, so it does not require Node\.js or npm\.
- To use ssh\-manager control from a source checkout, build the interface once with npm run build:ui\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Windows desktop builds in 4\.0\.x are not code\-signed, and signing is planned for a later release\.
- Live command output streams can contain secrets, so they are kept in memory and disappear with the window rather than touching disk\.
- If the control plane is unreachable or a request times out, approval\-required requests are denied\.
- npm/CLI deployment requires Node 18\+ on Linux, macOS, or Windows\.

## Overview

Meetily is a privacy\-first AI meeting assistant that runs entirely on your local machine\. It captures meetings, transcribes them in real\-time, and generates summaries without sending data to the cloud\. Built on Rust with Tauri, it supports macOS and Windows, with flexible AI provider options including Ollama, Claude, Groq, and OpenAI\-compatible endpoints\.

## Key Features

- Local First: All processing is done on your machine\. No data ever leaves your computer\.
- Real\-time Transcription: Get a live transcript of your meeting as it happens\.
- AI\-Powered Summaries: Generate summaries of your meetings using powerful language models\.
- Multi\-Platform: Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux\.
- Open Source: Meetily is open source and free to use\.
- Flexible AI Provider Support: Choose from Ollama (local), Claude, Groq, OpenRouter, or use your own OpenAI\-compatible endpoint\.

## Use Cases

- Professionals who need to maintain complete control over sensitive information\.
- Enterprises that need advanced meeting intelligence without compromising on privacy, compliance, or control\.
- Legal and healthcare providers who require data sovereignty and compliance with regulations like GDPR\.
- Teams and organizations (2\-100 users) requiring self\-hosted deployment\.

## Getting Started

- Windows: Download the latest x64\-setup\.exe from Releases and run the installer\.
- macOS: Download meetily\_0\.4\.1\_aarch64\.dmg, open it, drag Meetily to Applications, and launch\.
- Linux: Build from source following the provided guides (docs/building\_in\_linux\.md and docs/BUILDING\.md)\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Windows: Requires an AVX2\-capable x64 CPU; CUDA acceleration requires a source build with NVIDIA CUDA toolchain\.
- macOS: Requires Apple Silicon (aarch64) for the provided package\.
- Linux: Build from source with appropriate acceleration configuration\.
- GPU acceleration: macOS uses Metal and CoreML automatically; Windows packages use Vulkan; Linux requires source build\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Speaker diarization is not yet available in the Community Edition; it is planned for the PRO version\.
- CUDA acceleration is not enabled by default in the Windows installer; it requires a source build with a compatible NVIDIA CUDA toolchain\.
- The Windows installer requires an AVX2\-capable CPU\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mem0 is a drop\-in memory infrastructure for AI agents and apps, providing persistent context that enables continuous learning from past user interactions\. It is built for production use\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-Level Memory: retains User, Session, and Agent state with adaptive personalization
- Memory Compression Engine: condenses chat history into compact memories to cut tokens and latency
- Single\-pass hierarchical distillation and multi\-signal retrieval (semantic, BM25, entity matching)
- Developer\-friendly: intuitive API, cross\-platform SDKs (Python, Node\.js), and managed service option
- Enterprise governance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR compliance, BYOK, zero\-trust, and portable deployment

## Use Cases

- AI Assistants: consistent, context\-rich conversations
- Customer Support: recall past tickets and user history for tailored help
- Healthcare: track patient preferences and history for personalized care
- Sales & CRM: track interactions, objections, and milestones across long sales cycles

## Getting Started

- Install the SDK with pip install mem0ai or npm install mem0ai\. For the cloud platform, sign up at app\.mem0\.ai and use the API key\. For self\-hosted, use docker compose up in the server directory\. The CLI is available via npm install \-g @mem0/cli or pip install mem0\-cli\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires an LLM (default OpenAI gpt\-5\-mini) and an embedding model (default text\-embedding\-3\-small)\. For hybrid search, a stronger embedding model like Qwen 600M is recommended\. Self\-hosted deployment requires Docker\. Python 3\.x or Node\.js is needed for SDK usage\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Open\-source SDK may not match managed platform performance\.
- Mem0 requires an external LLM to function\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mercury Agent is an open\-source, soul\-driven AI agent that runs as a local background service\. It keeps a Second Brain memory in SQLite on your disk, asks for approval before writes or commands, and connects the same agent to the terminal, web dashboard, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and Signal\.

## Key Features

- Permission\-gated actions: reads run without prompts, while writes, shell commands, pushes, and scope changes wait for approval; a shell blocklist blocks commands such as sudo and rm \-rf / in any mode\.
- Second Brain memory: local SQLite with FTS5 full\-text search, 10 memory types, automatic extraction, conflict resolution, hourly consolidation, and /memory controls\.
- Always\-on runtime: mercury up installs a background service with boot start and crash recovery; schedules, heartbeat checks, proactive notifications, and a durable job queue are supported\.
- Mercury Code: a repo\-aware coding environment with AUTO mode, a live plan checklist, per\-file diffs, a workspace IDE, background sub\-agents, and verified completion after a build, test, or typecheck passes\.
- Mercury Bots: persistent specialists with their own persona, model, memory, permissions, and daily budget; fleets can delegate tasks and deliver finished files\.
- Multi\-channel and model flexibility: terminal, web dashboard, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, and 10\+ model providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Grok, Ollama, and Mercury Cloud, with automatic fallback\.

## Use Cases

- Use Mercury Code inside a repository to refactor code, add tests, and only mark work done after a typecheck or test passes\.
- Use Mercury Chat as an everyday assistant that answers from local memory and works with about 50 built\-in tools\.
- Run persistent bots or fleets for scheduled research, writing, and delivery of finished files\.
- Start a task in one channel and check its status from another, such as from the terminal to Telegram\.

## Getting Started

- Install via the one\-line installer for macOS or Linux, or the PowerShell installer for Windows; the standalone binary path does not require Node\.js\.
- Alternatively install with npm i \-g @cosmicstack/mercury\-agent on Node\.js 22 or newer\.
- Run mercury to start the setup wizard, which asks for your name, the agent name, Mercury Cloud or your own API keys, and optional channels such as Telegram\.
- Run mercury up to install and keep the background service running\.
- Use mercury code \. to open Mercury Code in the current repository, mercury doctor to change providers, keys, or channels, and mercury status to see what is running\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Mercury Desktop runs on macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, and Linux; the Mercury runtime also runs as a standalone binary, via npm on Node\.js 22\+, on Android via Termux, and on cloud VMs\.
- The standalone installer downloads a binary for the OS and CPU and verifies its checksum; Node\.js is not required on that path\.
- npm installation requires Node\.js 22 or newer\.
- Signal support uses signal\-cli; it runs natively on Linux and on macOS with Java 17\+\.
- Mercury Cloud is optional; local operation uses SQLite memory under ~/\.mercury and the agent ships no telemetry\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Mercury Desktop 1\.5\.0 is not code\-signed for Apple or Windows, so first launch may require an extra OS prompt\.
- The agent process is not OS\-level sandboxed; safety relies on approvals, a blocklist, and folder scopes, with Ask Me as the default\.
- Signal support depends on signal\-cli; it runs natively on Linux and on macOS with Java 17\+\.
- Community skills are not audited and should be reviewed before installation\.

Mercury Agent 是开源、由 soul 驱动的 AI 智能体，作为本地后台服务运行。它把 Second Brain 记忆保存在磁盘上的 SQLite 中，在写入或执行命令前请求批准，并将同一智能体连接到终端、Web 仪表盘、Telegram、Discord、Slack 和 Signal。

## 核心功能

- 权限门控操作：读取无需提示；写入、Shell 命令、推送和范围变更需等待批准；Shell 阻止列表在任何模式下都会阻止 sudo 和 rm \-rf / 等命令。
- Second Brain 记忆：本地 SQLite，支持 FTS5 全文搜索，包含 10 种记忆类型、自动提取、冲突消解、每小时整合以及 /memory 控制。
- 常驻运行时：mercury up 安装带开机启动和崩溃恢复的后台服务；支持定时计划、心跳检查、主动通知和持久任务队列。
- Mercury Code：面向仓库的编码环境，具备 AUTO 模式、实时计划清单、逐文件差异、工作区 IDE、后台子智能体，并在构建、测试或类型检查通过后确认完成。
- Mercury Bots：持久专家，拥有各自的人设、模型、记忆、权限和每日预算；机器人团队可委派任务并交付完成的文件。
- 多通道与模型灵活性：终端、Web 仪表盘、Telegram、Discord、Slack、Signal，以及 Anthropic、OpenAI、DeepSeek、Grok、Ollama 和 Mercury Cloud 等 10 多个模型提供商，支持自动回退。

## 适用场景

- 在仓库中使用 Mercury Code 重构代码、添加测试，并仅在类型检查或测试通过后才标记完成。
- 将 Mercury Chat 作为日常助手，从本地记忆回答，并使用约 50 个内置工具。
- 运行持久机器人或机器人团队，进行定时研究、写作并交付完成的文件。
- 在一个通道开始任务，并从另一个通道查看状态，例如从终端转到 Telegram。

## 快速开始

- 通过适用于 macOS 或 Linux 的一行安装器，或适用于 Windows 的 PowerShell 安装器安装；独立二进制路径不需要 Node\.js。
- 或者在 Node\.js 22 或更高版本上运行 npm i \-g @cosmicstack/mercury\-agent 安装。
- 运行 mercury 启动设置向导，填写你的名字、智能体名称、Mercury Cloud 或自己的 API 密钥，以及 Telegram 等可选通道。
- 运行 mercury up 安装并保持后台服务运行。
- 使用 mercury code \. 在当前仓库打开 Mercury Code，使用 mercury doctor 更改提供商、密钥或通道，使用 mercury status 查看运行状态。

## 部署与要求

- Mercury Desktop 支持 macOS（Apple Silicon 和 Intel）、Windows 和 Linux；Mercury 运行时也支持独立二进制、通过 npm 在 Node\.js 22\+ 上运行、在 Android 上通过 Termux 运行，以及在任何云 VM 上运行。
- 独立安装器会下载适用于相应操作系统和 CPU 的二进制文件并校验其校验和；该路径不需要 Node\.js。
- npm 安装需要 Node\.js 22 或更高版本。
- Signal 支持使用 signal\-cli；它可在 Linux 上原生运行，在 macOS 上需 Java 17\+。
- Mercury Cloud 为可选项；本地运行使用 ~/\.mercury 下的 SQLite 记忆，智能体不发送遥测数据。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

MetaHarness is the meta\-harness for AI agents and a factory for custom agent frameworks\. It generates repo\-aware harnesses with a CLI, coding agent, MCP server, project\-scoped memory, generated skills, governance policy, release verification, and witness\-signed provenance from a GitHub URL or blank slate\. The output is an npm\-publishable package with user branding and an npx CLI, designed to run across hosts such as Claude Code, Codex, pi\.dev, Hermes, OpenClaw, RVM, and GitHub Actions, within Cognitum's sovereign, verifiable, edge\-native agentic AI platform\.

## Key Features

- Generates a custom AI agent harness for a repository or blank slate, including recommended agents, skills, slash commands, MCP tools, scoped memory namespace, and governance policy\.
- Ships default\-deny MCP support with off, local stdio, and remote HTTPS/auth modes plus policy and audit files; harness mcp\-scan performs static checks for risky tool grants\.
- Includes Darwin Mode, which lets the harness mutate its own config, test changes in a sandbox, and keep only measurable improvements while the model stays frozen\.
- Provides a model router that selects the cheapest model predicted to clear the user's quality bar from eval logs, with optional training on custom data\.
- Supports ten agent hosts, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, pi\.dev, Hermes, OpenClaw, RVM, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Prime Agent, and GitHub Actions\.
- Outputs an npm\-publishable package with custom branding, a custom npx CLI, and host\-specific scaffold wrappers\.

## Use Cases

- Create a repo\-specific coding agent harness for an engineering team and publish it org\-wide as a versioned npm package\.
- Scaffold domain workflows such as DevOps incident response, multi\-source research, customer support, or paper\-by\-default trading\.
- Add governed MCP tools, project\-scoped memory, and generated skills to existing agent hosts such as Claude Code or Codex\.
- Score a repository before scaffolding to estimate harness fit, build likelihood, tool safety, and rough cost per run\.

## Getting Started

- Use the browser Studio, the wizard, or the CLI to generate a harness\.
- Run npx metaharness my\-bot \-\-template vertical:coding \-\-host claude\-code; then cd my\-bot and run npx \. \-\-help\.
- Run npx metaharness \-\-wizard when unsure which options to choose\.
- For an existing repository, run harness analyze\-repo \. \-\-scaffold my\-bot\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- GitHub Copilot host integration requires VSCode 1\.99 or later\.
- The Prime Agent host uses project\-scoped, Python\-backed skills under \.prime/agent/skills and does not use MCP\.
- The field memory overlay requires an absolute storage path, a compatible adapter, and a principal verifier backed by deployment authentication before it opens storage or accepts shared updates\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Minilytics is an open\-source, self\-hosted web analytics tool focused on revenue\. It tracks visitors, conversion rate, revenue per visitor, bounce rate, session time, and online\-now counts, with comparisons against the previous period\. It shows where visitors came from, what they did, and which source led to payment, and it can run on Cloudflare's free plan\.

## Key Features

- Tracks visitors, revenue, conversion rate, revenue per visitor, bounce rate, session time, and online\-now metrics with period\-over\-period changes\.
- Visualizes visitors as a line chart and revenue as bars across hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly views with flexible date ranges\.
- Attributes traffic by channel, referrer, campaign, keyword, and ref tags, and breaks down country, region, city, browser, OS, and device\.
- Records pages, entry pages, exit links, button clicks, custom goals, and funnels\.
- Provides a Journey list connecting each customer to source, amount, time to convert, and a visit\-to\-payment timeline\.
- Supports multiple websites from one login and lets users click a dashboard row to filter the whole view\.

## Use Cases

- Indie hackers and solo founders can see which launch tweet, article, search page, or AI assistant referred paying visitors\.
- Site owners can track signup button clicks, custom goals, and funnels to understand conversion behavior\.
- Teams selling through Dodo Payments can connect payments and refunds to the visitor source that drove them\.
- Developers can self\-host a private analytics dashboard on their own Cloudflare account\.

## Getting Started

- Clone the repository, change into the project directory, and run npm install\.
- Log in to Cloudflare with npx wrangler login, create a D1 database with npx wrangler d1 create minilytics, and paste the printed database\_id into wrangler\.jsonc\.
- Set ADMIN\_PASSWORD and SESSION\_SECRET with npx wrangler secret put, then deploy with npm run deploy\.
- After deployment, open the printed Workers URL, log in, add a website, and copy its script tag\.
- Install the tracker on a site with a script tag using data\-website\-id and the Minilytics host\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A free Cloudflare account, Node\.js 20 or newer, and Git are required\.
- Each deployment creates its own Cloudflare D1 database and requires ADMIN\_PASSWORD and SESSION\_SECRET secrets\.
- The app deploys to Cloudflare Workers; a custom domain can be attached through Cloudflare's Domains & Routes settings\.
- Revenue attribution with Dodo Payments requires configuring a Dodo webhook and pasting its signing secret into the site settings\.
- The free Cloudflare plan provides limits such as 100,000 Worker requests per day, 100,000 D1 rows written per day, 5M D1 rows read per day, and 5 GB D1 storage\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Safari limits cookies set by JavaScript to at most seven days, so returning Safari visitors after a week may be counted as new\.
- With Dodo payment links, checkout metadata may not always reach the payment, so the source recommends an additional return\-page step\.
- The free Cloudflare plan has request, D1 write/read, and storage limits; outgrowing them requires Workers Paid\.

projects.content:
## Overview

mobile\-agent\-testers runs Claude Code agents as mobile app testers, each with its own iOS Simulator or Android emulator on GitHub Actions\. The agents adopt personas, explore apps like new users, and write bug reports with screenshots\.

## Key Features

- Runs up to 20 AI testers in parallel, each on a separate iOS Simulator or Android emulator\.
- Personas vary device model, OS, font size, dark mode, language, location, and user goals, including right\-to\-left languages, tablets, and accessibility text sizes\.
- Finds broken flows, silent failures, missing translations, layout problems, dark mode issues, and accessibility concerns, with numbered screenshots\.
- Supports exploration, end\-to\-end feature runs, bug reproduction, improvement reports, and comparison of two versions\.
- Works with Flutter, React Native/Expo, native Kotlin/Java, Swift/Objective\-C, Kotlin Multiplatform, Capacitor/Ionic, and \.NET MAUI beta\.
- Encrypts reports before they leave the runner, blocks analytics hosts, and groups duplicate findings into one summary\.

## Use Cases

- Run pre\-release exploratory testing on mobile apps without writing test scripts\.
- Exercise one feature end to end or reproduce a reported bug across many devices and locales\.
- Compare two branches or builds before a real A/B test\.
- Check internationalization, right\-to\-left layouts, large text, dark mode, tablet layouts, and accessibility\.

## Getting Started

- Create a public repository from the template, run setup\.sh on Linux or macOS or setup\.ps1 on Windows, trigger agent\-testers\.yml, then collect and decrypt reports with scripts/collect\.sh\.
- Alternatively, add the Claude Code plugin marketplace and install the mobile\-agent\-testers plugin to let Claude set it up\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- GitHub Actions runners; free for public repos, with private repos using your Actions minutes\.
- Linux runners for Android and macOS runners for iOS, provided by GitHub\.
- GitHub CLI and a Claude subscription or API key\.
- Read\-only SOURCE\_REPO\_TOKEN secret for testing a private app repository\.
- Optional model selection and LLM\_API\_KEY for Anthropic\-compatible APIs; optional prebuilt APK or \.app paths for custom builds\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Runs are exploratory and non\-deterministic; expect the same kinds of bugs, but not the same list\.
- Agents can misread screens, so findings should be verified against screenshots before filing\.
- Public repository logs are public, so reports, screenshots, and videos are encrypted before leaving the runner\.
- GitHub runner concurrency and usage limits can constrain large test batches\.
- Private repositories consume Actions minutes, and macOS minutes count ten times\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mochi Diffusion is a native macOS application for running Stable Diffusion and FLUX\.2 Klein models locally\. It uses Apple's Core ML Stable Diffusion implementation for performance and reduced memory requirements, plus the Iris pipeline for FLUX\.2 Klein models with native Metal GPU acceleration\.

## Key Features

- Generates images locally and completely offline\.
- Native macOS app built with SwiftUI\.
- Uses Apple's Core ML Stable Diffusion implementation for speed and reduced memory requirements, especially on Apple Silicon Macs with Neural Engine\.
- Runs FLUX\.2 Klein models through the Iris pipeline with native Metal GPU acceleration\.
- Saves generated images as PNG with generation settings readable by AUTOMATIC1111\-compatible tools and Civitai uploads\.
- Includes a built\-in gallery with import, save, and sync support\.

## Use Cases

- Local image generation on Apple Silicon Macs\.
- Offline image generation workflows where data should remain on the device\.
- Stable Diffusion generation using a starting image or ControlNet\.
- FLUX\.2 Klein generation using up to four input images\.

## Getting Started

- Download the latest Mochi Diffusion release\.
- Download or convert Core ML Stable Diffusion models, or download FLUX\.2 Klein model components\.
- Place models in the MochiDiffusion model folder under the home directory; the location can be customized in Settings\.
- For Core ML Stable Diffusion, create a model folder named as it should appear in the app and move or extract the converted model there\.
- For FLUX\.2 Klein, place text\_encoder, tokenizer, transformer, and vae components in the model folder\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Apple Silicon (M1 and later)\.
- macOS 15\.6 and later\.
- Xcode 26\.0 or later to build from source\.
- Core ML Stable Diffusion or FLUX\.2 Klein models are required to use Mochi Diffusion\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Mochi Diffusion requires separately obtained Core ML Stable Diffusion or FLUX\.2 Klein models to generate images\.
- The app does not collect data or telemetry, and generation happens locally without sending anything to the cloud\.
- First use of a model may take up to two minutes for Neural Engine compilation, after which generations are faster\.
- FLUX\.2 Klein may need constrained input image dimensions due to pipeline attention\-budget limits; Mochi resizes inputs and shows the new sizes\.

projects.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems. It enables access to data sources, tools, and workflows. This repository offers reference MCP servers and SDK examples.

projects.content:
## Overview

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open\-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems\. It lets AI applications connect to data sources, tools, and workflows, providing a standardized way to integrate capabilities\. The repository houses reference MCP server implementations and points to accompanying SDKs and community resources\.

## Key Features

- Open\-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems
- Enables AI applications to connect to data sources, tools, and workflows
- Standardized integration approach compared to a USB\-C port for AI applications
- Broad ecosystem support across AI assistants, development tools, and clients
- Reference servers demonstrate MCP features and official SDK usage
- SDKs available for languages including C\#, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, and TypeScript

## Use Cases

- Agents can access Google Calendar and Notion to act as more personalized AI assistants
- Claude Code can generate a web app using a Figma design
- Enterprise chatbots can connect to multiple organizational databases for chat\-based data analysis
- AI models can create 3D designs on Blender and print them with a 3D printer

## Getting Started

- TypeScript\-based servers in the repository can be run directly with npx, such as npx \-y @modelcontextprotocol/server\-memory
- Python\-based servers can be run with uvx, such as uvx mcp\-server\-git, or installed with pip
- Servers should be configured into an MCP client; for example, Claude Desktop accepts mcpServers entries with command and args
- On Windows, npx\-based client entries should wrap npx with cmd /c

## Deployment & Requirements

- TypeScript servers require npx to run directly
- Python servers require uvx or pip
- An MCP client is needed to use a server in practice
- On Windows, npx commands must be wrapped with cmd /c

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The servers are reference implementations intended as educational examples, not production\-ready solutions\.
- Developers should evaluate security requirements and implement safeguards for their threat model\.
- Some reference servers are archived and may be replaced or maintained elsewhere\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into AI coding agents\. It is stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams alongside the web development community and steers agents away from legacy patterns toward modern web platform solutions\.

## Key Features

- Embeds web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data into coding agents\.
- Provides 200\+ expert\-vetted guides across CSS, Web UI, HTML, JavaScript, Core Web Vitals, accessibility, security, and Web AI\.
- Works with preferred AI coding agents and offers installation through npx, Vercel Agent Skills, Claude Code, Copilot CLI, and Antigravity CLI\.
- Includes CLI commands for searching guides, retrieving guides by ID, and scanning codebases for legacy patterns\.
- Uses live web\-features Baseline data and project browser targets to generate progressive enhancement, @supports queries, or polyfills\.
- Designed to be token\-efficient by pruning lowest\-common\-denominator content that models already know\.

## Use Cases

- Guide coding agents to build new user experiences with modern web features\.
- Modernize legacy code such as modal windows, tooltips, and other older patterns\.
- Improve security and performance tasks through targeted agent prompts\.
- Pair with Chrome DevTools for agents to close the build\-and\-verify loop in a live browser\.

## Getting Started

- Run npx modern\-web\-guidance@latest install to start the interactive installation wizard\.
- Add the skills with npx skills add GoogleChrome/modern\-web\-guidance\.
- Install for Claude Code with claude plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern\-web\-guidance and claude plugin install modern\-web\-guidance@googlechrome\.
- Try commands without installing: npx modern\-web\-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop", npx modern\-web\-guidance@latest retrieve "animate\-to\-from\-top\-layer", and npx modern\-web\-guidance@latest legacy\-scan \.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is presented as a 1\.0 release with expert\-vetted skills and a public evaluation benchmark\.
- Coding agents may default to legacy patterns because their training data includes large amounts of legacy code, so guidance is needed to steer them toward modern solutions\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mole is a Mac utility that combines cleaning, app management, system optimization, disk analysis, and live status monitoring in one app\. It is also offered as a fast open\-source CLI, with native Mac and Windows apps noted in the project description\.

## Key Features

- Clean system junk and stale AI data, with System Data grouped into snapshots, system caches, and logs, and review before cleaning\.
- AI Cleanup covers caches and old versions from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other AI tools, plus old Codex sessions and cleanable worktrees reviewed one by one\.
- Software management checks updates from Sparkle, App Store, Homebrew, and other supported sources; uninstalls apps with leftovers; and manages supported login and background items\.
- Optimize maintains Quick Look, caches, metadata, and common macOS services in one run, with one admin authorization for the whole run\.
- Analyze uses a whole\-disk treemap to spot large files and folders, drill into folders, reveal items in Finder, and move items to Trash\.
- Status shows live CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network, temperature, and fan metrics, plus battery status and process sorting or pinning\.

## Use Cases

- Free up disk space by cleaning system junk, caches, logs, and stale AI tool data\.
- Remove apps with their leftovers and manage supported login and background items\.
- Find large files and folders with a visual disk\-usage treemap\.
- Monitor system performance, battery status, and menu bar metrics\.

## Getting Started

- Download the Mac app from the official site, or buy it; the page lists a $19 one\-time price, macOS 14\+, and a 14\-day refund\.
- For the CLI, the page shows brew install tw93/tap/mole and mo clean\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 14 or later\.
- Accessibility support is listed\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Users are advised to review cleanup items before deciding what to clean, skip, or protect\.
- AI cleanup starts with caches selected, while sessions and tools require user choice, and the Moon entry can be hidden in Settings\.
- Scans and cleanup are described as staying on the Mac, with files and results not uploaded\.

projects.tagline: Open-source headless browser for AI agents
projects.taglineZh: 面向 AI 智能体的开源无头浏览器
projects.description: Moli is a production-ready, open-source headless browser for AI agents, built in Rust. It fetches and extracts web pages, searches the web, and automates browser tasks via CLI, CDP, and WebDriver with a structure-first design.
projects.descriptionZh: Moli 是用 Rust 构建的开源无头浏览器，面向 AI 智能体，可通过 CLI、CDP 和 WebDriver 获取与提取网页、搜索网页并自动化浏览器任务，采用结构优先设计，仅在需要时进行布局和绘制。
projects.content:
## Overview

Moli is a production\-ready open\-source headless browser for AI agents, built in Rust\. It is designed for web access and browser automation, using structure\-first operations that avoid layout and paint unless needed\. Moli can fetch and extract pages, search the web, and automate browser tasks, and it can be used standalone or with Lexmount Browser as a managed cloud runtime\.

## Key Features

- Complete web runtime with streaming HTML parsing, native DOM, V8 JavaScript, iframes and workers, CSS cascade, Fetch/XHR/WebSocket, cookies, WebCrypto, and profile\-scoped storage\.
- Extraction\-optimized CLI output in HTML, Markdown, JSON, semantic text trees, and frame\-aware serialization, with selector, script, and response waits and network tracing\.
- A unified automation binary serves CDP, WebDriver Classic, and WebDriver BiDi from the same kernel and scheduler, without separate ChromeDriver, geckodriver, or browser installation\.
- On\-demand visual capabilities via \-\-layout include layout\-backed hit\-testing and input, viewport screenshots, full\-page screenshots, PDF output, and low\-frequency DevTools screencast frames\.
- Operational controls cover profiles, cookies, HTTP cache, proxies, resource families, connection limits, timeouts, private\-network policy, user\-agent overrides, and diagnostic logging\.
- Structure\-first performance skips layout and paint for most automation requests and generates layout and pixels only when needed\.

## Use Cases

- Fetching and extracting web pages for AI agents and retrieval pipelines\.
- Running browser automation tasks through CDP, WebDriver Classic, or WebDriver BiDi\.
- Searching the web and controlling isolated cloud browser sessions with Lexmount Browser when using managed infrastructure\.
- Crawling, browser\-use agents, evaluation environments, and reinforcement\-learning workloads\.

## Getting Started

- Install the latest prebuilt Moli binary using the provided shell installer on Linux or macOS, or the PowerShell installer on Windows; alternatively, use the README prompt with an AI agent to install the skills and binary\.
- Use moli fetch with options such as \-\-dump markdown, \-\-dump semantic\_tree\_text, or \-\-layout with screenshot or PDF output to extract or render a page\.
- Start the automation server with moli serve; add \-\-layout for geometry, coordinate input, and screenshots, or \-\-layout \-\-resource to fetch optional visual and media resource families\.
- Connect automation clients through CDP, WebDriver Classic, or WebDriver BiDi; Playwright can connect over CDP when the server is running\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Moli supports Linux, macOS, and Windows\.
- The open\-source headless browser can run standalone and is fully usable without Lexmount Browser; Lexmount Browser is an optional managed cloud runtime and control plane\.
- The unified automation binary does not require separate ChromeDriver, geckodriver, or browser installation for CDP, WebDriver Classic, and WebDriver BiDi\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Moli is described as production\-ready within its documented agent\-browser scenarios and remains under active development\.
- Moli intentionally does not pursue pixel\-for\-pixel Chrome parity or high\-fidelity Canvas, WebGL, and media playback\.
- Expensive browser operations such as layout, rendering, and optional resource fetching require explicit opt\-in and are not enabled by default\.
- Unsupported protocol paths return explicit errors rather than implying that a browser action, event, network observation, or visual result occurred\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Monty is a minimal, secure Python sandbox written in Rust for code written by AI\. It avoids the latency, complexity, and cost of a container\-based sandbox for running LLM\-generated code\. It is available as OSS Monty, an MIT\-licensed Python 3\.14 sandbox installed as a package, and as Full Monty, a commercial server that runs the same sandbox behind a gRPC stream\.

## Key Features

- Low\-latency sandboxing: a new OSS Monty sandbox takes under 1 ms from a running pool, and Full Monty takes about 2 ms, compared with around 1500 ms for a sandbox service\.
- The sandbox has no filesystem, environment variables, or network; it reaches the host only through functions and mounts passed in\.
- Host functions and external lookups let sandboxed code call host\-provided tools while seeing only their return values\.
- Snapshots allow the whole sandbox state to be dumped to bytes at an external function call or at the end of a REPL snippet, supporting suspend and resume\.
- Strict resource limits for maximum memory and execution time are enforced by the VM, so operations such as 'x' \* 10\*\*12 raise MemoryError before the allocation is attempted\.
- Packages are available for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Rust; commercial Full Monty runs the same workers behind gRPC as a container image with OS\-level isolation and horizontal scaling\.

## Use Cases

- Running Python programs generated by LLMs safely, especially when agents write short programs that call tools rather than making a sequence of individual tool calls\.
- Powering Code Mode in Pydantic AI, where generated code needs a safe execution environment\.
- Implementing long\-running REPL sessions and human\-in\-the\-loop workflows by suspending and resuming sandbox state from bytes\.
- Scaling many sandbox workers with minimal cost and complexity because no new VM or container is provisioned for every sandbox\.

## Getting Started

- Install for Python with uv add pydantic\-monty\.
- Install for JavaScript or TypeScript with npm install @pydantic/monty\.
- Install for Rust with cargo add monty\.
- Follow the Python, JavaScript, or Rust quickstarts for next steps\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- OSS Monty is installed as a package for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Rust and runs in the application's local execution environment\.
- Full Monty is a commercial server that runs the same sandbox behind a gRPC stream as a service and is available as a container image for larger\-scale deployments with OS\-level isolation and horizontal scaling\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The sandbox does not include a filesystem, environment variables, or network by default; access to the host must be supplied explicitly through functions and mounts\.
- Monty supports a subset of Python and maintains a limitations section covering known divergences from CPython\.
- Full Monty runs code remotely, which the source says reduces the blast radius of an escape and lets sandboxes scale independently of calling hosts\.

## 项目简介

Monty 是用 Rust 编写的轻量安全 Python 沙箱，用于运行 AI 生成的代码，旨在避免基于容器的沙箱在延迟、复杂性和成本上的开销。它有两种形态：OSS Monty 是以软件包形式安装的 MIT 许可 Python 3\.14 沙箱；Full Monty 是商业服务器，通过 gRPC 流以服务形式运行同一沙箱。

## 核心功能

- 低延迟沙箱：从运行中的沙箱池获取新的 OSS Monty 沙箱耗时低于 1 毫秒，Full Monty 约为 2 毫秒，而沙箱服务约为 1500 毫秒。
- 沙箱内不存在文件系统、环境变量和网络；只能通过传入的函数和挂载访问宿主。
- 宿主函数和外部查找让沙箱代码调用宿主提供的工具，同时只看到其返回值。
- 快照可将整个沙箱状态在外部函数调用时或 REPL 片段结束时转储为字节，支持挂起与恢复。
- VM 强制执行最大内存和执行时间等严格资源限制，因此像 'x' \* 10\*\*12 这样的操作会在尝试分配前引发 MemoryError。
- 提供 Python、JavaScript/TypeScript 和 Rust 包；商业版 Full Monty 通过 gRPC 以容器镜像运行相同工作进程，并增加操作系统级隔离和横向扩展。

## 适用场景

- 安全运行 LLM 生成的 Python 程序，尤其适用于 agent 编写调用工具的短程序，而不是依次发起多个单独工具调用。
- 在 Pydantic AI 中支撑 Code Mode，为生成的代码提供安全执行环境。
- 通过从字节挂起和恢复沙箱状态，实现长时间运行的 REPL 会话和人工介入工作流。
- 无需为每个沙箱新建 VM 或容器，以较低成本和复杂度扩展大量沙箱工作进程。

## 快速开始

- Python：uv add pydantic\-monty
- JavaScript 或 TypeScript：npm install @pydantic/monty
- Rust：cargo add monty
- 后续步骤可参考 Python、JavaScript 或 Rust 快速入门。

## 部署与要求

- OSS Monty 以 Python、JavaScript/TypeScript 或 Rust 软件包安装，并在调用它的应用程序本地执行环境中运行代码。
- Full Monty 是商业服务器，通过 gRPC 流以服务形式在远程运行同一沙箱，并以容器镜像形式提供，适合需要操作系统级隔离和横向扩展的较大规模部署。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

Morrow is a free, open\-source, local\-first desktop workspace for notes, databases, canvases and ideas\. It stores each page as a Markdown file in a folder chosen by the user, and it is presented as an alternative to Notion and similar apps without accounts, subscriptions or cloud storage\.

## Key Features

- Pages are plain Markdown files stored in a folder you choose, with no account, subscription or cloud requirement\.
- A rich editor supports headings, lists, checklists, callouts, tables, maths, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams and embedded media\.
- Databases offer table, board, calendar, list and gallery views with properties, filters, sorts and grouping\.
- Wiki links, tags, backlinks, graph views and templates support connected note\-taking\.
- Encrypted pages, same\-network encrypted sync, flashcards, page history and static publishing are built in\.
- Import from Notion or Markdown folders and export to Markdown or PDF\.

## Use Cases

- Building a private personal knowledge base in Markdown that can be opened and synced with other tools\.
- Writing and organising notes, daily notes and research with links, tags and templates\.
- Tracking projects or collections through databases with table, board, calendar, list and gallery views\.
- Migrating an existing Obsidian vault or Notion export into a local\-first workspace\.

## Getting Started

- Use Node\.js 20\.19 or newer to build from source\.
- Clone the repository, run npm install, then run npm run dev to open the desktop app with live reload\.
- npm start runs the built desktop app, and npm run dist builds installers for your platform\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Development and builds require Node\.js 20\.19 or newer\.
- Installers can be produced for Windows x64 and ARM64, macOS Apple silicon and Intel, and Linux x64\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Release builds are not code signed yet, so operating\-system security warnings may appear on first launch\.

projects.content:
## Overview

MotionSites Web Builder is a free Claude skill by MotionSites that helps Claude produce award\-level, cinematic landing pages rather than average AI layouts\. It addresses vague plans, lack of real media, and missing review by supplying example prompts, a cinematic media shelf, technique recipes, design taste rules, a build spec template, and a screenshot\-based look\-and\-fix loop\.

## Key Features

- 40 example prompts drawn from the most\-liked free prompts on MotionSites, with Claude reading the closest 2\-3 for each brief\.
- A media shelf with 50\+ cinematic hero videos, 30 transparent 3D cut\-outs, and 29 images shown on numbered contact sheets\.
- 55\+ technique recipes with working code, including seamless video loops, liquid glass, word\-by\-word blur headlines, mouse\-scrubbed video, spotlight reveals, depth carousels, scroll stories, and real 3D models with Three\.js\.
- Design taste rules with real numbers for type scale, tracking, spacing, colour, motion timing, and copy\.
- A spec template for the precise brief Claude writes before coding, plus a look\-and\-fix loop with a screenshot and QA script and scoring rubric\.
- Prompt mode that returns a prompt tuned for Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Manus, Google AI Studio, or Kimi\.

## Use Cases

- Build a landing page hero for a luxury sleep\-tracking ring\.
- Create an editorial, quiet portfolio homepage for an architectural photographer in Lisbon\.
- Write a Lovable prompt for a waitlist page for an AI travel app\.
- Improve an existing site so it looks award\-winning\.

## Getting Started

- For Claude\.ai and Claude desktop, download motionsites\-web\-builder\.zip from the latest release, then open Customize → Skills → \+ → Create skill → Upload a skill, choose the zip, and switch the skill on\.
- For Claude Code with the plugin, run /plugin marketplace add Motionsites\-AI/claude\-skill and then /plugin install motionsites\-web\-builder@motionsites; an HTTPS marketplace add command is available as an alternative when no GitHub SSH key is available\.
- For manual Claude Code installation, copy plugins/motionsites\-web\-builder/skills/motionsites\-web\-builder into ~/\.claude/skills/\.
- Ask Claude for a site and the skill kicks in automatically; for example, request a landing page hero, a portfolio homepage, a Lovable prompt, or an award\-winning redesign\.
- Optionally install Playwright for the look\-and\-fix loop with pip install playwright && python \-m playwright install chromium\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Code execution must be enabled in Settings → Capabilities for Claude\.ai and Claude desktop use\.
- Claude Code installations use either the plugin marketplace flow or manual copying into ~/\.claude/skills/\.
- The optional look\-and\-fix loop works best with Playwright; install it with pip install playwright && python \-m playwright install chromium\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Claude\.ai and Claude desktop use requires enabling code execution before the skill can run\.
- The screenshot\-based look\-and\-fix loop works best with Playwright, an optional external dependency\.

projects.content:
## Overview

MR Office publishes the source code of its office editors: Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, PDF and Code\. The suite runs on the web and in a free desktop app, includes an AI assistant beside each document, and supports live co\-editing\. The repository contains the same editors used by the commercial product, plus developer integrations for embedding and MCP\-based AI workflows\.

## Key Features

- Five editors: Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, PDF and Code, available in the browser and in a desktop shell\.
- Copilot in every editor edits paragraphs, tables, cells, formulas, shapes and slides in place, previews changes, and allows undo\.
- Edits real Word, Excel and PowerPoint files through the hosted embed and desktop app; the open\-source editors save their own \.mrdoc, \.mrsheet and \.mrslides formats and open CSV, HTML, Markdown and PDF\.
- Live co\-editing and sharing in MR Office online and the desktop app\.
- Embeddable SDK on npm as mroffice\-embed, plus React component packages for the five editors\.
- MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and other MCP clients create, open, edit, read, render and export documents and spreadsheets\.

## Use Cases

- Embed document, spreadsheet, presentation, PDF or code editors in a web app using the hosted embed and session\-token flow\.
- Let AI agents or MCP clients create and edit Office documents and spreadsheets through the MR Office MCP server\.
- Self\-host and build the open\-source editors under AGPL\-3\.0 for products that need document editing\.
- Use the free desktop app for offline editing of Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files with AI and the full formula engine\.

## Getting Started

- Run npm install, npm run fonts, npm run build, and npm run preview to build and preview the five editors locally at localhost:5178\.
- Use npm run dev for a development server at the same address, and npm run smoke to check a build\.
- For the desktop shell, run npm run desktop after npm run build\.
- To embed, run npx mroffice\-embed init, mint a short\-lived session token with createSessionToken from mroffice\-embed/server, and open the editor with open() from mroffice\-embed\.
- To connect MCP clients, use the hosted endpoint or npx \-y mroffice\-mcp locally; Claude Code and Codex can add it with claude mcp add mroffice \-\- npx \-y mroffice\-mcp or codex mcp add mroffice \-\- npx \-y mroffice\-mcp\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Building the editors uses npm commands: npm install, npm run fonts, npm run build, and npm run preview or npm run dev\.
- The desktop shell is Electron\-based and starts with npm run desktop after npm run build\.
- The hosted embed requires a server that signs a short\-lived session token; the secret key is kept on the server\.
- The MCP server can run as a hosted endpoint with OAuth sign\-in or locally through npx \-y mroffice\-mcp\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The embed option depends on MR Office\-hosted editors and a server\-side session token rather than running entirely inside your own app\.
- The hosted embed Free plan includes session limits and app\-count limits\.
- The MCP integration depends on external MCP clients to create, open, edit and export documents and spreadsheets\.
- The open\-source editors alone handle their own formats, CSV, HTML, Markdown and PDF; Word, Excel and PowerPoint support is provided through the hosted embed\.

## Overview

Multica is a workspace that brings AI coding agents and human teammates together\. Agents are assigned issues, pick them up, work on a runtime you control, comment as they go, and hand results back for review\. The intent, run, decisions, and diff stay connected to the same issue, so context is never lost and nothing ships without human approval\.

## Key Features

- Works with 26 agent CLIs including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more\.
- Assign issues to agents like teammates; they pick up, report progress, and hand back for review\.
- Squads: put agents and people on one team with a leader routing work\.
- Skills: turn solved problems into reusable playbooks every agent can use\.
- Self\-host everything with Docker Compose or Helm on your own infrastructure\.
- Review gates ensure work lands in review, not main, so you decide what ships\.

## Use Cases

- Manage multiple AI coding agents in one workspace instead of separate terminal tabs\.
- Assign coding tasks to agents and track progress, blockers, and results\.
- Run automated standups, audits, and reports on a schedule with autopilots\.
- Self\-host for full control over data and infrastructure\.

## Getting Started

- Sign up at multica\.ai or download Multica Desktop for macOS, Windows, or Linux\. The desktop app automatically connects the computer it runs on as a runtime\. Ensure at least one supported agent CLI (like Claude Code or Codex) is installed and signed in on the machine that will

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-hosting requires Docker and pulls official images from GHCR\. The architecture uses Next\.js frontend, Go backend, and PostgreSQL 17\. For development, prerequisites include Node\.js 22, pnpm 10\.28\.2, Go 1\.26\.6, and Docker\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- iOS builds are available from source but not yet on the App Store\.
- The main branch moves quickly with frequent releases, so pull often\.

projects.content:
## Overview

nanobot is an ultra\-lightweight, open\-source, self\-hosted personal AI agent framework written in Python\. It can be used in a browser WebUI, terminal, or chat app to work with files, remember preferences, and schedule tasks, with model providers or local model servers supplying the AI\.

## Key Features

- Runs in a browser WebUI or terminal and connects to chat channels such as Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, and Linear\.
- Built\-in file tools read PDF, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files for tasks such as summarizing reports\.
- Supports shell, web search/fetch, MCP integrations, cron, image generation, and multi\-agent delegation\.
- Keeps session history and long\-term memory through Dream, and supports long\-horizon goals and scheduled automations\.
- Offers model freedom through OpenAI\-compatible APIs, local LLMs, image generation, search, and fallbacks\.
- Exposes a Python SDK and OpenAI\-compatible API for integrations and can deploy as a long\-running local or server\-side agent gateway\.

## Use Cases

- Review a release with parallel agents covering code, regression tests, and rollout risk, then bring their findings into one report\.
- Turn customer feedback into Linear issues with source quotes and acceptance criteria\.
- Schedule recurring work such as a morning brief or weekly review, then check each run and pick up results in the original topic\.
- Read local files such as notes\.txt and write a short summary, or summarize PDF, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint reports\.

## Getting Started

- Install nanobot using the recommended installer, or use uv tool install nanobot\-ai or python \-m pip install nanobot\-ai in a managed Python environment\.
- Python 3\.11 or newer is required, along with access to a supported model provider or local model server\.
- Run nanobot webui for browser setup, then open Settings → Models, save a provider/model preset, start a new topic, and send Hello\! to verify the model connection\.
- For terminal\-only setup, run nanobot onboard \-\-wizard; nanobot \-m "Hello\!" checks one reply, and nanobot opens the interactive TUI\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.11 or newer and access to a supported model provider or local model server are required\.
- nanobot does not supply a model account; model fees or local hardware requirements depend on the chosen service\.
- Self\-hosting guidance covers Docker, Docker Compose, Linux services, and macOS LaunchAgent setup\.
- Render deployment asks for ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY and a private NANOBOT\_WEB\_TOKEN; persistent disks require a paid Render service\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- nanobot depends on an external model provider or local model server and does not include a model account\.
- WebUI access provides administration of the agent instance and should be limited to trusted operators\.
- Background gateway mode does not set up reboot startup or crash restart; an OS\-managed service is needed for that\.
- Interrupted subagent work is not automatically relaunched, and missed scheduled times are not replayed\.
- Render deployments with persistent disks require a paid Render service\.

projects.description: nanochat is a minimal, hackable harness for training LLMs end to end on a single GPU node, covering tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference. It is pitched as the best ChatGPT that $100 can buy.
projects.descriptionZh: nanochat 是一个极简、可修改的 LLM 训练实验框架，覆盖分词、预训练、微调、评估和推理，可在单张 GPU 节点上端到端运行，并被称为“100 美元能买到的最好的 ChatGPT”。
projects.content:
## Overview

nanochat is an experimental harness for training LLMs\. It is designed to run on a single GPU node with minimal, hackable code and covers tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference\. A single depth setting controls model size and automatically derives other hyperparameters so runs remain compute\-optimal\.

## Key Features

- End\-to\-end LLM pipeline covering tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference\.
- A single complexity dial, \-\-depth, sets the transformer depth and automatically calculates width, heads, learning\-rate adjustments, training horizons, and weight decays\.
- The reference speedrun trains a GPT\-2 capability model on an 8XH100 GPU node in about 1\.5 hours for roughly $48, or closer to $15 on a spot instance\.
- A time\-to\-GPT\-2 leaderboard tracks wall\-clock training time against the DCLM CORE score, with runs/speedrun\.sh as the reference path\.
- A CLI chat interface lets users talk to the trained model\.
- Precision is managed explicitly through a global COMPUTE\_DTYPE and can be overridden with the NANOCHAT\_DTYPE environment variable\.

## Use Cases

- Train and then chat with a GPT\-2 capability model on a single 8XH100 GPU node\.
- Run short pretraining experiments with a 12\-layer GPT\-1\-sized model to test code changes quickly\.
- Study scaling laws and train a miniseries of compute\-optimal models by varying depth\.
- Run a small CPU or Apple Silicon/MPS example, with a dramatically reduced model and weaker results\.

## Getting Started

- Install dependencies with uv sync \-\-extra gpu for CUDA or uv sync \-\-extra cpu for CPU\-only/MPS, then activate the virtual environment with source \.venv/bin/activate\.
- On an 8XH100 GPU node, start the reference training pipeline with bash runs/speedrun\.sh; the run takes about 1\.5 hours\.
- After training, talk to the model over the CLI with python \-m scripts\.chat\_cli\.
- For development dependencies, use uv sync \-\-extra gpu \-\-group dev\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The target setup is a single GPU node; the reference speedrun is designed for an 8XH100 GPU node\.
- The code also runs on an 8XA100 GPU node, somewhat slower, and on a single GPU by omitting torchrun, but that takes about eight times longer\.
- GPUs with less than 80GB require tuning hyperparameters such as \-\-device\-batch\-size to avoid OOM or running out of VRAM\.
- CPU and Apple Silicon/MPS execution is shown through a small example script, but it does not produce strong results\.
- Dependencies are managed with uv, using either the gpu or cpu extra\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- GPUs with less than 80GB require hyperparameter tuning to avoid out\-of\-memory failures\.
- CPU or Apple Silicon execution uses a dramatically smaller model and does not produce strong results\.
- The original nanochat announcement contains deprecated information and describes an older model with worse results than current master\.
- Some alternate PyTorch backends are less tested and may have rough edges\.

## 适用场景

- 在单张 8XH100 GPU 节点上训练 GPT\-2 能力模型，并通过 CLI 与其对话；用 12 层 GPT\-1 规模的模型运行短时间预训练实验，以快速测试代码改动；研究缩放规律，并通过改变深度训练计算最优的 miniseries 模型；运行面向 CPU 或 Apple Silicon/MPS 的小型示例，此时模型被大幅缩减且结果较弱。

## 部署与要求

- 目标环境是单张 GPU 节点，参考 speedrun 面向 8XH100 GPU 节点；代码也可在 8XA100 GPU 节点上运行但稍慢，省略 torchrun 后可在单张 GPU 上运行，但耗时约增加八倍；显存低于 80GB 的 GPU 需要调整超参数，例如降低 \-\-device\-batch\-size，以避免 OOM 或显存耗尽；CPU 和 Apple Silicon/MPS 通过小型示例脚本运行，但不会产生强结果；依赖由 uv 管理，可选择 gpu 或 cpu extra。

## 采用前须知

projects.content:
## Overview

NanoClaw is a secure, lightweight alternative to OpenClaw\. It runs your personal AI agent in isolated Docker containers, with a small codebase designed to be understood and customized\. It supports multiple messaging channels, scheduled tasks, and per\-agent workspaces, with credentials secured via a gateway\.

## Key Features

- Container isolation: every active session runs in its own Docker container\.
- Multi\-channel messaging: supports WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, and more, installed on demand\.
- Flexible isolation: connect each channel to its own agent or share one agent across channels\.
- Scheduled tasks: recurring jobs with optional script gates\.
- Credential security: agents never hold raw API keys; outbound requests route through a credential gateway\.
- Skills over features: add channels and providers via skills, keeping your fork lean\.

## Use Cases

- Personal AI assistant on messaging apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Slack\.
- Scheduled briefings and recurring tasks, such as morning news summaries\.
- Customized agent for individual workflows, with per\-agent group providers\.

## Getting Started

- Clone the repository and run the install script: git clone https://github\.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw\.git nanoclaw\-v2, cd nanoclaw\-v2, bash nanoclaw\.sh\. The script installs dependencies, sets up Docker and a credential gateway, and pairs your first channel\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires macOS, Linux, or Windows via WSL2, Node\.js 20\+ (or 22\+ per README), pnpm 10\+, Docker Desktop or Engine, and a Claude or Codex credential\. Claude Code is needed for customization and error recovery\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Users should review the codebase before granting access, though its small size makes review feasible\.
- Docker is the only supported container runtime\.

projects.descriptionZh: Nasiko 是面向 AI 代理、编码代理框架与工具的开放运行时，可发现已在运行的编码代理，按代理框架和模型归集成本，将调用路由到指定模型，并在网关执行策略、追踪每次运行。
projects.content:
## Overview

Nasiko is an open runtime for AI agents, coding harnesses, frameworks, and tools\. It discovers already\-running coding agents, attributes their spend by harness and model, routes LLM calls to chosen models, and enforces policy at the gateway while tracing each run\.

## Key Features

- TokenOps forecasts the cost of a run before it starts, monitors live spend by team, agent, and model, and halts or escalates runs that cross cost, loop, or retry boundaries\.
- The LLM Router gives agents a base URL and short\-lived identity token instead of a real API key, resolving provider, model, and key server\-side so agents and logs never see the real key\.
- Runtime Controls enforce policy at the gateway on each call, including tool and data restrictions, budget and retry ceilings, approvals for sensitive actions, a kill switch, and an audit trail\.
- The Multi\-Agent Harness composes workflows across existing models, providers, and frameworks, coordinating provider switching, fallback routing, state across steps, and traces for every handoff\.
- The platform includes an agentic registry, identity and access mapping, tenant isolation, gateway routing, and observability for cost and traces\.
- Nasiko discovers and manages coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor CLI, with session reporting and LLM routing available for supported harnesses\.

## Use Cases

- Attribute AI spend across coding agents, harnesses, models, and teams instead of reconciling a single provider invoice\.
- Route Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode LLM calls to a chosen provider and model, including serving Anthropic\-format traffic with an OpenAI key\.
- Enforce MCP tool and data access policies, approvals, budget limits, and kill switches for production agents\.
- Compose and trace multi\-agent workflows that span multiple model providers and frameworks while checking cost and policy in flight\.

## Getting Started

- Install the CLI from a checkout with cargo install \-\-path cli/ \-\-force, then run nasiko agents discover to see detected coding agents without changing their settings\.
- Use the Docker\-only quick start when you do not want to install Rust\.
- Download the Nasiko desktop app for macOS, Windows, or Linux\.
- For routing, create an LLM config and connect a supported harness, such as nasiko connect claude \-\-config \<llm\-config\-name\>\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker is sufficient for the Docker\-only quick start; Rust is required for installing the CLI from source\.
- Reporting and routing require an active control plane and valid login\.
- AGENT\_JWT\_SECRET is required for local coding\-agent routing, including custom LLM configs\.
- CODING\_AGENT\_OTLP\_ENDPOINT is needed for coding\-agent telemetry export; when unset, receipts remain pending without an export worker\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Connecting a coding agent changes per\-user global settings and affects every Claude Code or OpenCode process on the machine\.
- Local coding\-agent routing requires AGENT\_JWT\_SECRET, including for custom LLM configs\.

## 项目简介

Nasiko 是面向 AI 代理、编码代理框架与工具的开放运行时。它能发现已在运行的编码代理，按代理框架和模型归集成本，把 LLM 调用路由到指定模型，并在网关执行策略、追踪每次运行。

## 核心功能

- TokenOps 在运行前预测成本，实时按团队、代理和模型监控支出，并在运行越过成本、循环或重试边界时中止或升级处理。
- LLM Router 向代理提供基础 URL 和短期身份令牌，而不是真实 API 密钥；提供商、模型和密钥在服务端解析，代理与日志都不会看到真实密钥。
- Runtime Controls 在网关对每次调用执行策略，包括工具与数据限制、预算与重试上限、敏感操作审批、紧急停止开关和审计记录。
- Multi\-Agent Harness 跨现有模型、提供商和框架组合工作流，协调提供商切换、回退路由、跨步骤状态，并追踪每次交接。
- 平台提供代理注册表、身份与访问映射、租户隔离、网关路由，以及成本与追踪的可观测性。
- Nasiko 可发现并管理 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 和 Cursor CLI 等编码代理，并为受支持的代理框架提供会话上报和 LLM 路由。

## 适用场景

- 按编码代理、代理框架、模型和团队归集 AI 支出，而不是只对一张提供商账单做反向拆解。
- 将 Claude Code、Codex 或 OpenCode 的 LLM 调用路由到指定提供商和模型，包括用 OpenAI 密钥承接 Anthropic 格式流量。
- 为生产代理执行 MCP 工具与数据访问策略、审批、预算限制和紧急停止。
- 组合并追踪跨多个模型提供商和框架的多代理工作流，同时在运行中检查成本与策略。

## 快速开始

- 从代码检出安装 CLI：cargo install \-\-path cli/ \-\-force，然后运行 nasiko agents discover，在不改动设置的情况下查看已检测到的编码代理。
- 不想安装 Rust 时，可使用仅用 Docker 的快速开始。
- 下载适用于 macOS、Windows 或 Linux 的 Nasiko 桌面应用。
- 需要路由时，创建 LLM 配置并连接受支持的代理框架，例如 nasiko connect claude \-\-config \<llm\-config\-name\>。

## 部署与要求

- 仅用 Docker 的快速开始只需 Docker；从源码安装 CLI 需要 Rust。
- 会话上报和路由需要可用的控制平面与有效登录。
- 本地编码代理路由需要 AGENT\_JWT\_SECRET，自定义 LLM 配置也不例外。
- 编码代理遥测导出需要 CODING\_AGENT\_OTLP\_ENDPOINT；未设置时，回执会在没有导出 worker 的情况下保持待处理状态。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：Other。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

NeonClipping is a free, local, open\-source engine for turning long videos into vertical, captioned clips\. It accepts YouTube, Twitch, and Kick links or local MP4 files, finds candidate moments with audio and optional visual signals, writes titles and hooks with a local LLM when configured, and renders 1080x1920 clips with burned\-in captions\. Processing and the clip library are local by default, and no account or subscription is required\.

## Key Features

- Audio\-first Fast mode downloads audio only first, uses YouTube word\-timed captions when available, and downloads only the chosen video sections before rendering 1080x1920 clips\.
- Deep mode adds optical\-flow motion and cut density, shortlists more candidates, and gives the local LLM context before and after each moment\.
- 11 native layouts, facecam position presets, automatic facecam finding, independent face and gameplay selection, and a face\-size slider\.
- Caption styles include GTA Neon, Impact, Clean, Hormozi and MrBeast, with word\-timed editable captions, SRT and WebVTT export, and 52 caption languages\.
- Live clipping reads chat anonymously, counts messages in 10\-second buckets, cuts around chat spikes, and supports a phone remote with a PIN\.
- Creator watch can monitor a Twitch name or Twitch/YouTube channel link, record when the creator goes live, and clip chat spikes using the selected layout and caption style\.

## Use Cases

- Creating vertical captioned clips from long YouTube, Twitch, or Kick videos or local MP4 files\.
- Finding and clipping live\-stream moments around chat spikes on Twitch or YouTube Live, including control from a phone on the same Wi\-Fi\.
- Editing saved clips with layouts, captions, opening headings, templates, background cards, logos, credits, music, and caption animations\.
- Using a free chatbot manually to propose moments from long stream transcripts split into smaller parts, then rendering only the selected sections\.

## Getting Started

- On Windows, download and double\-click NeonClipping\-Setup\.bat; it checks the PC, installs Python and FFmpeg if missing, installs NeonClipping into %LOCALAPPDATA%\\NeonClipping, creates a Desktop shortcut, and opens the app\.
- On Mac or Linux, run install\.sh, or clone the repository and run \./run\.sh; on Windows, run \./run\.ps1\.
- Open the local app in your browser, paste a link, and press Make clips\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10 to 3\.13 and FFmpeg on PATH are required\.
- Optional but recommended: Ollama with llama3\.2:3b for AI titles, hooks, and scores; without it, clips are picked by the audio/motion score\.
- An NVIDIA GPU is optional for NVENC and faster\-whisper; the encoder can fall back to Apple VideoToolbox or CPU x264, and the speech model runs on CPU when no CUDA GPU exists\.
- The desktop server binds to 127\.0\.0\.1 by default; phone access is off unless started with the phone\-access option\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Highlight selection is heuristic and uses a small local LLM, so clips should be reviewed before posting\.
- Videos without YouTube captions must be transcribed by a local speech model, which can be slow on CPU\.
- Deep mode was verified only on a short video and downloads the whole file first on multi\-hour videos, making it slow by design\.
- Live clipping handles one live session at a time and requires the computer to stay awake and online; unattended creator\-watch sessions stop after 3 hours or when less than 8 GB of disk is free\.

projects.content:
## Overview

neuron\-explorer is a steering\-first neuron explorer for Qwen3\.5\-4B\. It pushes every MLP neuron in a layer up and down on a few prompts, keeps every rollout, and lays the results out over a 3D view of the model\. The explorer provides map, list, neuron, embeddings, and Claude chat panels for browsing neurons, steered rollouts, lenses, connections, and live inference\.

## Key Features

- 3D map of model layers with attention and MLP points per neuron, plus hover and click inspection of steer and logit lenses\.
- Neuron list ranked by word\-cluster mass against random\-direction controls, with lens token search and activation filtering\.
- Per\-neuron steered rollouts per prompt and dose, including a three\-column multi\-turn steered chat with negative, zero, and positive steering\.
- UMAP embeddings of a layer's rollouts colored by neuron, prompt, dose, or kind\.
- Claude chat panel using the claude CLI with the explorer as an MCP server to read neurons, cones, and lenses, run live model operations, move views, and use file tools and a shell\.
- Sweep tooling that records neuron stats, rollout text, token IDs, logprobs, top\-k data, rank data, steer lenses, depth reports, embedding layouts, and connection caches\.

## Use Cases

- Investigating how individual MLP neurons affect model behavior by steering them across prompts and doses\.
- Browsing model internals through layer maps, neuron lists, lenses, and connection views\.
- Comparing rollout embeddings by neuron, prompt, dose, or kind to spot structure in steering results\.
- Using an MCP\-enabled Claude chat to query neurons and run live model experiments from the explorer\.

## Getting Started

- Install dependencies with uv sync\.
- Start the explorer with uv run python explorer/server\.py; it reads sweep runs from runs/ and per\-layer stats from stats/\.
- Generate sweep data on a CUDA 13 GPU pod by running sweep/setup\_pod\.sh, then sweep/neuron\_stats\.py and sweep/steer\_sweep\.py\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The explorer loads Qwen3\.5\-4B locally on MPS, CUDA, or CPU\.
- Sweep workflows run on a CUDA 13 GPU pod with the steering fork of vLLM\.
- The Claude chat panel requires the claude CLI to be installed and logged in\.
- The explorer reads runs from runs/ and per\-layer stats from stats/, while explorer/cache/ ships with the repository\.

## Before You Adopt

- No recognizable license was detected; verify permission to use, modify, and distribute the project before adoption\.
- Sweep workflows depend on a CUDA 13 GPU pod and the steering fork of vLLM\.

## 核心功能

- 3D 模型层地图，按注意力与 MLP 展示每个神经元对应的点；悬停可查看 steer lens 与 logit lens，点击可打开神经元，点击层标签可正对该层视图。

## 适用场景

- 研究单个 MLP 神经元在跨提示与跨剂量 steering 时如何影响模型行为。

- 在 CUDA 13 GPU pod 上运行 sweep/setup\_pod\.sh，再运行 sweep/neuron\_stats\.py 与 sweep/steer\_sweep\.py 生成 sweep 数据。

- Claude 对话面板要求 claude CLI 已安装并登录。
- 探索器从 runs/ 读取运行结果，从 stats/ 读取逐层统计；explorer/cache/ 中的缓存随仓库提供。

## Overview

New API is a self\-hosted AI gateway for applications, agents, and teams\. It connects upstream model services such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, DeepSeek, and Qwen, then exposes consistent APIs to clients while centralizing routing, access control, usage tracking, and cost accounting\.

## Key Features

- Unified access to 30\+ AI providers and 100\+ models through a single endpoint\.
- Support for OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini APIs, with streaming, tools, reasoning, and multimodal inputs where supported\.
- Routing controls including model mappings, channel priorities and weights, retries, channel affinity, and multiple upstream keys\.
- Usage and cost management with quotas, subscriptions, usage logs, cache accounting, and expression\-based pricing for different usage tiers\.
- Access control with users, groups, fine\-grained permissions, API key restrictions, OAuth/OIDC, passkeys, two\-factor authentication, and login session management\.
- A web console for configuring channels and models, inspecting usage and audit logs, and trying models in the playground, available in multiple languages\.

## Use Cases

- Share authorized model access across a team while switching upstream providers without reconfiguring every client\.
- Operate a private multi\-model service with a web console for channels, models, usage, and costs\.
- Centralize organization\-level authentication, multi\-model management, usage analytics, cost accounting, and private deployment\.

## Getting Started

- Start a single local instance with Docker and SQLite, persist data in a mounted data directory, then open the console on port 3000 and complete the setup wizard to create the administrator account\.
- Add a channel with an upstream API key, available models, and group assignment, then run a channel test\.
- Configure model pricing and ensure the user has quota or a valid subscription, then create an API key in the console for the same group and models\.
- Point OpenAI\-compatible clients at the local /v1 base URL with the New API\-issued key; list accessible models through GET /v1/models and call supported endpoints such as /v1/responses\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Main database options are SQLite, MySQL 5\.7\.8 or later, or PostgreSQL 9\.6 or later; a separate log database can be configured with LOG\_SQL\_DSN, including ClickHouse\.
- Redis is optional for caching; application nodes that need shared rate limits must use shared Redis\.
- The repository Docker Compose configuration starts New API with PostgreSQL and Redis by default and includes examples for MySQL and a separate ClickHouse log database\.
- Before starting Docker Compose, replace database and Redis example passwords and set a persistent random SESSION\_SECRET\.
- For an HTTPS console, set SESSION\_COOKIE\_SECURE=true and SESSION\_COOKIE\_TRUSTED\_URL to exact public HTTPS origins without paths or wildcards\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Operating as a public generative AI service or API resale service requires completing filing, licensing, content safety, real\-name verification, log retention, tax, payment, and upstream authorization obligations\.
- Users must lawfully obtain upstream API keys, accounts, model services, and interface permissions and comply with upstream terms and applicable laws\.
- Feature availability depends on the channel, upstream model, and conversion path; protocol\-specific tools and fields may not map exactly, and WebSocket support requires a compatible upstream and channel configuration\.
- Production operation requires HTTPS behind a reverse proxy configured for streaming and WebSocket upgrades, plus persistent backups; multi\-node deployments must share the main database and authentication secrets\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Nginx UI is an open\-source web dashboard for editing and safely reloading Nginx site configurations, with automatic backup and version comparison\. It is developed by 0xJacky, Hintay, and Akino and distributed as a single executable binary built with Go and Vue\.

## Key Features

- Web\-based editing of Nginx site configurations with NgxConfigEditor or Ace Code Editor, including syntax highlighting and optional LLM code completion\.
- Automatic configuration backup after changes, with version comparison and restore\.
- Online statistics for server indicators such as CPU usage, memory usage, load average, and disk usage\.
- One\-click deployment and automatic renewal of Let's Encrypt certificates\.
- Cluster management supporting mirroring operations to multiple nodes, plus encrypted configuration export for deployment and recovery\.
- Online Nginx log viewing with indexed search, a traffic dashboard, and visitor maps\.

## Use Cases

- Teams that prefer a browser\-based panel for day\-to\-day Nginx configuration instead of editing files by hand\.
- Operators managing multiple Nginx servers who need cluster mirroring and configuration backup and restore\.
- Users who want to manage Let's Encrypt certificates and inspect Nginx logs and traffic from a web interface\.
- Environments that prefer Docker\-based deployment alongside an existing Nginx container\.

## Getting Started

- Use the latest release build or the Linux installation script to install Nginx UI\.
- On first run, open the panel in a browser to complete configuration\.
- Run Nginx UI from the executable with nginx\-ui \-config app\.ini, as a systemd service, or with Docker\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker deployment uses the uozi/nginx\-ui:latest image and maps Nginx and Nginx UI configuration directories to volumes\.
- For first\-time Docker use, ensure the volume mapped to /etc/nginx is empty\.
- Keep /etc/nginx\-ui on a volume because installed plugins are stored under /etc/nginx\-ui/plugins\.
- Nginx UI follows the Debian web server configuration file standard, placing created site configurations in sites\-available and linking enabled sites into sites\-enabled\.
- Non\-Debian systems may need nginx\.conf adjusted to include sites\-enabled in Debian style\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The source notes that the README does not document the safety model for configuration handling, so production use should follow the documentation\.
- First\-time Docker use requires an empty volume mapped to /etc/nginx\.
