projects.content:
## Overview

Promptfoo is a CLI and library for evaluating and red\-teaming LLM\-based applications\. It supports automated evaluations of prompts and models, red teaming and vulnerability scanning, model comparisons, CI/CD checks, code scanning, and sharing results with a team\. It is open source and MIT licensed\.

## Key Features

- Automated evaluations for prompts, models, and RAG pipelines
- Red teaming and vulnerability scanning for LLM applications
- Side\-by\-side comparison of model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, and Ollama
- CI/CD integration and code scanning for LLM\-related security and compliance issues in pull requests
- Local execution for LLM evals so prompts do not leave your machine
- Declarative configs with command line and library usage

## Use Cases

- Test and improve prompts, agents, and RAGs with automated evaluations
- Secure AI applications with red teaming and vulnerability scanning
- Compare model performance across providers
- Add automated LLM checks to CI/CD and review pull requests for security and compliance issues

## Getting Started

projects.content:
## Overview

PromptHub is a local\-first desktop workspace for managing AI assets such as prompts, skills, rules, MCP entries, plugins, and agent configurations\. It combines organization, version history, multi\-model testing, local scanning, export, backup, and sync so reusable assets can be applied across multiple AI coding tools\.

## Key Features

- Prompt management with folders, tags, favorites, template variables, full\-text search, Markdown rendering, and inline editing
- Skill store and one\-click distribution to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and other mainstream tools, with local scanning and symlink or copy modes
- Agent workspace for skills, rules, MCP connections, plugins, model providers, and session history
- Version history for prompts, skills, and rules with diffs and rollback
- Sync and backup through WebDAV, S3, local snapshots, and self\-hosted PromptHub Web, plus ZIP export and import
- AI testing and generation with multiple providers and models, including parallel model comparison and prompt or skill generation

## Use Cases

- Centralize prompt libraries with variables and version history for repeated reuse and testing
- Distribute reusable skills to multiple AI coding tools from one workspace
- Manage agent\-specific rules, MCP entries, plugins, and model configuration for projects
- Back up or sync AI assets across devices and keep a self\-hosted snapshot for local or LAN access

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop release for Windows, macOS, or Linux, or install the macOS cask with Homebrew
- Create a prompt with a title, description, system prompt, and user prompt; template variables appear as fillable fields when copied or tested
- Open the Skills tab to choose store skills or scan local directories for existing SKILL\.md files
- Optionally configure WebDAV, S3, or a self\-hosted PromptHub Web instance for sync or backup

## Deployment & Requirements

- Desktop builds are available for Windows, macOS, and Linux; macOS packages use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization
- Building from source requires Node\.js 24 or later and pnpm 9
- Self\-hosted PromptHub Web can run with Docker on a NAS, VPS, or LAN and requires a JWT\_SECRET of at least 32 random characters; registration should remain disabled after first user setup
- Desktop and self\-hosted Web must be exactly the same version to create backups

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Private folders are hidden inside the app but are not encrypted on disk\.
- WebDAV and S3 online sync allow only one active sync source to avoid multi\-source conflict writes\.
- Desktop and self\-hosted Web backups require exactly matching versions, and restore is user\-triggered after creating a local safety snapshot\.
- The CLI is not installed automatically by the desktop app and must be packaged and installed from the repository\.
- The Cloudflare Workers branch is not treated as a safe self\-hosted backup endpoint until the desktop backup route is completed\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Pyrefly is a type checker and language server for Python written in Rust\. It combines command\-line type checking with editor features such as go\-to\-definition, autocomplete, hover information, inlay hints, semantic highlighting, and code navigation, with results intended to be consistent across the CLI and editor\. It includes built\-in support for Pydantic, Django, and pytest and reports adoption at Google, Microsoft Pylance, Instagram, and open source projects including PyTorch and JAX\.

## Key Features

- Fast type checking: Pyrefly checks over 1\.85 million lines of code per second and type checks projects like PyTorch 15x faster than Mypy and Pyright; IDE rechecks typically complete in under 10 milliseconds after saving a file\.
- Full\-featured language server: go\-to\-definition, autocomplete, hover, inlay hints, semantic highlighting, and code navigation, with consistent results across the CLI and editor\.
- Editor support for VS Code, Neovim, Zed, and more\.
- Built\-in support for Pydantic, Django, and pytest\.
- Experimental tensor shape checking finds shape mismatches in PyTorch code\.
- Adoption tooling includes pyrefly init for migration from Mypy or Pyright, pyrefly suppress for silencing existing errors, and pyrefly infer for adding annotations\.

## Use Cases

- Type checking large Python codebases where type\-checking time and editor latency are real costs\.
- Providing IDE feedback for Python development through language server features such as go\-to\-definition, autocomplete, and code navigation\.
- Migrating incrementally from Mypy or Pyright by initializing Pyrefly, suppressing existing errors, and adding annotations over time\.
- Checking framework\-heavy Python projects that use Pydantic, Django, or pytest\.

## Getting Started

- Try Pyrefly in the browser using the sandbox\.
- Install the command\-line tool with pip install pyrefly\.
- Run pyrefly init in your project to set things up, generate a config, and access migration options from Mypy or Pyright\.
- Install the editor extension for VS Code, Neovim, Zed, or another supported editor\.
- Use pyrefly suppress to silence existing errors and pyrefly infer to add annotations\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database written in Rust\. It provides a production\-ready service with an API to store, search, and manage points, which are vectors with an additional payload\. Qdrant is tailored for extended filtering support, making it useful for neural\-network or semantic\-based matching, faceted search, and other applications\.

## Key Features

- Dense, sparse, and multi vector search, including late interaction models such as ColBERT\.
- Filtering on JSON payload with keyword matching, full\-text search, numeric ranges, geo\-locations, and should, must, and must\_not clauses\.
- Hybrid search combining multiple vectors in a single query with configurable fusion strategies like Reciprocal Rank Fusion and Distribution\-Based Score Fusion\.
- Vector quantization and on\-disk storage to reduce RAM usage and tune the trade\-off between search speed and precision\.
- Distributed deployment with sharding and replication, plus zero\-downtime collection updates and resizing\.
- REST and gRPC APIs, official client libraries for multiple languages, and a Web UI for exploring collections and monitoring deployment health\.

## Use Cases

- Semantic text search that finds meaningful connections in short texts beyond keyword\-based search\.
- Similar image search, such as visual food discovery where users find meals by appearance rather than names or ingredients\.
- Extreme classification, including e\-commerce product categorization with millions of labels\.
- Recommendation, discovery, and faceted search across neural\-network or semantic\-based matching applications\.

## Getting Started

- Run the Qdrant container locally with docker run \-p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant\.
- Connect to the server with a client, for example Python using qdrant\_client\.QdrantClient with url http://localhost:6333\.
- Use the Quick Start Guide, detailed documentation, and the Qdrant Essentials course for further setup\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The local Docker command starts an insecure deployment without authentication, open to all network interfaces, so the instance should be secured\.
- Before deploying Qdrant to production, review the installation and security guides\.
- Qdrant is also available as a fully managed Qdrant Cloud service, including a free tier\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The default local container deployment is insecure: it lacks authentication and is open to all network interfaces\.

projects.content:
## Overview

QMD is an on\-device search engine for retrieving content from markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases\. It supports keyword and natural language search with BM25 full\-text search, vector semantic search, and LLM re\-ranking, all running locally via node\-llama\-cpp with GGUF models\.

## Key Features

- Hybrid search combines BM25 full\-text search, vector semantic search, and LLM re\-ranking\.
- Runs locally on\-device using node\-llama\-cpp and GGUF models\.
- Indexes collections of markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases\.
- Supports keyword and natural language queries through search, vsearch, and query commands\.
- Provides an MCP server with query, get, multi\_get, and status tools for agent integration\.
- Offers a Node\.js and Bun SDK for embedding search in applications\.

## Use Cases

- Search personal notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases from the command line\.
- Feed structured search results to AI agents and LLM workflows via JSON and file output\.
- Add local document retrieval to Node\.js or Bun applications with the SDK\.
- Enable MCP clients such as Claude Desktop or Claude Code to query local indexed content\.

## Getting Started

- Install globally with npm install \-g @tobilu/qmd or bun install \-g @tobilu/qmd, or run directly with npx @tobilu/qmd or bunx @tobilu/qmd\.
- Create collections for notes, docs, and meeting transcripts using qmd collection add, then add context with qmd context add\.
- Generate embeddings with qmd embed, and search using qmd search for keywords, qmd vsearch for semantic search, or qmd query for hybrid search with reranking\.
- Configure an MCP client to run qmd mcp, or start the HTTP transport with qmd mcp \-\-http\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js version 22 or higher\.
- Bun version 1\.0\.0 or higher\.
- On macOS, Homebrew SQLite for extension support\.
- Local GGUF models are auto\-downloaded on first use from HuggingFace and cached; default models include embeddinggemma\-300M\-Q8\_0, qwen3\-reranker\-0\.6b\-q8\_0, and qmd\-query\-expansion\-1\.7B\-q4\_k\_m\.
- The embedding model requires re\-indexing with qmd embed \-f when switching models, because vectors are not cross\-compatible\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The HTTP MCP server is unauthenticated, so users must add their own authentication before exposing it off\-host\.
- AST\-aware chunking depends on optional tree\-sitter grammars\.
- MCP tool parameters are not strictly validated, so unknown parameters are silently ignored\.

projects.content:
## Overview

quiet\.md is a free, open\-source Beta notes app for macOS and Windows\. It is drawn natively with Rust and GPUI, without WebView or Electron, and stores notes locally as XML files\. It is a rich\-text editor compatible with Feishu (Lark) DocxXML and is designed to remain smooth even with million\-character documents\.

## Key Features

- Native performance: Rust and GPUI render the interface directly on the GPU, with no WebView or Electron\.
- Local\-first files: notes are stored on the user's computer as XML files in a normal folder, with no account or cloud requirement by default\.
- Feishu DocxXML compatibility: notes are saved in Feishu DocxXML format, and copy/paste, import, and export preserve structure\.
- Rich\-text editing: supports headings, lists, to\-dos, quotes, code blocks with syntax highlighting, LaTeX formulas, tables, highlight blocks, columns, images, attachments, and covers\.
- Organization and search: includes a document tree, pinning, favorites, full\-text search, and trash\.
- Import, export, and themes: import Markdown and Feishu DocxXML; export Markdown or PDF; print; built\-in Craft, Feishu, Notion, and Obsidian themes; customizable shortcuts\.

## Use Cases

- Taking and organizing local notes on macOS and Windows without an account or cloud dependency\.
- Writing and editing very large documents, including million\-character documents, with smooth typing and scrolling\.
- Working with Feishu/Lark\-compatible documents, including copy/paste, import, and export while preserving structure\.
- Managing notes as plain XML files with external tools such as Git, iCloud, or other sync utilities, and with agent tools that can read and write local text files\.

## Getting Started

- Download the macOS Apple Silicon build or the Windows x64 installer from quiet\.md or GitHub Releases, then install it\. On macOS, unzip and drag quiet\.md\.app into Applications; on Windows, run the installer\. On first launch, the app adds a Start Guide to an empty document library

## Deployment & Requirements

- The macOS build requires Apple Silicon and macOS 13 or later\. The Windows build requires x64 and Windows 10 2004 or later\. The app has no WebView, Electron, or background service runtime\. The macOS installer is signed and notarized; the Windows installer defaults to the current

## Before You Adopt

projects.descriptionZh: Qwen3 是阿里云 Qwen 团队开发的大型语言模型系列，包含稠密与混合专家（MoE）模型，提供思考与非思考模式，支持多语言、长上下文、推理、编码与智能体能力，并推出 2507 更新版本。
projects.content:
## Overview

Qwen3 is the large language model series developed by the Qwen team at Alibaba Cloud\. It includes dense and Mixture\-of\-Experts models in sizes from 0\.6B to 235B\-A22B, along with Qwen3\-2507 updates in Instruct and Thinking variants\. The series supports thinking and non\-thinking modes for reasoning and chat, multilingual use, long\-context understanding, and deployment or local execution across multiple frameworks\.

## Key Features

- Dense and Mixture\-of\-Experts models in sizes including 0\.6B, 1\.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 30B\-A3B, and 235B\-A22B\.
- Qwen3\-2507 provides Instruct and Thinking variants in 235B\-A22B, 30B\-A3B, and 4B sizes\.
- Switching between thinking mode for complex logical reasoning, math, and coding, and non\-thinking mode for efficient general\-purpose chat\.
- Support for 100\+ languages and dialects with multilingual instruction following and translation\.
- Long\-context understanding of 256K tokens, extendable up to 1 million tokens for Qwen3\-2507\.
- Agent capabilities for precise integration with external tools and complex agent\-based tasks\.

## Use Cases

- Complex logical reasoning, mathematics, science, and coding tasks\.
- Efficient general\-purpose chat, creative writing, role\-playing, and multi\-turn dialogue\.
- Multilingual instruction following and translation across 100\+ languages and dialects\.
- Tool use and complex agent\-based tasks requiring integration with external tools\.

## Getting Started

- Install Transformers with transformers\>=4\.51\.0, load a Qwen3 checkpoint with AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoTokenizer, apply the chat template, and generate text\.
- ModelScope is recommended for users in mainland China and provides a Python API similar to Transformers plus the modelscope download CLI\.
- Other local run options include llama\.cpp, Ollama, LMStudio, ExecuTorch, MNN, MLX LM, and OpenVINO\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Transformers\>=4\.51\.0 is required for Transformers usage, and the latest version is recommended\.
- SGLang\>=0\.4\.6\.post1 is required for SGLang serving\.
- vLLM\>=0\.9\.0 is recommended for vLLM serving\.
- TensorRT\-LLM\>=0\.20\.0rc3 is recommended for TensorRT\-LLM serving\.
- llama\.cpp\>=b5401 is recommended for full Qwen3 support\.

## Before You Adopt

- No recognizable license was detected; verify permission to use, modify, and distribute the project before adoption\.
- Qwen3\-Instruct\-2507 only supports non\-thinking mode\.
- Qwen3\-Thinking\-2507 only supports thinking mode\.
- Ollama naming may not be consistent with Qwen original naming\.
- Ollama default context and prediction settings can cause trouble for Qwen3 models\.
- SGLang and vLLM may have suboptimal multi\-step tool use quality with Qwen3 thinking models due to dropped reasoning content; the suggested workaround is to pass content as\-is while fixes are pending\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Qwen3\-VL is the multimodal large language model series developed by Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud\. It delivers comprehensive upgrades in text understanding and generation, visual perception and reasoning, extended context length, spatial and video dynamics comprehension, and agent interaction capabilities\. It is available in Dense and MoE architectures that scale from edge to cloud, with Instruct and reasoning\-enhanced Thinking editions\.

## Key Features

- Visual Agent: Operates PC/mobile GUIs—recognizes elements, understands functions, invokes tools, completes tasks\.
- Visual Coding Boost: Generates Draw\.io/HTML/CSS/JS from images/videos\.
- Advanced Spatial Perception: Judges object positions, viewpoints, and occlusions; provides stronger 2D grounding and enables 3D grounding\.
- Long Context & Video Understanding: Native 256K context, expandable to 1M; handles books and hours\-long video with full recall and second\-level indexing\.
- Expanded OCR: Supports 32 languages (up from 10); robust in low light, blur, and tilt; better with rare/ancient characters and jargon\.
- Enhanced Multimodal Reasoning: Excels in STEM/Math—causal analysis and logical, evidence\-based answers\.

## Use Cases

- Omni recognition for animals, plants, people, scenic spots, cars, and merchandise\.
- Document parsing with layout position information and Qwen HTML format\.
- Video understanding including video OCR, long video understanding, and video grounding\.
- Mobile and computer\-use agents for GUI control\.

## Getting Started

- Install transformers version 4\.57\.0 or later: pip install "transformers\>=4\.57\.0"\.
- Use ModelScope for checkpoint downloads, especially recommended for users in mainland China\.
- Load models such as Qwen3\-VL\-235B\-A22B\-Instruct with Transformers AutoModelForImageTextToText and AutoProcessor, then apply the chat template for inference\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Requires transformers version 4\.57\.0 or later\.
- Users in mainland China are advised to use ModelScope for downloading checkpoints\.

projects.content:
## Overview

raea, the Render Anything Engine, is a creative studio and desktop app where your own AI writes React and TypeScript for videos, motion graphics, 3D scenes, and games\. The engine draws each frame on the GPU in its own renderer instead of screenshotting a browser, and the app collects agent output in a project feed for watching, scrubbing, marking up, and sending back notes\.

## Key Features

- AI\-directed making: describe what you want in chat, and your own AI model, such as Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, or a local model, writes the raea code and renders it into the project feed\.
- GPU rendering: raea draws each frame in its own engine on the GPU instead of screenshotting a browser, so revisions can come back sooner and the same time can hold more ideas\.
- Video and motion graphics: layout, text, Tailwind, SVG, animation, GPU compositing, hardware encoding where available, and checks for clipped text, low contrast, unsafe areas, freezes, and loudness\.
- 3D and games: TypeScript scenes drawn by Bevy with cameras, lights, materials, glTF models, Gaussian splats, and Bevy plugins; games can be played live and exported as standalone programs\.
- Agent tooling: agent skills, a Claude plugin, craft guides, and queryable render data let an agent render a frame, look at it, and fix issues\.
- Manual editing and review: a timeline for trimming, splitting, moving clips, speed curves, freeze frames, and keys, plus walkable 3D scenes and project review comments\.

## Use Cases

- Creating videos and motion graphics with an AI agent, such as intros, explainers, and short product or promotional pieces\.
- Building and previewing interactive 3D scenes and small games written in TypeScript\.
- Reviewing agent\-generated media through project feeds, comments, annotations, and automated render checks\.
- Using raea from coding agents like Claude Code through installed skills and plugins\.

## Getting Started

- Install raea with the curl installer on macOS or Linux, or the PowerShell installer on Windows 10 or 11\.
- Create a composition as a React component and render it with raea render hello\.tsx \-o hello\.mp4\.
- Use raea init to start a project and raea \-\-help to list every verb\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The app and engine run on macOS with Apple Silicon, Windows 10 or 11 on x86\_64, or Linux on x86\_64\.
- On Windows, raea needs a DirectX 12 or Vulkan GPU driver; the Visual C\+\+ runtime, FFmpeg, and uv are included in its bin folder\.
- Building from source needs Rust, bun, and CMake; macOS needs Xcode command\-line tools\.
- Linux source builds need ALSA, fontconfig, udev, xkbcommon with its X11 part, Vulkan libraries, and NASM, as public CI installs them\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project describes itself as young and fast\-moving\.
- Rough edges are explicitly expected\.
- Windows support is explicitly described as the newest and least tested platform\.
- On Windows, raea requires a DirectX 12 or Vulkan GPU driver\.
- Users bring their own AI model, such as Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, or a local model\.

- 用 AI 代理制作视频与动态图形，例如片头、讲解片和简短产品宣传片。编写并预览用 TypeScript 编写的交互式 3D 场景和小游戏。通过项目动态、评论、标注和自动渲染检查审阅代理生成的媒体。在 Claude Code 等编码代理中，通过已安装的技能和插件使用 raea。

projects.content:
## Overview

Rakazo is an open\-source platform for running persistent AI teammates\. It is available on the web, as an Electron desktop app, and through an Expo mobile app\. Users can bring their own model and computer provider, or run the complete stack locally\.

## Key Features

- Persistent bots with their own conversations, memory, routines, and history\.
- Voice mode for spoken replies, dictation, and calling a bot, with bring\-your\-own keys from ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Cartesia, or Fish Audio\.
- Shared Team Computers and isolated Private computers with browser, terminal, file, and graphical desktop access\.
- Bots that can delegate to peer bots or short\-lived subagents\.
- Bring\-your\-own model credentials through Pi, plus app integrations through Composio or Pipedream Connect and user\-installed Treg, remote MCP, and OpenAPI tool sources\.
- Support for Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, Box, and trusted local computers\.

## Use Cases

- Run persistent AI teammates that keep conversations, memory, routines, and history\.
- Use voice mode to speak replies, dictate text, and call a bot\.
- Give bots browser, terminal, file, and graphical desktop access for computer\-based tasks\.
- Connect external apps and tools through Composio, Pipedream Connect, Treg, remote MCP, or OpenAPI sources\.

## Getting Started

- Use the published\-image installer with Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL; no clone or Node install is required\.
- Run install\-images\.sh to download Compose files, create \.env with random secrets, and start Rakazo\.
- Open the local web interface at the default loopback address, create an account, and connect a model\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- For published images: Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL\.
- For local development: Node\.js 22\.22\.2 or newer in the 22\.x line, Node\.js 24\.x, or Node\.js 26\+; pnpm 9; and Docker\.
- For server deployment: set SANDBOX\_PROVIDER with its API key and RAKAZO\_HOST, and put HTTPS in front of port 5173\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Rakazo is in beta\.
- Node\.js 23\.x and 25\.x are not supported\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Raven is a self\-evolving multi\-agent orchestration ecosystem and a host agent that brings built\-in and third\-party agents together to carry out complex tasks\. It generates DAGs and orchestrates specialized agents, supports harness self\-evolution, and is powered by EverOS for memory and context across sessions\.

## Key Features

- Generates DAGs and orchestrates multiple specialized agents for complex tasks\.
- Includes four built\-in agents: Raven\-Research, Raven\-Code, Raven\-Design, and Raven\-Oncall\.
- Connects third\-party agents via ACP, CLI, or OpenAI\-compatible APIs, with presets for 13 agents\.
- Uses EverOS Memory to preserve user context, agent experience, and world knowledge across sessions\.
- Uses SkillForge to retrieve relevant skills from local libraries, EverOS memory, and SkillHub's catalog\.
- Combines event monitoring and scheduled execution for proactive reminders and follow\-up work\.

## Use Cases

- Deep research for complex questions, literature reviews, and technical analysis, with structured reports and traceable sources\.
- Agentic software development for feature implementation, debugging, refactoring, data processing, and data analysis\.
- Visual design for PowerPoint slide decks, brand assets, charts, diagrams, and web interfaces\.
- Unattended workflow automation for experimentation, optimization, and continuous monitoring\.

## Getting Started

- On Linux, macOS, or WSL2, run: curl \-fsSL https://raven\.evermind\.ai/install\.sh \| bash
- On native Windows PowerShell, run: irm https://raven\.evermind\.ai/install\.ps1 \| iex
- For a container deployment, clone the repository, enter the Raven directory, and run: docker compose \-f docker/docker\-compose\.yml up
- After container deployment, open http://localhost:18793 in your browser\.
- Run raven web to launch the WebUI, or raven web \-\-stop to stop the background service\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The shell installer supports Linux, macOS, and WSL2\.
- Native Windows PowerShell is supported\.
- Container deployment requires Git and Docker with Docker Compose\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The Curator component is explicitly experimental and is distributed with the source repository rather than the installed package\.
- Third\-party agent orchestration depends on ACP, CLI, or OpenAI\-compatible APIs\.

projects.descriptionZh: Raven 通过在 Linux 上重新实现 Windows 内核及其服务，而非模拟整台 PC，来运行 Windows 应用和安装程序；无需虚拟机、winetricks 或 DLL 覆盖。
projects.content:
## Overview

Raven runs Windows applications on Linux by reimplementing the Windows kernel and its services rather than emulating a whole PC\. Program code executes directly on the CPU inside a sandbox where every system call is answered by Raven, covering processes and threads, files, the registry, windows, and input\. Graphics go to Wayland and Vulkan, with DXVK and vkd3d\-proton handling Direct3D\.

## Key Features

- Kernel reimplementation rather than emulation, so application code runs natively while Raven intercepts and answers system calls\.
- Sandbox boundary in which programs cannot reach Linux directly; file dialogs grant only the chosen file or folder and refusals are logged in sandbox\.log\.
- Installer support for NSIS, Inno Setup, and Windows Installer (MSI) packages, including custom actions, rollback, and elevation\.
- Graphics through Wayland and Vulkan, with DXVK and vkd3d\-proton for Direct3D 8, 9, 11, and 12\.
- 32\-bit and 64\-bit programs can run side by side in the same prefix\.
- Provisioning scripts fetch pinned versions of DXVK, vkd3d\-proton, Skia, and root certificates\.

## Use Cases

- Running Windows installers and desktop applications on x86\_64 Linux without a virtual machine\.
- Running 32\-bit and 64\-bit Windows programs side by side in one prefix\.
- Running Direct3D programs and games through DXVK and vkd3d\-proton\.
- Testing Windows applications in sandboxed prefixes with snapshots and per\-program layers\.

## Getting Started

- Build Raven from source on x86\_64 Linux with CMake 3\.20 or newer, a C\+\+20 compiler, Python 3\.11 or newer, and MinGW\-w64 13 or newer for x86\_64 and i686\.
- Clone the repository and configure a build with CMake using the RelWithDebInfo build type, then build it\.
- A minimal build runs console programs and simple windows; installers and most desktop apps need the provisioned common controls, shell dialogs, and installer services\.
- Provision the components, reconfigure with the RAVEN\_\* component paths, rebuild, and launch a program with the native raven binary using \-\-run\-process and an installer executable\.
- Run tests with ctest \-\-test\-dir build \-\-output\-on\-failure \-j1\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Linux on x86\_64\.
- CMake 3\.20 or newer, a C\+\+20 compiler, and Python 3\.11 or newer\.
- MinGW\-w64 13 or newer for x86\_64 and i686 to build the Windows test programs\.
- clang, widl, bison, and patch to build the installer components\.
- Optional OpenSSL for crypt32 certificate chains, Schannel, HTTPS, and CryptoAPI ciphers\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is described as early\-stage and source\-only, and its build and component\-provisioning setup is non\-trivial\.
- The X11 desktop path is experimental, and OpenSSL is optional but needed for certain certificate\-chain, Schannel, HTTPS, and CryptoAPI cipher functionality\.

projects.content:
## Overview

REA is an MCP\-based toolset for reverse engineering with coding agents\. It connects an agent to tools that inspect native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, \.NET assemblies, websites, Android packages, firmware, and other targets\. Analysis runs locally, and results include evidence and limitations\.

## Key Features

- Connects coding agents through MCP to inspect targets and trace relevant code\.
- Supports native binary analysis with Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA, returning pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references\.
- Analyzes JavaScript and Electron applications, including modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC, and native add\-on relationships\.
- Covers many targets such as \.NET assemblies, Android APKs and devices, websites, firmware, saved network captures, SQLite databases, recorded packets, and process behavior\.
- Runs analysis locally and returns findings with the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion\.

## Use Cases

- Explain how a feature in an app, game, or website works by having an agent inspect the target and trace the code behind it\.
- Recover logic from a binary or application and build a version of the feature for your own project\.
- Investigate native binaries to examine functions, strings, references, and call relationships in executables and libraries\.
- Follow runtime behavior through browser or process activity and compare results across runs\.

## Getting Started

- Install Node\.js and npm, then run npx rea\-agents@latest setup in your terminal\.
- Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, approve them, and restart your agent afterward\.
- Ask your agent to inspect a target, for example: Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project\.
- Use terminal commands such as npx \-y rea\-agents@latest analyze\-javascript\-application /absolute/path/to/app \-\-json\.
- To install the rea command for regular use, run npm install \-\-global rea\-agents and then rea \-\-help\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- REA requires Node\.js 22\.x (\>=22\.19), 24\.x (\>=24\.11), or 26\+, plus npm\.
- Native binary analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval\.
- Static JavaScript and Electron analysis needs Node\.js and npm; on Linux it requires a procps\-compatible ps on REA's PATH for process ownership checks\.
- Other targets may require caller\-supplied tools such as JADX and a full JDK for Android APKs, adb for Android devices, Binwalk or Unblob for firmware, TShark 4\.x for recorded packets, or pwntools for offline ELF layout and recorded Linux crashes\.
- Static JavaScript and \.NET inspection read supplied files without running the application\. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- A similar repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official\.
- REA requires Node\.js 22\.x (\>=22\.19), 24\.x (\>=24\.11), or 26\+, plus npm\.
- Native binary analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval\.

## 项目简介

REA 是一套基于 MCP 的逆向工程工具集，供编程智能体使用。它把智能体连接到可检查原生二进制、JavaScript 与 Electron 应用、\.NET 程序集、网站、Android 包、固件等多种目标的工具。分析在本地运行，结果会附带证据与局限。

## 核心功能

- 通过 MCP 连接编程智能体，检查目标并追踪相关代码。
- 原生二进制分析可配合 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA，返回伪代码、汇编、字符串、符号、调用与引用。
- 分析 JavaScript 与 Electron 应用，涵盖模块、导入、source map、路由、IPC 与原生插件关系。
- 覆盖 \.NET 程序集、Android APK 与设备、网站、固件、已保存的网络抓包、SQLite 数据库、录制的数据包以及进程行为等目标。
- 分析在本地运行，每项结论都附带证据与局限。

## 适用场景

- 让智能体检查某个应用、游戏或网站，并追踪其背后的代码，解释该功能是如何工作的。
- 从二进制或应用中还原逻辑，并为自己的项目重建该功能。
- 调查原生二进制，查看可执行文件与库中的函数、字符串、引用和调用关系。
- 通过浏览器或进程活动跟踪运行时行为，并比较多次运行的结果。

## 快速开始

- 安装 Node\.js 与 npm，然后在终端运行 npx rea\-agents@latest setup。
- 选择要接入的智能体，检查它提出的更改并批准，随后重启你的智能体。
- 让智能体检查某个目标，例如：了解 Notes 应用中的搜索是如何工作的，向我展示证据，并为我的项目构建类似功能。
- 也可以使用终端命令，例如 npx \-y rea\-agents@latest analyze\-javascript\-application /absolute/path/to/app \-\-json。
- 若要安装常用的 rea 命令，运行 npm install \-\-global rea\-agents，然后运行 rea \-\-help。

## 部署与要求

- REA 需要 Node\.js 22\.x（\>=22\.19）、24\.x（\>=24\.11）或 26\+，以及 npm。
- 原生二进制分析可使用现有的 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA 安装；setup 可在获得批准后选择安装 Hopper。
- 静态 JavaScript 与 Electron 分析需要 Node\.js 和 npm；在 Linux 上还需要 REA 的 PATH 中有兼容 procps 的 ps，用于进程归属检查。

- 静态 JavaScript 与 \.NET 检查只读取提供的文件，不运行应用。运行时捕获会以你的用户权限运行或与所选目标交互。

projects.content:
## Overview

Reason Network connects coding\-agent sessions across teammates' computers\. A small daemon runs on each computer, and agents can list the team, send messages, ask users for approval, and exchange small text files directly or through an encrypted relay\.

## Key Features

- Agents can discover teammates and send messages using tools such as list\_team, send\_message, ask\_user, and check\_inbox\.
- Supports coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, Command Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Grok CLI, opencode, pi, DeepSeek Harness, and Reason\.
- Messages are delivered according to each agent's delivery path, and idle sessions can wake\.
- Messages can carry up to 10 text files, 256 KB each and 512 KB total, saved under ~/\.reason/network/inbox and never executable or opened automatically\.
- Peer\-to\-peer connections are end\-to\-end encrypted, and relays only see encrypted bytes\.
- A macOS menu bar icon shows who is online and what their sessions are doing\.

## Use Cases

- Ask a teammate's coding agent a question or request a small text file without relaying the message yourself\.
- Coordinate work across multiple coding\-agent sessions and repositories on a team\.
- Let an agent ask you to approve or deny a request when a teammate's agent needs a decision only you can make\.
- Check who is online and what their agent sessions are working on\.

## Getting Started

- Paste the provided join line into a supported coding agent, or run the Reason Network installer in a terminal\.
- Sign in with Reason using Google, GitHub, Apple, or email; other computers join by signing in with the same account\.
- Friends join with the invite line printed at the end; hosted assistants can be connected through an MCP server\.
- On Windows, use the PowerShell installer\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- One small daemon runs per computer\.
- macOS, Linux, and Windows are supported\.
- Direct connections use a random UDP port; a fixed port can be set in ~/\.reason/network/config\.toml for firewall or router forwarding\.
- Teams can run their own relay; otherwise computers use n0 address lookup\.
- Hosted assistants require an MCP server connection\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Computers find each other through n0 address lookup by default, with an option for teams to run their own relay\.
- Relayed traffic is encrypted, so the relay only sees encrypted bytes\.
- Direct connections use a random UDP port each time the daemon starts\.
- On macOS, notifications come from Script Editor and must be allowed once in System Settings\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Recordly is an open\-source desktop app for recording and editing screen captures with motion\-driven presentation tools built in\. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, combining platform\-specific capture with a renderer\-driven editor and export pipeline for demos, walkthroughs, and product videos\.

## Key Features

- Automatic zoom suggestions, smooth cursor movement, motion effects, and styled frames with wallpapers, colors, gradients, blur, padding, and shadows\.
- Dynamic webcam bubble overlays with positioning, mirroring, shadow, roundness, and optional zoom\-reactive scaling\.
- Drag\-and\-drop timeline editing for zooms, trims, speed regions, annotations, audio regions, and crop\-aware edits, with projects saved as \.recordly files\.
- Recording of an entire display or a single app window, with microphone and system audio capture and native capture backends where supported\.
- MP4 and GIF export with quality, frame\-rate, loop, size, aspect ratio, and output dimension controls\.
- Community\-driven extensions and a marketplace for cursor click sounds, device frames, browser mockups, wallpapers, render hooks, and settings panels\.

## Use Cases

- Creating product demos and walkthroughs\.
- Recording tutorials and educational videos\.
- Producing quick social posts as MP4 or looping GIF\.
- Adding polish to raw screen captures without a motion designer\.

## Getting Started

- Download a prebuilt release for macOS, Windows, or Linux\.
- On Arch Linux or Manjaro, install the recordly\-bin package from the AUR with yay \-S recordly\-bin\.
- To build from source, clone the repository, run npm install, then npm run dev; use npm run build for packaged builds\.
- On macOS, if a locally built app is quarantined, remove the quarantine flag with xattr \-rd com\.apple\.quarantine /Applications/Recordly\.app\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 14\.0 (Sonoma) or later\.
- Windows 10 20H1 (Build 19041, May 2020) or later for the native Windows Graphics Capture helper and best cursor\-hiding behavior\.
- Linux on modern distros; system audio generally requires PipeWire\.
- macOS build from source requires Xcode Command Line Tools\.
- Linux Ubuntu/Debian build from source requires build\-essential, cmake, libx11\-dev, libxtst\-dev, libxrandr\-dev, and libxt\-dev\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- On Linux, cursor hiding is not currently supported through Electron desktop capture\.
- On Linux, enabling the rendered cursor overlay while using Electron desktop capture may result in exports showing both the real cursor and the styled cursor\.
- On Windows builds older than 19041, recording can fall back to Electron capture and the real OS cursor may remain visible in recordings\.
- System audio support varies by platform, and Linux system audio generally requires PipeWire\.
- Locally built macOS apps may be quarantined by macOS\.

projects.descriptionZh: Repomix 可将整个代码库打包为一个 AI 友好文件，便于把完整仓库上下文共享给大型语言模型和其他 AI 工具，用于代码审查、重构、实现规划、文档生成和项目协助。
projects.content:
## Overview

Repomix is a tool that transforms an entire repository into a single AI\-friendly file\. It formats the codebase for AI comprehension and can produce XML, Markdown, JSON, or plain text output\. It is designed for sharing full repository context with large language models and other AI tools\.

## Key Features

- AI\-optimized output formats codebase content for easier AI understanding and processing\.
- Token counting reports token counts for each file and the entire repository\.
- Git\-aware behavior automatically respects \.gitignore, \.ignore, and \.repomixignore files\.
- Security\-focused scanning uses Secretlint to detect files matching known credential formats and leave them out of output\.
- Code compression uses Tree\-sitter to extract key code elements and reduce token usage\.
- Customization supports include and ignore patterns, output styles, persistent configuration, and remote repository packing\.

## Use Cases

- Code review and refactoring with AI assistants using the packed repository as context\.
- Implementation planning, bug investigation, and third\-party library security checks\.
- Documentation generation and test case generation from the whole codebase\.
- Creating LLM\-compatible knowledge datapacks from written content such as blogs, documentation, and books\.

## Getting Started

- Run npx repomix@latest in a project directory to try Repomix without installation\.
- Install globally with npm install \-g repomix, yarn global add repomix, bun add \-g repomix, or Homebrew, then run repomix\.
- Repomix generates repomix\-output\.xml in the current directory containing the repository in an AI\-friendly format\.
- Run repomix \-\-init to create a repomix\.config\.json file for persistent settings\.
- Use repomix \-\-remote with a repository shorthand or URL to pack a remote repository\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Repomix can be run through npx, a global npm, yarn, or bun installation, Homebrew, or Docker\.
- Container use is supported with the ghcr\.io/yamadashy/repomix image\.
- The CLI can access private repositories because it uses the locally installed git\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Credential\-file exclusion depends on Secretlint matching known credential formats\.
- Enabling output escaping according to the chosen style schema can increase token count\.

projects.name: Rerun
projects.tagline: The data layer for physical AI. From collection to training.
projects.taglineZh: 面向物理 AI 的数据层，覆盖从采集到训练
projects.description: Rerun is the data layer for physical AI, with an open source SDK to log, query, visualize, and stream multimodal robotics data from collection to training.
projects.descriptionZh: Rerun 是面向物理 AI 的数据层，提供开源 SDK，用于记录、查询、可视化和流式传输多模态机器人数据，贯穿从采集到训练的全流程。
projects.content:
## Overview

Rerun is the data layer for physical AI\. It ingests multi\-rate, multimodal data such as images, point clouds, transforms, time series, joint states, and video from robot logs, human\-data rigs, simulation, and web video\. The built\-in viewer renders everything in sync and in realtime, while the same data can be queried with dataframes or SQL and streamed directly into training\. It is built in Rust on column\-chunk storage purpose\-built for multi\-rate physical data, with SDKs in Python, Rust, and C\+\+\.

## Key Features

- Log, query, visualize, and stream multimodal robotics data with an open source SDK\.
- Visualize multi\-rate, multimodal sequences in sync and in realtime with a time\-aware built\-in viewer\.
- Query recordings with full dataframe or SQL queries down to columns, time ranges, and values\.
- Store multi\-rate, multimodal data as column\-chunks in rrd files, and ingest from formats such as MCAP, rrd, and LeRobot\.
- Stream dataset mixes directly to training without an export step, using a column\-aware and video\-codec\-aware dataloader\.
- Rerun Hub provides catalog, byte\-range indexing, retrieval, query, transform, train, and team sharing infrastructure for Rerun data\.

## Use Cases

- Debugging robotics systems by visualizing RGB camera feeds, depth images, lidar scans, segmentation outputs, 3D maps, detected objects, and confidence over time\.
- Running computer vision pipelines such as SLAM, hand tracking, and motion retargeting as table edits\.
- Querying raw, intermediate, and derived data with dataframes or SQL to build datasets for training and evaluation\.
- Streaming dataset mixes directly to GPUs for training without export jobs or stale copies\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Python SDK with pip install rerun\-sdk\.
- Add the Rust SDK with cargo add rerun\.
- Install the Rerun Viewer binary to stream log data over the network or load \.rrd data files; it can be installed with pip install rerun\-sdk or cargo install rerun\-cli \-\-locked \-\-features nasm\.
- Run the Rerun Viewer in a browser, or follow the C\+\+, Python, or Rust quick start guides\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- To stream log data over the network or load \.rrd data files, install the rerun binary\.
- Only the Python SDK comes bundled with the Viewer; C\+\+ and Rust rely on a separate Viewer install\.
- The nasm Cargo feature requires the nasm CLI to be installed and available in your path; skipping it may result in inferior video decoding performance\.
- The Rerun Viewer can run in a web browser\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Rerun is in active development and the API is still evolving, so breaking changes should be expected\.
- Viewer performance can degrade when there are too many entities\.
- Multi\-million point clouds can be slow\.
- Rerun Hub, the scalable catalog for robotic data, is currently available only for a few select design partners\.

## 项目简介

projects.content:
## Overview

RGB MoCap is a native Windows application for turning ordinary video into editable human motion\. It provides a workspace to track video, preview 3D motion, review results, and export or stream animation\. AI processing runs locally on the user's hardware, so footage is not uploaded to someone else's server\.

## Key Features

- Local AI motion capture from ordinary video, with processing on the user's own hardware and no upload of footage to a remote server\.
- Supports ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR, MAMMA, PromptHMR, GEM\-X, and experimental PEAR live preview across different body representations and workflows\.
- Foot and palm contact correction with editable contact timings to reduce sliding\.
- Retarget motion to Mixamo FBX, VRM, and PMX humanoid characters, or import a character and retarget motion\.
- Export FBX or BVH, VMD for MMD, portable Blender projects, and UE5 mannequin animation; stream bones to Blender or Unreal Live Link, including MetaHuman expressions\.
- Multi\-camera capture and optional real\-time webcam or video tracking with PEAR's experimental body and finger preview\.

## Use Cases

- Animators who want to capture motion from ordinary video without a marker suit, studio, or cloud subscription\.
- Blender and Unreal Engine creators who need to stream captured motion into existing character workflows\.
- Multi\-camera setups that need more reliable motion capture than a single view\.
- MMD, VRM, and humanoid rig workflows that need retargeting and VMD or FBX export\.

## Getting Started

- Install Git for Windows and use a short, writable installation path\.
- Clone the repository, run install\.cmd to prepare base runtimes, then start the app with RGBMoCap\.cmd and keep the console open\.
- Use Model Manager to prepare AI weights and body files; some require account registration and manual download\.
- To update, close the app and run update\.cmd from the same folder\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires 64\-bit Windows, a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver, and OpenGL 4\.3\.
- Installed six offline models and runtimes are approximately 77\.8 GB (72\.5 GiB), excluding projects, caches, or retained downloads; app source, C\+\+/CUDA compiler tools, temporary install files, and saved work need additional space\.
- MAMMA and PromptHMR require Visual Studio 2022 C\+\+ Build Tools, the Windows SDK, and CUDA Toolkit 12\.8 for local native builds; GEM\-X does not require the C\+\+ build tools or CUDA Toolkit\.
- On Windows 11, Smart App Control in On mode may block the unsigned private Python runtime used by RGB MoCap, stopping installation or launch\.
- Optional SAM 3\.1 tracking uses a 1\.75 GB checkpoint and more VRAM than default tracking\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Model files are prepared separately in Model Manager, and some require account registration and manual downloads, which adds setup overhead\.
- The project explicitly is not a one\-click tool; setup involves multiple runtimes and dependencies\.
- MAMMA, PromptHMR, and GEM\-X require separate runtime installation beyond the base install and update scripts\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Rivet is an open\-source, self\-hostable orchestrator for agentic workloads\. It runs agents, workflows, and sandboxes as durable Actors, with in\-memory state, persistence, networking, and scheduling built in\. Actors are long\-running lightweight processes that can hibernate when idle and scale to zero\.

## Key Features

- Durable Actors with in\-memory state and automatic persistence through SQLite or a BYO database\.
- Workflows, queues, and scheduling with automatic retries and durable state across steps\.
- Sandboxes with a filesystem, shell, and network for code you did not write\.
- HTTP and WebSocket networking, multi\-region routing, and end\-to\-end type safety\.
- Typed SDKs for TypeScript, Node\.js, Rust, React, and Effect\.
- Built\-in observability with OpenTelemetry, traces, metrics, structured logs, and an inspector\.

## Use Cases

- AI agents: each agent runs as its own Actor with persistent context, memory, and scheduled tool calls\.
- Sandbox orchestration: coordinate sandbox sessions, queue work, and schedule cleanup in one long\-lived Actor per workspace\.
- Workflows: multi\-step operations with automatic retries, scheduling, and durable state across steps\.
- Collaborative documents and chat: each document or room is an Actor broadcasting changes or realtime messages to connected users\.

## Getting Started

- Install RivetKit with npm install rivetkit\.
- Give a coding agent the Rivet skills with npx skills add rivet\-dev/skills\.
- Start from scratch with quickstarts for Node\.js and Bun, React, or Next\.js\.
- Self\-host locally with docker run \-p 6420:6420 rivetdev/engine\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Run as just a library during development; actors run in your process with no servers or infrastructure\.
- Self\-host with a single Rust binary or Docker container using Postgres, file system, or FoundationDB\.
- Use Postgres or FoundationDB for persistence and tiered storage to S3\.
- Supported deployment targets include Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Virtual Machine, AWS ECS, Railway, Render, and custom platforms\.
- For BYOC, the control plane runs inside your own VPC and is maintained by Rivet over an outbound connection\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The Rust client for RivetKit is marked experimental\.
- The Python client for RivetKit is marked experimental\.
- The 12\.3 ms cold start figure uses an experimental Rivet feature that will be enabled by default in an upcoming update\.
- With BYOC, the control plane and storage run inside your VPC, your data never leaves your cloud, and there is no inbound management connection\.

projects.content:
## Overview

RocketRide is an open\-source AI pipeline engine and development environment\. It defines workflows as portable JSON \.pipe files, built visually in VS Code or through the CLI, and executes them on a multithreaded C\+\+ runtime\. It supports LLM workflows, multi\-agent orchestration, observability, SDK integration, and deployment on Docker, on\-premises, or RocketRide Cloud\.

## Key Features

- Visual pipeline builder in VS Code with portable JSON \.pipe files and real\-time observability for token usage, LLM calls, latency, and execution\.
- High\-performance multithreaded C\+\+ runtime designed for AI and data workload throughput\.
- Pipeline nodes cover LLM providers, vector databases, OCR, NER, PII anonymization, chunking, and embedding models, and are Python\-extensible\.
- Multi\-agent workflows with built\-in CrewAI and LangChain support, shared memory across pipeline runs, and nodes callable as tools\.
- TypeScript, Python, and MCP SDKs integrate pipelines into applications or expose them as callable tools for AI assistants\.
- Deployment paths include Docker, local or on\-premises operation, and managed RocketRide Cloud\.

## Use Cases

- Build RAG pipelines that retrieve relevant documents and ask an LLM questions with them in context\.
- Process PDFs and images to extract text, find names and addresses, and detect personal data\.
- Orchestrate multi\-agent workflows where agents call tools and nodes repeatedly until a task is complete\.
- Call RocketRide pipelines from Python or TypeScript applications through the SDK\.

## Getting Started

- Install the RocketRide extension from your IDE marketplace and open it\.
- Deploy a server by choosing Local (recommended) to pull the server into the IDE, or On\-Premises to run on your own hardware\.
- Open examples/document\-processor\.pipe, start it from the source node, and send input through the pipeline\.
- Install the rocketride SDK and call the running pipeline from Python or TypeScript; the extension writes connection details into the opened folder's \.env\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Local deployment pulls the server into the IDE without additional setup\.
- On\-premises deployment can run the Docker image or build from source\.
- Docker deployment requires Docker to be installed\.
- RocketRide Cloud is managed hosting with no infrastructure to provision\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- On\-premises deployment supports data residency and air\-gapped operation for teams that need data and model calls to stay on their own infrastructure\.
- Running the SDK outside the folder opened in the IDE makes the client fall back to RocketRide Cloud\.

## Overview

Ruflo is an agent meta\-harness for Claude Code and Codex\. It adds a coordination layer around coding agents, providing specialized agents, swarm coordination, self\-learning memory, federation, and vector RAG integration\. The project is part of the Cognitum One / RuvNet ecosystem\.

## Key Features

- 100\+ specialized agents for coding, testing, security, docs, and architecture\.
- Swarm coordination with hierarchical, mesh, and adaptive topologies and consensus\.
- Self\-learning via SONA neural patterns, ReasoningBank, and trajectory learning\.
- Vector memory with HNSW\-indexed AgentDB and measured performance versus brute force\.
- Federation for agents across machines and organizations to discover, authenticate, and exchange work securely\.
- Plugin marketplace with native Claude Code plugins and npm packages\.

## Use Cases

- Build AI coding teams that plan, remember, test, and improve across sessions\.
- Coordinate autonomous multi\-step workflows and swarms for software development\.
- Give agents persistent memory and RAG context over repositories and project knowledge\.
- Run secure multi\-machine agent collaboration through federation\.

## Getting Started

- In Claude Code, add the marketplace with /plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo, then install ruflo\-core@ruflo, ruflo\-console@ruflo, and ruflo\-mods@ruflo\.
- For Codex or another MCP\-enabled tool, run npx ruflo@latest init wizard in your project terminal\.
- To configure a local stdio MCP server, use command npx and arguments \-y, ruflo@latest, mcp start\.
- Install globally with npm install \-g ruflo@latest, or run npx ruflo@latest init for non\-interactive setup\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Claude Code plugin path requires Claude Code 2\.1\.287 or later\.
- CLI path can run on macOS, Linux, WSL, Git\-Bash, Windows PowerShell, and cmd\.
- For local stdio MCP clients, configure command npx and arguments \-y ruflo@latest mcp start\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Mods run with the user's account permissions and are not sandboxed, so code should be reviewed before installation\.
- Performance data is derived from simulations and prototypes and may not reflect final production hardware\.
- Specifications, figures, and statements on the site are subject to change and are not guaranteed\.

projects.content:
## Overview

rust\-anything is a tool for rewriting an existing application in Rust incrementally while keeping it working\. It records the behavior of the original app, supports porting CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries piece by piece, and checks each Rust port against recorded cases\. The original remains the source of truth until the port passes the gate\.

## Key Features

- Records what the original app does and replays recorded cases against the Rust port\.
- Profiles real workloads to show hot functions, callers and loops worth batching\.
- Generates bridge crates and wrappers so existing callers keep the original API\.
- Provides diff, bench, shadow and gate steps for behavior, performance and rollout checks\.
- Supports whole\-app workflows for CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries with record, replay, front\-door, wire and lift commands\.
- Registers an MCP server and workflow skill with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI\.

## Use Cases

- Port a CLI, server or library from TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby or Java to Rust while preserving the original API\.
- Move a hot loop or slow function to Rust after profiling and verify identical results\.
- Plan and track a whole\-app migration with units, port order, dependencies and decisions\.
- Prove a Rust rewrite against recorded app cases before cutover, including HTTP routes and libraries\.

## Getting Started

- Install with cargo install rust\-anything, then run rust\-anything setup\.
- For JavaScript projects, npm install \-g rust\-anything installs the same binary\.
- Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each GitHub release\.
- setup registers the tool with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI and can be undone with \-\-remove\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A Rust toolchain is needed for cargo install; otherwise use prebuilt binaries or npm install \-g for JavaScript projects\.
- Server workflows use \-\-http and take the port from PORT or \{port\} in the command\.
- Other MCP clients can add rust\-anything mcp as a stdio server by hand\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- PHP and C\# support is explicitly marked as preview\.

- 将 TypeScript/JavaScript、Python、C、Go、Ruby 或 Java 的 CLI、服务器或库移植到 Rust，同时保留原 API。
- 在性能分析后把热点循环或慢函数迁移到 Rust，并验证结果一致。
- 通过单元、移植顺序、依赖项和决策来规划和跟踪整应用迁移。
- 在切换前用记录的应用用例验证 Rust 重写，包括 HTTP 路由和库。

## 快速开始

- 使用 cargo install rust\-anything 安装，然后运行 rust\-anything setup。
- 对于 JavaScript 项目，npm install \-g rust\-anything 会安装同一个二进制文件。
- 每个 GitHub release 附有适用于 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的预构建二进制文件。
- setup 会将工具注册到 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 和 Gemini CLI，并可通过 \-\-remove 撤销。

## 部署与要求

- 通过 cargo install 安装需要 Rust 工具链；否则可使用预构建二进制文件，或对 JavaScript 项目使用 npm install \-g。
- 服务器工作流使用 \-\-http，并从 PORT 或命令中的 \{port\} 获取端口。
- 其他 MCP 客户端可以手动将 rust\-anything mcp 添加为 stdio 服务器。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.taglineZh: 面向 AI 代理的自托管元搜索与页面文本引擎
projects.description: RustXNG is a self-hosted metasearch engine written in Rust and based on SearXNG. It combines results from external search providers and can fetch page text for AI agents through a JSON API or MCP.
projects.descriptionZh: RustXNG 是用 Rust 编写、基于 SearXNG 的自托管元搜索与页面文本获取引擎，可聚合外部搜索提供商结果，并通过 JSON API 或 MCP 为 AI 代理获取页面文本。
projects.content:
## Overview

RustXNG is a self\-hosted metasearch engine written in Rust and based on SearXNG\. It combines results from external search providers and can fetch page text for AI agents through a JSON API or MCP\. It does not maintain a web\-scale search index; selected\-site local indexes and Wikipedia dumps can be added separately\.

## Key Features

- Self\-hosted metasearch engine written in Rust and based on SearXNG\.
- JSON API search endpoint with optional page text and parameters such as language, engines, domain include/exclude, time range, and raw content\.
- Built\-in MCP server exposes search and read\_page tools for AI agents\.
- Provider profiles include standard, clean for local indexes only, and full for additional HTML providers plus billed Exa Search when configured\.
- Optional local index via rustxng\-index and separate Wikipedia dump import\.
- Supports a web interface plus CSV, RSS, and HTML output\.

## Use Cases

- AI agents needing search and page\-text grounding through MCP or a JSON API\.
- Self\-hosted search over selected websites using a local index\.
- Deployments that need a clean profile searching only prebuilt local crawl and Wikipedia\-dump indexes\.
- Automated clients that need structured search results with titles, URLs, snippets, and source metadata\.

## Getting Started

- Install from release binaries or with Cargo using the documented locked command for v0\.30\.0\.
- Start a local server with rustxng \-\-bind 127\.0\.0\.1 \-\-port 29483\.
- Query the JSON API at /search with q, format=json, and max\_results parameters\.
- Start the built\-in MCP server with rustxng mcp\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Rust 1\.88 or newer and a C build toolchain are required for source installation\.
- A Docker image is available; by default the service binds to loopback, and exposing it to another network requires appropriate access controls\.
- PDF text extraction requires Poppler (pdftotext); scanned PDFs require a separate OCR tool\.
- JavaScript\-rendered pages need the optional Firefox renderer, and neither PDF support nor the Firefox renderer is enabled automatically by a standalone release binary\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Standard and Full profiles send queries to enabled external search providers even when RustXNG runs locally; Clean searches local indexes only, though explicit raw page fetching or other network\-backed features can still make outbound requests\.
- Provider permissions are still required, and a private instance does not override provider terms\.
- Returned web text should be treated as untrusted content\.
- Dated experiments are not guaranteed to reflect v0\.30\.0 performance, and general superiority over Exa or Tavily should not be inferred\.
- The code license does not grant permission to collect or redistribute data from external search providers\.

projects.taglineZh: 永不卡顿的快速文件管理器
projects.description: rustyfiles is a fast file manager for Windows and macOS built in Rust. It keeps listing, thumbnails, context menus and file operations off the UI thread so large folders and slow network shares do not freeze the window.
projects.descriptionZh: rustyfiles 是一款为 Windows 和 macOS 打造的文件管理器，用 Rust 编写并在 GPU 上绘制。它将列表、缩略图、右键菜单和文件操作放在 UI 线程之外，因此超大文件夹或缓慢的网络共享不会让窗口卡住。
projects.content:
## Overview

rustyfiles is a file manager for Windows and macOS written from scratch in Rust and drawn on the GPU\. It is designed to replace File Explorer for everyday work by running listing, icons, thumbnails, context menus and file operations off the UI thread, so huge folders and slow network shares do not freeze the window\.

## Key Features

- Tabs and dual panes, with tabs that can be reordered or pulled out into a new window\.
- Archives such as ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar, tar\.zst and ISO open like folders; ZIP, 7z and tar can be edited inside\.
- DirectLook previews video, audio, images, PDFs, code and archive contents with the Space key\.
- File operations use a parallel engine and run off the UI thread; the interface is GPU\-drawn with automatic CPU fallback when the GPU is busy\.
- Ferry sends files and folders directly between paired computers on the same network, encrypted with QUIC and TLS 1\.3 and without a server or account\.
- A name index supports fast search by file name, and quick search finds apps, files, bookmarks and Windows settings\.

## Use Cases

- Replacing File Explorer on Windows for everyday file management, including folders, This PC, the Recycle Bin, Win\+E and other apps' Open and Save dialogs\.
- Browsing and managing very large folders or slow network shares without the window freezing\.
- Opening, extracting and editing archives, and previewing media, documents and code without launching separate apps\.
- Sending files between Windows and macOS devices on the same local network with Ferry\.

## Getting Started

- Windows: download rustyfiles\-win\-Setup\.exe and run it; it installs for your user and requires no administrator rights\.
- If Windows SmartScreen warns, choose More info and then Run anyway\.
- Optionally set rustyfiles as the default file manager in Settings › Advanced; uninstalling puts Explorer back\.
- macOS beta: download rustyfiles\-mac\-arm64\.dmg, open it and drag rustyfiles to Applications\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Windows 11 on x64 or ARM64; portable builds are available\.
- macOS beta requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) on Apple silicon; the macOS build is signed and notarized by Apple\.
- Linux is planned but not currently listed as available\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The macOS build is a beta and is limited to Apple silicon running macOS 26 (Tahoe)\.
- The Windows installer is not code\-signed yet, so Windows may show a SmartScreen warning\.
- Ferry is off until enabled, and Windows Firewall may need to allow it for private networks\.

projects.name: RuView
projects.tagline: WiFi sensing for pose, vitals, and presence
projects.taglineZh: 用 WiFi 感知姿态、生命体征与在场状态
projects.description: RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, contactless vital-sign monitoring, and presence detection using radio signals alone — no cameras, wearables, or cloud calls required.
projects.descriptionZh: RuView 将普通 WiFi 信号转化为实时空间智能，可检测房间占用、17 点身体姿态、呼吸与心率，并进行多人跟踪，全程不使用摄像头、可穿戴设备，也不依赖云端调用。
projects.content:
## Overview

RuView is a WiFi sensing system that turns ordinary WiFi channel state information into real\-time spatial intelligence: room occupancy, 17\-point body pose, breathing and heart rate, and multi\-person tracking, all without cameras, microphones, or wearables\. It runs on the Cognitum stack with a Rust\-based sensing pipeline and Ed25519\-signed WASM edge modules, and can fuse its radio view with radar, lidar, depth cameras, thermal, acoustic, and BLE/UWB feeds into a single point cloud\. The project is open source under the MIT license and is also delivered through Cognitum hardware tiers, from a low\-cost ESP32\-S3 node to a Seed and a v0 Appliance\.

## Key Features

- 17\-point COCO body pose reconstructed from WiFi CSI, reported at 92\.9% PCK@20 in upstream benchmarks
- Contactless vital signs, covering breathing at 6\-30 BPM and heart rate at 40\-120 BPM without a wearable
- Multi\-person tracking of 3\-5 or more people per access point, with persistent identity, pose, and vitals
- Through\-wall sensing using Fresnel zones and multipath, including detection through 30 cm of concrete
- More than 60 signed WASM edge modules, each 5\-30 KB, covering health, safety, building automation, analytics, and interaction
- Fusion runtime that merges WiFi CSI with radar, lidar, depth, thermal, acoustic, satellite, and BLE/UWB/Zigbee feeds

## Use Cases

- Elderly care and sleep monitoring, including fall detection and contactless breathing and heart rate during sleep
- Retail and hospitality analytics such as queue length, dwell heatmaps, table turnover, and occupancy counts without cameras
- Smart building automation where room\-level occupancy drives HVAC setpoints and lighting
- Search and rescue, where the WiFi\-Mat kit detects vital signs through concrete and provides 3D survivor localization

## Getting Started

- Pull and run the Docker image ruvnet/wifi\-densepose:latest, publishing port 3000, then check the /health endpoint\.
- Use the CLI with a simulator via ruview \-\-source simulate, or connect an ESP32\-S3 node over a serial port with ruview \-\-source esp32\.
- Query sensing state over REST at endpoints such as /api/v1/sensing/latest, /api/v1/vital\-signs, and /api/v1/pose/current, or subscribe to the WebSocket stream on port 3001\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The Docker container exposes port 3000 for REST requests and port 3001 for the live WebSocket stream\.
- Radio capture requires ESP32\-S3 sensor nodes; the recommended Seed adds persistent local memory and Ed25519 hardware\-key attestation\.
- On\-device inference runs on a Cognitum Seed or a v0 Appliance; the v0 Appliance is a dedicated hub for 3\-6 ESP32\-S3 nodes with a private REST and WebSocket API on the LAN and can run air\-gapped\.
- Cloud aggregation is optional; frames stay in the room unless a cloud destination is explicitly configured\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Health and vitals modules are released as developer previews, and regulated clinical uses require validation beyond the stock repository\.
- Field accuracy depends on the radio\-frequency environment, with per\-room adaptation taking up to about 30 seconds\.
- Published performance figures come from simulations and prototypes and may not match final production hardware\.
- Compliance statements describe architectural posture and design intent; regulated production deployments need customer\-specific validation\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Sand3D is presented as an open\-source 3D library written as code\. The dataset contains 3D objects created with Sand3D, an LLM\-friendly language, and each object is a Python program describing parts, holes, positions, and materials\. The collection also includes mechanical CAD parts whose dimensions are program parameters, plus meshes for Blender, three\.js, and glTF engines\.

## Key Features

- 3D objects written as code in Sand3D, an LLM\-friendly language\.
- One Python program per object, describing part shape, holes, position, and material\.
- Open\-source dataset and library available through Hugging Face and GitHub\.
- Mechanical CAD parts with dimensions expressed as program parameters\.
- Meshes ready for Blender, three\.js, and any glTF engine\.
- Programs written part by part so people can read them and LLMs can learn from them\.

## Use Cases

- Learning 3D modeling through readable, part\-by\-part code examples\.
- Building 3D applications or experiments from parametric object programs\.
- Rendering object meshes in Blender, three\.js, or glTF\-based engines\.
- Using mechanical CAD part programs with adjustable dimensions\.

## Getting Started

- Download the dataset from Hugging Face or access the Sand3D library on GitHub\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Meshes are intended for external 3D tools such as Blender, three\.js, or glTF\-compatible engines\.
- Object programs are Python files that import the sky3d library\.

## Overview

sapper\-v2 is a multi\-agent orchestration harness for autonomous penetration testing, not a single agent\. It lets an AI commander read the board, decide, and dispatch while general, scout, and soldier agents work in parallel in tmux sessions, with a zero\-strategy watchdog keeping the run alive\. Knowledge is written to a layered fact\-intent graph that survives individual agent sessions\. The README says agents and models can be swapped behind each role and that the project was designed for competition scenarios\.

## Key Features

- Commander, general, scout, and soldier division of labor, with a watchdog process for keep\-alive and a commander that does not execute attacks itself\.
- Layered fact\-intent graph with title, summary, and evidence\-document layers for shared memory and context control\.
- Create, Language, and History capabilities: spawn new AI sessions via tmux, type into each other's input boxes, and persist knowledge in the graph\.
- Model tiering: commander and generals on GLM\-5\.3, soldiers and scouts on DeepSeek V4\.1 Flash\.
- Swappable agent CLI and model per role, with role composition defined in the doctrine\.
- Emergent roles and practices reported by the project, including a signalman, performance reviews, and inherited lessons\.

## Use Cases

- Competition CTF scenarios such as the Tencent Intelligent Attack\-Defense Challenge\.
- Authorized penetration\-testing campaigns where a commander coordinates parallel agents against a target\.
- Forking and replacing the competition doctrine for other long\-horizon cooperative work such as office, research, or engineering\.
- Building on the nvwabase foundation for general\-purpose multi\-agent work with Create, Language, and History\.

## Getting Started

- Run bash install\.sh to symlink the sapper CLI; the install is stdlib\-only with zero dependencies\.
- Run sapper setup with a goal and \-\-agents to initialize the board and ready\-to\-work frontier\.
- Run sapper status to view the board and frontier\.
- For the full legion, build with docker build \-f docker/Dockerfile\.commander \-t sapper:latest \. or load the pre\-built image from the v18\-champion release\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The full legion requires Docker; options are building from docker/Dockerfile\.commander or loading the pre\-built image (~1\.2GB, full Kali toolchain plus sapper and offline KB)\.
- Configure model gateways, key pool, and budget through environment variables as documented in docker/ENV\.md\.
- The sapper CLI install is stdlib\-only with zero dependencies\.
- tmux is used to run AI sessions in panes\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Use is restricted to authorized security testing\.
- The project is explicitly designed for competition scenarios\.
- The README offers forking the project as an option for using the mechanism outside its competition design\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Scientific Agent Skills is an open library of scientific procedures for AI agents, created by K\-Dense\. The current repository lists 177 skills; the associated paper describes 163 skills across 16 areas of practice\. Each skill is a directory built around a versioned, human\-readable SKILL\.md instruction file, often with reference material and runnable scripts\. The collection follows the open Agent Skills standard and is also packaged as an Agent Plugins package\.

## Key Features

- 177 scientific and research skills spanning biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, engineering, Earth science, data analysis, and scientific communication\.
- Each skill has a SKILL\.md with purpose, workflow, and version metadata, plus optional code examples, reference documentation, executable helpers, or templates\.
- Documents 100\+ scientific and financial databases, including a Database Lookup skill covering 80 sources such as PubChem, ChEMBL, UniProt, COSMIC, ClinicalTrials\.gov, FRED, and USPTO\.
- Provides 70\+ optimized Python package skills with version\-aware workflows for packages such as RDKit, Scanpy, scikit\-learn, pydicom, QuTiP, GeoPandas, pymatgen, and Qiskit\.
- Follows the Agent Skills standard and works with hosts such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity; also available as an Agent Plugins package\.
- Includes skills for scientific integration platforms such as Benchling, DNAnexus, LatchBio, OMERO, Protocols\.io, Open Notebook, Ginkgo Cloud Lab, LabArchives, and Opentrons\.

## Use Cases

- Guiding AI agents through field\-accepted analysis procedures, validation checks, and provenance requirements in scientific workflows\.
- Working with specialized scientific libraries, databases, and tools across genomics, cheminformatics, medical imaging, and other research domains\.
- Supporting research tasks such as literature review, evidence\-traceable scientific writing, grant writing, and confidential peer review assistance\.
- Packaging reusable scientific skills for compatible agent hosts through the Agent Skills and Agent Plugins standards\.

## Getting Started

- Install with the standards\-based installer by running npx skills add K\-Dense\-AI/scientific\-agent\-skills for supported hosts\.
- With GitHub CLI v2\.90\.0 or later, run gh skill install K\-Dense\-AI/scientific\-agent\-skills; optionally target a host with \-\-agent cursor, \-\-agent claude\-code, \-\-agent codex, or \-\-agent gemini\.
- Browse the illustrated skill guides, skill categories, or complete catalog to choose skills relevant to your work\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The npx installer is described for supported Agent Skills hosts including current versions of Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Codex, Gemini CLI, Google Antigravity, and Cursor\.
- GitHub CLI installation requires GitHub CLI v2\.90\.0 or later\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The associated paper reports no task\-level evaluation and no host selection rate, so it does not provide task\-level performance evidence\.
- The paper warns that 29 of 46 documented workflows would exceed the token window if every reference file were loaded\.
- Each skill records compatibility requirements and validation scope, and the source advises checking those details before reusing an older workflow because test coverage differs\.
