projects.descriptionZh: Scrapling 是一个 Python 网页抓取框架，支持快速 HTTP 请求、隐蔽浏览器、强大解析与并发爬取，可从单次请求扩展到全站抓取。
projects.content:
## Overview

Scrapling is a Python web scraping framework that combines fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling in one library\. It supports static pages, JavaScript rendering, website interaction, API capture, reusable sessions, proxy rotation, retries, pause/resume, and built\-in data exports\. It can be used from Python, the terminal, or an AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill\.

## Key Features

- Spiders provide a Scrapy\-like API with concurrent crawling, multi\-session support, pause and resume, streaming, blocked\-request detection, AutoThrottle, and optional Robots\.txt compliance\.
- Fetchers support fast HTTP requests, stealthy browser automation, JavaScript rendering, persistent sessions, proxy rotation, domain and ad blocking, and background API capture\.
- Parsing supports CSS and XPath selectors, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar\-element matching, and clean Markdown output\.
- Built\-in exporters produce JSON, JSONL, CSV, and XML results, with ready\-made spider templates for common crawling patterns\.
- AI features include an MCP server for agents, an Agent Skill, and RAG\-ready Markdown generation\.
- Developer tooling includes an interactive shell, CLI usage, auto selector generation, type hints, and a Docker image\.

## Use Cases

- Scraping static pages or rendering JavaScript to extract structured data from websites\.
- Building concurrent crawlers with sessions, proxy rotation, retries, pause and resume, and data exports\.
- Capturing API responses behind web pages for data extraction\.
- Enabling AI agents to browse and extract data through the MCP server or preparing web content as Markdown for RAG systems\.

## Getting Started

- Scrapling requires Python 3\.10 or higher\.
- Install the base package with pip install scrapling\.
- For fetchers or spiders, install optional dependencies with pip install "scrapling\[fetchers\]" and then run scrapling install\.
- Additional extras include scrapling\[ai\], scrapling\[rag\], scrapling\[shell\], and scrapling\[all\]\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10 or higher is required\.
- The base installation includes the parser engine only; fetchers and spiders require optional dependencies\.
- Browser fetchers require running scrapling install to download browsers and system and fingerprint dependencies; HTTP requests do not need a browser installation\.
- A Docker image is available as pyd4vinci/scrapling and ghcr\.io/d4vinci/scrapling:latest with all extras and browsers\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: BSD\-3\-Clause\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The base pip package includes only the parser engine and its dependencies; fetchers and spiders require installing optional dependencies first\.
- Browser\-based fetchers require the scrapling install step, while HTTP requests do not require a browser installation\.

## Overview

Screenshot to Code is an open\-source project and hosted product that uses AI to turn screenshots, mockups, Figma designs, and screen recordings into clean, functional code\. It supports multiple frontend stacks and lets users run locally or use the hosted app\.

## Key Features

- Convert screenshots, mockups, Figma designs, and screen recordings into clean, functional code using AI\.
- Supported stacks: HTML \+ Tailwind, HTML \+ CSS, React \+ Tailwind, Vue \+ Tailwind, Bootstrap, and Ionic \+ Tailwind\.
- Default AI models include Gemini 3 Flash Preview, Gemini 3\.1 Pro Preview, GPT\-5\.5, GPT\-5\.4 Mini, Claude Opus 4\.6, Claude Opus 4\.8, and z\-image\-turbo via Replicate\.
- Supports turning a screen recording of a website in action into a functional prototype\.
- With multiple provider keys, the app can compare models and automatically pick a stronger mix of models per variant\.
- Optional screenshot preview lets the agent render generated pages in a headless browser and visually check its work\.

## Use Cases

- Converting a screenshot into clean HTML, Tailwind, React, Vue, or other supported code\.
- Turning Figma designs or mockups into functional frontend code\.
- Creating a functional prototype from a screen recording of a website in action\.
- Comparing multiple AI model providers per generation when multiple API keys are configured\.

## Getting Started

- Use the hosted app for the fastest way to try Screenshot to Code with no local setup\.
- Run locally by setting up the React/Vite frontend and FastAPI backend; local operation requires API keys\.
- Backend setup uses Poetry: install dependencies, configure \.env with model provider keys, install Chromium through Playwright, activate the Poetry environment, and run uvicorn main:app \-\-reload \-\-port 7001\.
- Frontend setup uses pnpm: run pnpm install and pnpm dev\.
- Docker setup: from the root directory, create \.env with OPENAI\_API\_KEY and run docker\-compose up \-d \-\-build\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Running locally requires API keys and a backend/frontend setup\. The app has a React/Vite frontend and a FastAPI backend\.
- You need at least one model provider key among OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini; Gemini and Replicate are strongly recommended for the best quality\.
- Replicate must be configured in backend/\.env as REPLICATE\_API\_KEY; without it, edit\_images and remove\_backgrounds are unavailable\.
- Optional screenshot preview requires Chromium installed via Playwright or automatically in the Docker image; if Chromium is missing, the app skips the tool\.
- Docker deployment requires Docker installed and a \.env file with OPENAI\_API\_KEY; docker\-compose up \-d \-\-build starts the app\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Operational caution: Optional screenshot preview depends on Chromium; if Chromium is missing, the app skips the tool\.
- Operational caution: Running with Ollama open\-source models is not recommended due to poor\-quality results\.
- Operational caution: The Docker setup cannot be used for development because file changes won't trigger a rebuild\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Search is a web browser for macOS built by Office Commun\. The interface is a row of tabs, either down the left or across the top, and the page\. It has no toolbar, start page, suggestion sidebar, or account; users type an address or search terms into one field to reach the page\. It runs on WebKit and is about 14 MB\.

## Key Features

- A minimal interface consisting of tabs and the page, with no toolbar, start page, suggestion sidebar, or account\.
- A single field for addresses and searches; it completes from local history and does not send typed text until Return is pressed\.
- WebKit\-based design keeps the app at about 14 MB and avoids bundling a second browser engine\.
- Tabs can be pinned, restored from the last session without immediate cost, and listed by name with Command\-K\.
- Built\-in ad blocking stops third\-party trackers and ad networks at the network level before pages render\.
- Hide elements permanently per site with Shift\-Command\-H; hidden items remain hidden on later visits before the page draws\.

## Use Cases

- Everyday Mac browsing where the page, not browser chrome, should be the focus\.
- Users who want local password handling and no account or cloud service\.
- Reading long articles with reading mode and keeping video visible in a floating window\.
- Comparing two pages side by side with Split View\.

## Getting Started

- Check that the Mac runs macOS 14 or later\.
- Download Search or install it with Homebrew using: brew install \-\-cask driceroland/tap/search\.
- Open Search, type an address or search terms into the single field, and press Return\.
- Use Settings to configure tabs, passwords, extensions, themes, and other options\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 14 or later\.
- About 14 MB on disk\.
- Uses WebKit, the engine included with macOS\.
- Chrome extension support requires macOS 15\.4 or later\.
- Building from source requires macOS 14 or later and the Xcode 16 / Swift 6 toolchain\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Search requires macOS 14 or later\.
- Chrome extension support requires macOS 15\.4 or later\.
- A self\-built copy is not notarized and needs a right\-click Open or a Privacy & Security allowance on first launch\.
- Keeping a selected site awake can increase memory use\.
- Search says it sends no telemetry, analytics, or crash reports\.

projects.content:
## Overview

SeeCode is an Agent Skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and other Agent Skills hosts\. It converts a short JSON spec into editorial\-quality diagrams that can be explored in a self\-contained HTML file or exported for documents, presentations and social media\.

## Key Features

- Turns a short JSON spec into animated, explorable diagrams for Claude and other coding agents\.
- Supports 45 diagram types plus 15 variants, each with its own animation and an option to be fully static\.
- Interactive HTML diagrams include hover trace, click focus, route playback, lenses, step\-through presentation, search, pan and zoom, an overview map and shareable view links\.
- Exports diagrams as interactive HTML, SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF and MP4; the in\-page Export menu works in the browser without installing extra tools\.
- Redraws existing diagrams and data from Mermaid, Graphviz, PlantUML, D2, draw\.io, Excalidraw, Structurizr, BPMN, SQL, Prisma, DBML, OpenAPI, CSV, TSV and JSON\.
- The agent writes 30 to 150 lines of JSON instead of SVG, while SeeCode renderers handle layout, edge routing, label placement, typography, accessibility and motion\.

## Use Cases

- Explain software architecture, deployment, dependencies, data models, flows, sequences, state machines and other technical systems\.
- Produce diagrams for READMEs, docs sites, Notion, Confluence, PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides, Slack, social posts and talks\.
- Import and redraw existing Mermaid, Graphviz, PlantUML, D2, draw\.io, Excalidraw, Structurizr, BPMN, SQL, Prisma, DBML, OpenAPI or data files at a requested level of detail\.
- Draw non\-code explanatory visuals such as leave timelines, monthly spending Sankey diagrams, rental communication sequences or job\-search state diagrams, with labels in any language\.

## Getting Started

- For Claude Code, run /plugin marketplace add Aryanutkarsh/seecode, then /plugin install seecode@seecode\.
- For Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and other Agent Skills hosts, run npx skills add Aryanutkarsh/seecode \-g\.
- Then ask the agent in plain language to use SeeCode to show a flow or system, and continue with requests such as highlighting a path, making it dark or exporting it for slides\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Node 20 or later\.
- The diagram's own Export menu can create PNG, JPEG, SVG, GIF and MP4 in the browser with nothing installed\.
- From the command line, SVG needs only Node; other export formats use Chrome or Edge already installed on the machine\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Running SeeCode requires Node 20 or later\.
- In Claude\.ai or Claude Desktop, the sandbox has no browser, so image and video files must be produced through the diagram's own Export menu\.
- Command\-line exports have external runtime dependencies: SVG requires Node, while other formats require Chrome or Edge\.
- SeeCode should be skipped when a reader would not learn more from the picture than from a good paragraph\.

## Overview

SEO Skills is an open\-source collection of agent skills for SEO, copywriting and product work\. Each skill is one markdown file that can be installed in Cursor, Claude Code or Codex, or pasted into ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Grok\. It includes SEO autopilot, title tags, blog refreshes, backlinks, customer journeys, video transcripts and copywriting\.

## Key Features

- Open\-source agent skills for SEO, copywriting and product work, with each skill as one markdown file\.
- Each skill is a folder with a SKILL\.md that follows the Agent Skills spec\.
- SEO skills include seo\-autopilot, blitz\-seo, seo\-title\-optimization, blog\-refresher and linkdr\.
- Content, marketing and copywriting skills include intro, scribiz, customer\-journey, diff\-marketing, blitz\-copy and understand\-customers\.
- Code and product skills include eval and extension\-store\-assets\.
- Skills can be installed in Cursor, Claude Code or Codex, or pasted into ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Grok\.

## Use Cases

- Run daily SEO checks, fix title tags, refresh posts that slipped, buy backlinks, map search intent, and write the copy that ranks\.
- Turn videos or audio into transcripts, SRT or VTT subtitles, summaries, chapters, blog posts, show notes or social posts with Scribiz\.
- Generate customer\-focused marketing content from recent git changes, commits, merged pull requests and shipped features\.
- Create browser extension branding, Chrome Web Store assets, app icon concepts, store descriptions, or AI prompt evaluation benchmarks\.

## Getting Started

- Install one skill with npx skills add Illyism/seo\-skills \-\-skill seo\-autopilot\.
- Install all skills with npx skills add Illyism/seo\-skills\.
- List available skills with npx skills add Illyism/seo\-skills \-\-list\.

## Before You Adopt

projects.taglineZh: 通过 MCP 为编码代理提供 IDE 级语义代码工具
projects.description: Serena is an MCP toolkit that gives coding agents IDE-like semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging tools operating at symbol level and using relational structure.
projects.descriptionZh: Serena 是一个 MCP 工具包，为编码代理提供类似 IDE 的语义代码检索、编辑、重构与调试能力，在符号层面运行并利用关系结构，帮助代理在大型复杂代码库中更高效、更可靠地工作。
projects.content:
## Overview

Serena is a model context protocol toolkit that provides coding agents with essential semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging capabilities similar to an IDE\. It operates at the symbol level and exploits relational structure, integrating with clients and LLMs via MCP\. Its agent\-first tool design uses high\-level abstractions rather than line numbers or primitive search patterns, aiming to make agents faster, more efficient and more reliable in larger and complex codebases\.

## Key Features

- Semantic retrieval tools let agents explore codebases at the symbol level, including symbol search, file outlines, referencing symbols, declarations and implementations where supported by the backend\.
- Symbolic editing tools support replacing symbol bodies, inserting before or after symbols, and safe deletion with less error\-prone and token\-efficient operations than typical alternatives\.
- Refactoring tools support symbol renames with the language server backend, while the JetBrains plugin adds move, inline and propagate\-deletion capabilities\.
- Interactive debugging is exclusive to the JetBrains plugin and lets an agent set breakpoints, inspect variables, evaluate expressions and control execution flow through a persistent REPL\-style interface\.
- A memory system supports long\-lived agent workflows and sharing knowledge across sessions, users and projects; it can be disabled if preferred\.
- A multi\-layered YAML configuration system allows active tools, tool descriptions, prompts, language backend details and other aspects to be configured per case\.

## Use Cases

- Equip coding agents with IDE\-like navigation and editing in large, complex codebases\.
- Perform cross\-file renames, moves and reference lookups more efficiently than step\-by\-step text operations\.
- Support long\-lived agent workflows that need shared project memory across sessions or users\.
- Enable agent\-driven debugging through the JetBrains plugin's persistent REPL\-style interface\.

## Getting Started

- Install uv, then install Serena with uv tool install \-p 3\.13 serena\-agent\.
- Run serena init to initialise Serena and verify the setup; add \-b JetBrains to use the JetBrains backend\.
- Connect your preferred MCP client by configuring a launch command, or start the Serena MCP server in HTTP mode and provide the client with the URL\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Serena is managed by uv, and installing uv is the only required prerequisite\.
- After installation, the serena command should be available in the shell\.
- When using the language server backend, some additional dependencies may need to be installed to support certain languages\.
- The JetBrains plugin supports languages and frameworks supported by JetBrains IDEs, but Rider and CLion are unsupported\.
- Clients connect to the Serena MCP server either through a launch command or through an HTTP URL\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Serena supplies tools but depends on an LLM or client to orchestrate their use and perform the coding work\.
- Installation should not be performed through MCP or plugin marketplaces because their commands may be outdated\.
- The JetBrains plugin is paid, though a free trial is available\.
- Language server usage may require installing additional dependencies for certain languages\.

projects.descriptionZh: Serie 是一款用 Rust 编写的终端界面工具，通过终端图像协议将 Git 提交图渲染为图像，让浏览仓库历史比 ASCII 提交图更清晰易读。
projects.content:
## Overview

Serie is a terminal UI application for browsing Git repositories, built around rendering the commit graph richly rather than approximating it with ASCII characters\. It uses the terminal emulator's image display protocol to draw a commit graph like git log \-\-graph \-\-all\. The project is written in Rust and built with Ratatui, and its scope is deliberately commit\-graph\-centric rather than a full\-featured Git client or a complex multi\-pane TUI\.

## Key Features

- Renders commit graphs as images inside supported terminal emulators using their image display protocols\.
- Offers selectable graph edge styles: rounded, angular, or curved\.
- Supports image protocol selection among auto, iterm, kitty, and kitty\-unicode\.
- Can keep a primary branch pinned to the leftmost column\.
- Lets users limit rendered commits with max count and choose chrono or topo commit ordering\.
- Supports overridable keybindings and config loading from SERIE\_CONFIG\_FILE or the XDG config path with defaults\.

## Use Cases

- Browsing branchy Git history where ASCII commit graphs are difficult to parse\.
- Keeping a main or develop branch visible in a predictable leftmost column while reviewing commits\.
- Opening a repository from another directory with the \-C option\.
- Adjusting graph appearance and terminal protocol settings for a preferred terminal setup\.

## Getting Started

- Install with Cargo using cargo install \-\-locked serie\.
- Run serie in the directory containing your Git repository\.
- Open a repository from another directory with serie \-C \<path\>\.
- Press ? inside the application to see keybindings\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Git is required\.
- A supported terminal emulator is required, using either the Inline Images Protocol (iTerm2) or the kitty terminal graphics protocol\.
- tmux is supported only when using the kitty Unicode placeholder protocol\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

## 核心功能

- 在支持的终端模拟器中通过图像显示协议将提交图渲染为图像；提供 rounded、angular、curved 三种图边样式；图像协议可选 auto、iterm、kitty、kitty\-unicode；可将主分支固定在最左列；可用最大提交数限制渲染数量，并选择 chrono 或 topo 提交排序；支持覆盖键位，并从 SERIE\_CONFIG\_FILE 或 XDG 配置路径加载配置，未设置时使用默认值。

projects.content:
## Overview

SGLang is a high\-performance serving framework for large language and multimodal models\. It provides production\-grade inference for large\-scale deployments, from a single GPU to distributed clusters, and supports a wide range of open models and hardware platforms\.

## Key Features

- Production\-grade inference built for large\-scale deployments with reliable, low\-latency, high\-throughput serving from a single GPU to distributed clusters\.
- Model and hardware flexibility across a wide range of open models, including LLMs and diffusion models, and diverse hardware platforms\.
- Advanced optimizations including disaggregated prefill/decode, speculative decoding, parallelisms, a zero\-overhead scheduler, and optimized GPU kernels\.
- OpenAI\-compatible API endpoints for querying served models\.
- Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, CPU servers, TPU, Ascend NPUs, and XPU\.

## Use Cases

- Large\-scale production inference for large language and multimodal models\.
- Serving open models across single\-GPU and distributed\-cluster deployments\.
- Running diffusion models and other supported open models on diverse hardware\.
- Agentic and RL\-rollout workloads that can use session\-aware caching\.

## Getting Started

- Install via pip or Docker\.
- Launch the server with a single command pointing to your model\.
- Query the API using standard OpenAI\-compatible endpoints\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supported hardware includes NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, CPU servers, TPU, Ascend NPUs, and XPU\.
- Installation options include Python via uv, Python, or Docker\.
- The installer offers Stable or Nightly builds, CUDA, ROCm, XPU, or CPU platforms, and CUDA 12\.9 or CUDA 13\.0 versions\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Beam search works alongside regular requests but does not yet support mixing with speculative decoding, disaggregation, or DP\.
- Prefill context parallelism v1 has been removed, and prefill CP is rejected on HIP, NPU, and MUSA until those platforms are ported\.
- Spec V1 is deprecated, with EAGLE and MTP now running on the unified V2 worker\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Shannon is an open\-source whitebox AI pentester for web applications and APIs from Keygraph\. It analyzes source code, identifies attack vectors, and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities\. The Keygraph platform extends this with continuous agentic pentesting on every build, covering whitebox and blackbox testing, business logic testing, code analysis, and verified remediation workflows\.

## Key Features

- Agentic whitebox and blackbox pentesting that reads code or attacks the app from the outside and reports findings with working exploits\.
- Business logic testing to prove where application logic breaks\.
- Code analysis including agentic SAST, SCA limited to reachable CVEs, and secrets scanning verified across history\.
- Code remediation that generates verified fixes as reviewable pull requests\.
- Reporting and analytics with deduplicated findings, dashboards, and Jira sync\.
- Signed attestation reports for audits\.

## Use Cases

- Continuous penetration testing on every build to close the gap between scheduled pentests\.
- Validating application security findings by requiring a working exploit before reporting\.
- Reviewing source code and dependencies for reachable vulnerabilities, leaked secrets, and business logic flaws\.
- Managing remediation and audit reporting through pull requests, dashboards, and signed reports\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-hosted and BYOK deployments are available\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Code remediation auto\-patching is not yet available for GitLab repositories\.

projects.content:
## Overview

SignuDoc is an open\-source document signature platform for an organization’s own Vercel account\. Users upload a PDF, place fields, add signers, and send signing links\. Signers can sign without an account by typing or drawing a signature on any device\. Completed documents include a sealed PDF and audit certificate, and copies can be checked on the install’s public Verify page\. SignuDoc is not affiliated with DocuSign\.

## Key Features

- Place signature, initials, date, name, text, number, checkbox, dropdown, and radio button fields, each required or optional and tied to a signer\.
- Support signing order, simultaneous signing, and copy\-only recipients\.
- Let signers open an email link and sign without an account on a phone, tablet, or computer; earlier signer fields stay visible and locked\.
- Provide a PAdES\-sealed PDF, a hash\-chained audit trail, and a public Verify page for checking copies\.
- Save envelopes as reusable templates that keep the document, fields, and signing order with roles instead of names\.
- Configure signing deadlines from 3 to 90 days, automatic reminders, branding, administrator accounts, retention rules, and signer data export or erasure tools\.

## Use Cases

- Small teams and consultancies sending contracts, NDAs, or consulting agreements on a semi\-regular basis\.
- Organizations that want agreements and related data hosted in their own Vercel, Neon, and Blob accounts and chosen region\.
- Teams that send recurring documents and want reusable templates with role\-based signing order\.
- Teams that need access codes or emailed one\-time codes to check signer identity\.

## Getting Started

- Click Deploy to Vercel and sign in to Vercel so SignuDoc is copied into your GitHub account and built from that copy\.
- Add Resend for email, a Neon Postgres database, and a private Vercel Blob store on free plans\.
- Click Deploy; the build creates the database tables\.
- Open the new site and name your organization\.
- Upload a PDF, place fields, add signers, and send signing links\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A Vercel account for hosting the application\.
- A Resend account or resource for outgoing email\.
- A Neon Postgres database for application data\.
- A private Vercel Blob store for PDFs\.
- Optional custom domain and branding configuration\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- SignuDoc depends on Vercel Blob, Neon Postgres, and Resend for storage, database, and email\.
- Free\-plan limits can cause files to become unreadable, email not to send, or the database to pause when allowances are exceeded\.
- Vercel’s free plan is restricted to personal, non\-commercial use; a company may need Vercel Pro\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Android Skills is a dedicated repository of AI\-optimized, modular instructions and resources for agents working on Android development\. It uses open\-standard agent skill markdown files, SKILL\.md, to provide task specifications and ground LLMs in specialized domains and workflows, with a focus on use cases where evaluations show LLMs underperform\.

## Key Features

- AI\-optimized, modular instructions and resources for Android development\.
- Open\-standard agent skill markdown files (SKILL\.md) that specify tasks and ground LLMs in specialized workflows\.
- Focus on Android use cases and workflows where evaluations show LLMs underperform\.
- Install individual skills, all skills, or selected agents through Android CLI\.
- Update all skills or specific skills with Android CLI\.
- Supports installation as an agent plugin for Claude Code and Codex\.

## Use Cases

- Help agents execute Android development patterns that follow official best practices\.
- Ground LLMs in specialized Android domains and workflows\.
- Install skills into a project directory or detected agent directories\.
- Prompt an agent to complete a relevant task so it automatically activates an installed skill\.

## Getting Started

- Install a specific skill into the current directory with Android CLI: android skills add r8\-analyzer \-\-project=\.
- Install all Android skills to directories for all detected agents: android skills add \-\-all\.
- Update all skills: android skills update \-\-all\.
- Update a specific skill: android skills update wear\-compose\-m3\.
- Install as a Claude Code plugin: /plugin install android\-skills \-\-marketplace android/skills\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Android CLI is used to install and update skills\.
- If no agent directories exist and no agents are specified, skills install for Gemini and Antigravity at ~/\.gemini/antigravity/skills\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- AI\-generated results can be incorrect, so users should verify outputs\.
- Installation and updates depend on Android CLI\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Skills is a collection of small, composable instructions for coding agents, designed to encode senior\-engineering habits\. The skills cover an idea\-to\-ship flow across alignment, specs, tickets, implementation, review, debugging, architecture improvement, and productivity workflows, and they work with agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Amp\.

## Key Features

- A set of 27 MIT\-licensed skills organized into getting started, main flow, shaping, engineering, productivity, and reference groups\.
- Slash\-command workflows for alignment, specs, tickets, implementation, code review, retro, debugging, triage, and architecture improvement\.
- Composable skills whose outputs feed the next step in the workflow\.
- Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Amp, and other coding agents\.
- The installer writes editable skill files into your project, while Claude Code can alternatively use a managed, read\-only plugin\.

## Use Cases

- Aligning with a coding agent before starting a change by running a grilling session\.
- Turning an agreed conversation into a written spec and splitting it into agent\-sized tickets\.
- Implementing a spec test\-first and reviewing the resulting diff against standards\.
- Surveying a codebase for refactoring opportunities or diagnosing hard bugs from a failing reproduction\.

## Getting Started

- Install the skills with npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills, selecting the skills and agents you use\.
- For Claude Code, install the complete set as a managed, read\-only plugin with claude plugins install mattpocock\-skills\.
- Run /setup\-matt\-pocock\-skills once per repo to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and where docs are saved\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The installer route copies editable skill files into your project, so updates are manual\.
- Choose either the plugin or the installer per agent because installing both duplicates every skill\.
- The architecture\-improvement skill is a survey that identifies candidates but does not refactor a legacy codebase for you\.

## 核心功能

- 包含 27 项 MIT 许可技能，分为入门、主流程、塑造、工程、生产力和参考等组；提供斜杠命令工作流，覆盖对齐、规格、工单、实现、代码审查、回顾、调试、分诊和架构改进；技能可组合，前一步的输出可作为下一步的输入；支持 Claude Code、Cursor、Codex、Copilot、Amp 等编码代理；安装器会把可编辑的技能文件写入项目，Claude Code 也可改用托管的只读插件。

projects.content:
## Overview

SkillSpector is a security scanner for AI agent skills\. It helps answer whether a skill is safe to install by running fast static checks by default and optionally adding LLM semantic analysis\. It accepts Git repositories, URLs, zip files, directories, and single files, and is part of the NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-format input: scans Git repositories, URLs, zip files, directories, and single files\.
- Covers prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply\-chain issues, excessive agency, output handling, system prompt leakage, memory poisoning, tool misuse, rogue\-agent behavior, trigger abuse, dangerous code patterns, taint tracking, YARA signatures, and MCP
- Two\-stage analysis: fast static checks by default plus optional LLM semantic evaluation of claimed versus actual behavior\.
- Live vulnerability lookups through OSV\.dev with automatic offline fallback\.
- Outputs terminal, JSON, Markdown, and SARIF reports\.
- Risk scoring from 0 to 100 with severity labels and recommendations, plus baseline suppression of known findings\.

## Use Cases

- Reviewing a third\-party agent skill before installing it\.
- Scanning local directories, single SKILL\.md files, Git repositories, or zip files during development\.
- Gating releases or CI pipelines with SARIF and JSON reports\.
- Batch auditing directories of skills or comparing MCP Registry snapshots\.

## Getting Started

- Install the CLI with uv, or clone the repository and run make install from an activated virtual environment; Docker is also available\.
- Run skillspector scan against a local skill directory, a SKILL\.md file, a Git repository, or a zip file\.
- Static checks run by default; configure an OpenAI\-compatible LLM provider to add semantic analysis\.
- Use the format option to produce terminal, JSON, Markdown, or SARIF output\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.12\+ and a virtual environment for source or CLI installation\.
- Docker is optional and requires no local Python install; the image is based on Python 3\.12\-slim\-bookworm\.
- Semantic analysis requires an LLM provider configuration and credentials; static analysis does not\.
- Live OSV\.dev lookups require network access, with an offline fallback available\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Semantic review depends on an external LLM provider and its credentials\.
- Live dependency vulnerability data depends on OSV\.dev, though an offline fallback exists\.
- Installing the project may download third\-party open source software, so review those licenses\.
- The Codex CLI provider is disabled because its sandbox can read host files\.
- The batch scanner defaults to DeepSeek, and DeepSeek\-Chat is expected to sunset\.

projects.content:
## Overview

SoduWork is an open\-source, AI\-native collaboration platform for enterprises\. It connects people, AI agents, models, and business systems around shared requests, with acceptance criteria, independent AI review, human approval, and reusable plugins\. The platform supports multiple agent harnesses, cloud or local models, and private deployment so teams can keep decisions, results, and proven methods within their own environment\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-harness execution connects harnesses such as Pi, OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Codex, Claude Code, and Google Harness through one adapter interface, allowing users to switch mid\-conversation while keeping history and the working folder\.
- Separate implementation and review agents let one harness do the work and another review it against acceptance criteria, with a person making the final approval decision\.
- Request\-centered collaboration links requirements, execution, review, approvals, result versions, and evidence to the same task in a shared issue pool\.
- Reusable plugins and skills turn proven chats and business methods into shared capabilities that can be reviewed, granted to teams or people, revoked, and reused across harnesses\.
- Enterprise governance includes plugin review and permissions, roles, usage, cost, audit logs, and self\-hosted deployment options\.
- Model and runtime choice lets teams configure cloud models, local models, and execution resources for each stage, including long tasks sent to their own cloud runner\.

## Use Cases

- Engineering teams can move from requirements to release\-ready software with code changes, test reports, cross\-review, and release records tied to the same request\.
- Business and operations teams can draft documents, create presentations, analyze spreadsheets and data, and turn meetings into minutes, decisions, and action items\.
- Research and analysis teams can plan research, collect sources, cross\-check evidence, and produce reports with citations and traceable sources\.
- Teams can capture individual know\-how as reviewed plugins so new members can follow proven methods and contribute improvements with appropriate permissions\.

## Getting Started

- Run from source with Python 3\.12\+, Node\.js 22\.19\+, and Git installed\.
- From the cloned repository, start the desktop app with sh start\.sh \-\-desktop on macOS or Linux, or \.\\start\.cmd \-\-desktop in Windows PowerShell\.
- On first run, set the admin account password and add a model provider under Model catalog in the admin console\.
- For evaluation, download the desktop client from Releases, enter the demo Hub address on the sign\-in screen, then sign up and sign in\.
- For Docker\-based team deployment, run python3 ops/self\-host/deploy\.py up and then python3 ops/self\-host/deploy\.py credentials to show the initial admin password\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Running from source requires Python 3\.12\+, Node\.js 22\.19\+, and Git\.
- The Docker team deployment starts the Hub, admin console, and PostgreSQL on one server\.
- Docker must be installed and running for the Docker deployment path\.
- An HTTPS reverse proxy should be placed in front of the Docker deployment to open it to a team\.
- Private deployment lets organizations configure the environment around model, network, and permission requirements\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- SoduWork is in public beta and should be evaluated before production use\.
- The live demo is intended only for evaluation and should not receive real business or sensitive data\.
- Plugin integrations depend on the APIs and permissions of existing business systems\.
- A successful connection probe does not guarantee successful inference; model balance, permissions, and protocol support still matter\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Solid Glass is a design system for AI applications built around a glass\-inspired material style\. It emphasizes solidity over transparency, using delicate highlights, fine borders, soft shadows, thickness, and restrained color and motion to keep interfaces calm and readable while retaining a tactile, technical feel\. It is built on shadcn/ui and Base UI and works in light and dark modes\.

## Key Features

- A glass\-inspired theme defined in one stylesheet, with colors, three glass thicknesses, one state, and motion\.
- Built on shadcn/ui and Base UI, and designed to work with existing shadcn/ui components without component changes\.
- Includes components for AI application interfaces such as status glyph, composer, tool steps, diff view, ask card, context ring, task notice, and reasoning\.
- Provides blocks, whole screens made from the components, including an agent workspace\.
- Includes a Create page for adjusting thickness, tint, chart color, type, radius, rim, and blur\.
- Supports light and dark modes, with dark described as the material as designed\.

## Use Cases

- Building AI application interfaces with streaming responses, agent tasks, and human decisions\.
- Styling existing shadcn/ui projects with a tactile glass aesthetic\.
- Prototyping agent workspaces and other whole\-screen AI product layouts from provided blocks\.
- Creating variants of the material by tuning thickness, tint, chart color, type, radius, rim, and blur\.

## Getting Started

- Start from a shadcn/ui project using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and Base UI components; initialize with npx shadcn@latest init\.
- Add the Solid Glass stylesheet with npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid\-glass/solid\-glass\.
- Import it after Tailwind and shadcn's stylesheet, and delete the :root and \.dark color variables written by shadcn init because Solid Glass defines the same names\.
- Install Solid Glass components the same way, for example npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid\-glass/status\-glyph\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires a shadcn/ui project with React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and Base UI components\.
- The stylesheet must be imported after Tailwind and shadcn's stylesheet, with shadcn init's :root and \.dark color variables removed\.
- Solid Glass's own components are installed through the shadcn CLI registry\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Adoption requires an existing shadcn/ui project based on React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and Base UI components\.

projects.content:
## Overview

SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) is a sandbox platform for running code in isolated Firecracker microVMs\. Applications use its HTTP API to create Linux environments, execute commands, collect output, and manage sandbox lifecycles\. A template supplies the starting environment, and a sandbox is an instance of that environment with its own VM and writable filesystem\.

## Key Features

- Runs agent, user, and code\-running jobs in isolated Firecracker microVMs\.
- Exposes an HTTP API for creating Linux environments, executing commands, collecting output, and managing sandbox lifecycles\.
- Supports multiple commands in the same sandbox, each with its own VM and writable filesystem\.
- Uses templates to supply starting environments and sandboxes as instances of those environments\.
- Provides asynchronous lifecycle operations through operation IDs that can be polled for completion\.
- Streams command output over a separate data\-plane connection using a session\-scoped attachment token\.

## Use Cases

- Running an agent in a separate execution environment\.
- Providing a user workspace for code execution\.
- Executing code\-running jobs in isolation\.

## Getting Started

- Follow Installation and configuration to deploy SPACE in a local Kind cluster and authenticate\.
- Follow Your first sandbox to run a command and collect its output\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The setup guide covers Kubernetes; the architecture guide also explains how SPACE can run without it\.
- Host prerequisites, local Kind deployment, configuration defaults, authentication, verification, and teardown are covered in the installation documentation\.
- A local deployment uses a Kind cluster and requires authentication\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Some API schema fields are marked incubating and are outside the supported contract\.
- Sandbox lifecycle changes are asynchronous; clients poll an operation ID for completion\.
- Command output uses a separate data\-plane connection and a session\-scoped attachment token\.
- The documented setup path uses Kubernetes\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes\. Its core Spec\-Driven Development flow carries a specification through planning, implementation, and convergence, while optional extensions support bug fixing and idea assessment\.

## Key Features

- Core Spec\-Driven Development process: Specify, Plan, Tasks, Implement, Converge, with each phase producing a Markdown artifact that feeds the next\.
- 38 coding\-agent integrations, including Copilot, Gemini, Codex, Claude, Zed, and Kiro, with a generic option for other tools and single\-command switching\.
- Optional bug\-fixing extension that assesses the cause, applies a scoped fix, and records verification with a verified, partial, or failed verdict\.
- Optional idea\-assessment extension that gathers evidence and produces a go, needs\-clarification, or kill decision\.
- Customization through extensions, presets, workflows, bundles, project\-local overrides, and community or self\-hosted catalogs\.
- Offline and air\-gapped operation with local sources and self\-hosted catalogs on Windows, macOS, and Linux\.

## Use Cases

- Build a feature or application from a specification that is carried through planning, implementation, and convergence\.
- Diagnose and repair broken behavior with an assessed cause, a scoped fix, and recorded verification\.
- Decide whether an idea deserves investment using an evidence\-backed go, clarify, or stop decision\.
- Adopt or create a different process for team standards, organizational governance, or non\-software workflows\.

## Getting Started

- Ensure Python 3\.11\+, uv, and a supported AI coding agent are available\. Install Spec Kit with uv tool install specify\-cli, create a project with specify init my\-project \-\-integration copilot, and launch your coding agent in the project directory\. For bug fixing, run specify

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Python 3\.11\+, uv, and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows\. Spec Kit works offline, behind firewalls, and in enterprise or air\-gapped setups using local sources and self\-hosted catalogs\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Adoption requires Python 3\.11 or newer\.
- A supported AI coding agent is required on Linux, macOS, or Windows\.
- Bug fixing and idea assessment are bundled, opt\-in extensions rather than mandatory core phases\.
- Community catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review source code before installing or running it\.

## 核心功能

- 核心规范驱动开发流程为 Specify、Plan、Tasks、Implement、Converge，每个阶段生成供下一阶段使用的 Markdown 产物；提供 38 个编程代理集成，包括 Copilot、Gemini、Codex、Claude、Zed 和 Kiro，并有通用选项及单命令切换；可选缺陷修复扩展评估原因、实施限定修复并记录验证，结论为 verified、partial 或 failed；可选想法评估扩展收集证据并给出 go、needs\-clarification 或 kill

## 适用场景

- 从规范构建功能或应用，并让规范贯穿规划、实现和收敛；诊断并修复异常行为，包含原因评估、限定修复和验证记录；用有证据支持的 go、clarify 或 stop 决策判断想法是否值得投入；采用或创建其他流程，以满足团队标准、组织治理或非软件工作流。

## 快速开始

- 确保已安装 Python 3\.11\+、uv 和受支持的 AI 编程代理；运行 uv tool install specify\-cli 安装 Spec Kit，运行 specify init my\-project \-\-integration copilot 创建项目，进入项目目录并启动编程代理，然后选择流程。缺陷修复需在项目目录运行 specify extension add bug；想法评估需运行 specify extension add assess。

## 部署与要求

- 需要 Python 3\.11\+、uv 以及 Linux、macOS 或 Windows 上的受支持 AI 编程代理。Spec Kit 可在离线、防火墙后以及企业或气隙环境中运行，使用本地来源和自托管目录。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.name: Splash

projects.taglineZh: 面向 Apple 芯片、围绕模型构建的本地推理引擎
projects.description: Splash is an open-source inference engine for Apple silicon, built around the model for efficiency. It combines DFlash 2 speculative decoding, Metal kernels, and automatic memory planning for local coding agents.
projects.descriptionZh: Splash 是面向 Apple 芯片的开源推理引擎，围绕模型进行专门优化，结合 DFlash 2 投机解码、Metal 内核和自动内存规划，在 Mac 本地运行编码智能体。
projects.content:
## Overview

Splash is Inco AI's open\-source inference engine for Apple silicon, designed around the model rather than a generic model zoo\. It specializes its Metal kernels, draft model, and memory plan for each supported model, combining DFlash 2 speculative decoding, paged KV cache reuse, and batched serving\. It runs coding agents and OpenAI\- or Anthropic\-compatible applications locally on one Mac, with a built\-in chat page\.

## Key Features

- Built around each supported model with specialized Metal kernels, trained DFlash 2 draft models, and automatic memory planning\.
- Uses DFlash 2 speculative decoding as part of the decode path, with draft state carried per request so speculation works with concurrency and cache reuse\.
- Supports paged KV cache and prefix reuse, including GDN state snapshots for hybrid models\.
- Serves OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses, and Completions plus Anthropic Messages, with streaming, tool calls, JSON Schema output, and image and PDF input\.
- Includes a built\-in chat page and can launch coding agents such as OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and Pi\.
- Loads GGUF and MLX checkpoints, converts weights to kernel layouts during loading, and ships precompiled kernels without requiring Xcode or local tuning\.

## Use Cases

- Running coding agents locally on a Mac\.
- Serving OpenAI\- or Anthropic\-compatible applications from a single local endpoint\.
- Using the built\-in chat page for local model interaction after the server reports Ready\.
- Handling concurrent subagent requests that share context, using batching and cache reuse\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Splash desktop app on an Apple M3 or newer Mac running macOS 26\.4 or later, or install the CLI with Homebrew\.
- Run brew install incoai/tap/splash, then splash serve \-\-model unsloth/Qwen3\.8\-27B\-GGUF:UD\-Q4\_K\_M\.
- The first run downloads the model and matching DFlash 2 draft and serves on 127\.0\.0\.1:8000; later starts reuse the downloads\.
- Once the server prints Ready, open 127\.0\.0\.1:8000 for the built\-in chat page, call the API, or attach an agent with splash opencode, splash claude, splash codex, splash hermes, or splash pi\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Apple M3 or newer Mac running macOS 26\.4 or later\.
- Homebrew for command\-line installation\.
- The 4\-bit Qwen3\.8\-27B model needs at least 36 GB of unified memory, with 48 GB or more recommended; 24 GB Macs can run smaller GGUF variants\.
- Leave room on disk for model and draft downloads\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The local server has no authentication by default and listens only on localhost, so LAN access requires additional configuration\.
- Initial setup downloads the model and matching draft, creating an external download and disk\-space dependency\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Strata is an open\-source local inference engine and desktop app for running Qwen3\.8\-Flash\-Next, a 125\-billion\-parameter model, on consumer hardware\. It provides one\-click installation for Windows and Linux, a terminal client, OpenAI\- and Anthropic\-compatible APIs on localhost, optional image input, and chat and monitoring tools while keeping chats and files on the PC\.

## Key Features

- Runs Qwen3\.8\-Flash\-Next, a 125\-billion\-parameter model, on consumer PCs with at least 32 GB of combined RAM and graphics memory\.
- One\-click app installers for Windows and Linux, plus a macOS app and a one\-line terminal installer\.
- OpenAI\-, Anthropic\-, and OpenAI Responses\-compatible APIs on localhost for connecting coding agents and other apps\.
- Optional picture input, with the image reader running on the CPU or GPU depending on available graphics memory\.
- Desktop chat with model, GPU, CPU, and RAM monitoring, a Models page, Settings, web search, and optional multi\-model support\.
- Terminal commands for launching, monitoring, updating, diagnosing, and connecting Strata to tools such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode\.

## Use Cases

- Run a large Qwen model locally on a gaming PC without relying on a cloud API\.
- Connect coding agents and other OpenAI\- or Anthropic\-compatible apps to a local model endpoint\.
- Chat with a model that can read pictures while keeping chats and files on the PC\.
- Monitor local inference speed, GPU, memory, and requests with the desktop app or terminal\.

## Getting Started

- Download the Strata app installer for your system and graphics card from the releases page, then run it; Windows installs per user without administrator rights\.
- On Linux, make the AppImage runnable with chmod \+x and install FUSE 2; on Mac, open the DMG and drag Strata to Applications\.
- Alternatively, run the one\-line install script for Linux or macOS, or the PowerShell installer for Windows, then run strata launch\.
- Follow the guided prompts to choose a model, context size, picture support, and access, then download the engine and model\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- At least 32 GB of RAM and VRAM combined; 64 GB of RAM runs every model size\.
- About 80 GB of free disk; an SSD makes the first start much faster\.
- Windows 10 or 11, Linux, or macOS, plus a current graphics driver\.
- Supported hardware includes NVIDIA RTX 20/30/40/50 series with 12 GB or more, AMD Radeon RX 6800 and newer, Intel Arc, Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or newer, and AMD Ryzen AI Max unified\-memory systems\.
- The model download is about 40\-70 GB and resumes if interrupted\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The Windows installer is not code\-signed, so Windows may show a protection warning\.
- Web search is an explicit exception to local\-only operation because search terms leave the PC\.
- Initial model loading can make the PC slow or unresponsive for one to three minutes\.
- The RX 6000 engine is built but not yet tested on real RX 6000 hardware\.
- Gyro model support on AMD is experimental\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Strix is an open\-source AI penetration testing tool and a full\-stack security platform\. Its autonomous AI agents run targets dynamically, find vulnerabilities, and validate findings with working proofs\-of\-concept\. Strix combines a pentesting toolkit, multi\-agent orchestration, auto\-fix, reporting, and coverage for code, APIs, web apps, infrastructure, and cloud\.

## Key Features

- Autonomous AI penetration testing agents that run targets dynamically, find vulnerabilities, and validate them with actual proofs\-of\-concept\.
- Full pentesting toolkit including reconnaissance, exploitation, validation, HTTP interception proxy, browser exploitation, shell execution, custom exploit runtime, and OSINT\.
- Multi\-agent orchestration with specialized agents for recon, exploitation, and post\-exploitation that share discoveries and chain vulnerabilities\.
- Auto\-fix and reporting with generated patches and compliance\-ready pentest reports\.
- Coverage across code and pull requests, APIs and web apps, and infrastructure and cloud\.
- Developer\-first CLI with actionable findings and remediation guidance\.

## Use Cases

- Application security testing to detect and validate critical vulnerabilities in applications\.
- Rapid penetration testing with compliance reports in hours rather than weeks\.
- Bug bounty automation to generate proofs\-of\-concept for faster reporting\.
- CI/CD integration to block vulnerabilities before they reach production\.

## Getting Started

- Install Strix with the official install script\.
- Set STRIX\_LLM to a supported model provider identifier and set LLM\_API\_KEY to your API key\.
- Run strix \-\-target \./app\-directory to scan a local codebase; \-\-target also accepts a repository or web application URL\.
- The first run automatically pulls the sandbox Docker image, and results are saved to the strix\_runs directory\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Local open\-source use requires Docker to be running\.
- Local runs require an LLM API key from a supported provider such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google\.
- Enterprise deployment can be self\-hosted in a VPC, on\-premise, or air\-gapped environment\.
- Strix Cloud is a managed option that does not require local Docker or an LLM key for terminal scans\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Strix is intended only for authorized testing; the source warns that unauthorized testing is illegal in most jurisdictions\.
- Local Strix runs require Docker to be running\.
- Local runs depend on an external LLM provider through an API key\.
- The enterprise offering states that source code is not stored or used for model training and that model providers operate under zero data retention agreements\.

projects.name: SuperMimic
projects.tagline: Humanoid whole-body control via differentiable world model
projects.taglineZh: 用单一可微世界模型训练人形全身控制
projects.description: SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model. The world model and policy train together; one policy transfers zero-shot to a real Unitree G1. It surpasses SONIC's return in 3 hours on one GPU.
projects.descriptionZh: SuperMimic 用单一可微世界模型训练人形全身动作跟踪器。世界模型与策略共同训练，通过想象 rollout 和解析策略梯度学习，无需对模拟器求导；同一策略可零样本部署到真实 Unitree G1。单块 GPU 训练 3 小时即超过 SONIC 的归一化回报。
projects.content:
## Overview

SuperMimic is a research project for humanoid whole\-body motion tracking that trains one general policy with a differentiable world model\. The world model and policy are trained together, and the learned model is used for imagined rollouts and analytic policy gradients instead of differentiating the simulator\. The project reports one policy running zero\-shot on a physical Unitree G1\.

## Key Features

- Trains a humanoid whole\-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model\.
- Updates the world model every iteration alongside the policy, holding it fixed only inside each policy update\.
- Uses a standard contact simulator, MuJoCo Warp, and does not differentiate the simulator\.
- Runs one general motion tracker policy zero\-shot on a real Unitree G1 with no per\-motion tuning\.
- Includes a browser demo for choosing motions and policies\.
- Reports surpassing SONIC's normalized return in 3 hours on one GPU\.

## Use Cases

- Humanoid whole\-body motion tracking across a large motion library\.
- Training policies in a learned world model to reduce simulator rollouts\.
- Evaluating whole\-body control policies on a physical Unitree G1\.
- Exploring analytic policy gradients through a learned world model\.

## Getting Started

- Install uv\.
- Clone supermimic and mjlab\_research as sibling repositories\.
- Choose a task ID: SuperMimic\-GenCoord\-G1 or SuperMimic\-MaxCoord\-G1\.
- Train a world model and policy with CUDA\_VISIBLE\_DEVICES=\<GPU\_ID\> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train\.py \<TASK\_ID\> \-\-runner\.run\_name \<description\>\.
- Play back a trained model with uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play\.py \<TASK\_ID\> \-\-wandb\-path \<RUN\_PATH\>\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Training commands select a GPU with CUDA\_VISIBLE\_DEVICES\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Setup depends on cloning both supermimic and mjlab\_research as sibling repositories\.
- The SONIC comparison differs in training data and GPU hardware, so the reported speedup is not a controlled like\-for\-like benchmark\.
- Failure counts on benchmark motions measure coverage of training motions rather than generalization\.
- Benchmark evaluation uses deterministic physics without domain randomization or observation noise\.

## 项目简介

SuperMimic 是一个研究项目，面向人形机器人全身动作跟踪，用单一可微世界模型训练一个通用策略。世界模型与策略一起训练，学习后的模型用于想象 rollout 和解析策略梯度，而不是对模拟器求导。项目报告称，同一策略无需逐动作调参即可零样本运行在真实 Unitree G1 上。

## 核心功能

- 以单一可微世界模型训练人形全身动作跟踪器；世界模型在每次迭代中与策略一同更新，仅在每次策略更新内部保持固定；使用标准接触模拟器 MuJoCo Warp，且不对模拟器求导；一个通用动作跟踪策略可零样本运行在真实 Unitree G1 上，无需逐动作调参；提供可在浏览器中选择动作和策略的演示；报告称单块 GPU 训练 3 小时即超过 SONIC 的归一化回报。

projects.content:
## Overview

SuperPlane is an open source AI software factory for routine engineering work\. It continuously scans codebases and backlogs to identify high\-confidence issues, applies workflow\-level guardrails, and coordinates coding agents, source control, CI, review, approvals, and feedback\. Verified changes are brought to human review, while ambiguous work stays with the team\.

## Key Features

- Continuous scanning of the codebase and backlog to find issues suitable for agent automation, ranked by confidence signals such as scope, available context, and test coverage\.
- Workflow\-level guardrails for allowed scope, required checks, review policies, approval points, and escalation paths, applied consistently to every run\.
- Failure handling that captures agent or CI failures, gives the agent actionable feedback, reruns required checks, and escalates when human judgment is needed\.
- Verification and review readiness, including agent review of merge confidence and remaining concerns before human approval\.
- Flexible operation with any model, cloud or on\-prem deployment, and coordination with existing source control, CI, and review tools\.

## Use Cases

- Automating focused bugs, maintenance work, paper cuts, test fixes, documentation updates, and small improvements with clear outcomes\.
- Turning high\-confidence backlog issues into verified, review\-ready pull requests\.
- Reducing engineer touchpoints and shortening the issue\-to\-reviewed\-PR cycle for routine work\.
- Applying consistent guardrails and approval policies to agent\-generated changes\.

## Getting Started

- Sign up for SuperPlane Cloud and create a workspace\.
- Connect a GitHub repository\.
- Choose a small bug, a test fix, or a documentation update for the first run; SuperPlane imports the issues and assesses which tasks are suitable for an agent\.
- Follow the quickstart for setup and read the product overview to learn how SuperPlane coordinates agents and verification\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- SuperPlane Cloud requires sign\-up, a workspace, and a connected GitHub repository for the initial setup\.
- Self\-hosting can use Docker Compose on one Linux VM\.
- Self\-hosting can use Kubernetes on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud\.
- SuperPlane coordinates existing coding agents, source control, CI, and review tools; it does not replace those existing tools or infrastructure\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- SuperPlane depends on the coding agents, source control, CI, and review tools already used by a team rather than replacing them\.
- Teams must define workflow guardrails such as allowed scope, checks, review policies, approvals, and escalation paths so SuperPlane can apply them consistently\.
- Ambiguous work or tasks requiring human judgment remain with the team rather than being fully automated\.
- When an agent or CI check still requires human judgment after failure feedback, the workflow pauses and escalates with context\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology for coding agents\. It steps back to draw out intent, presents design in digestible chunks, creates an implementation plan, then uses composable skills that trigger automatically to support implementation, testing, review, and branch completion\.

## Key Features

- Composable skills and initial instructions that make coding agents use the methodology automatically\.
- Workflow covers brainstorming, design approval, writing plans, subagent\-driven development or inline execution, test\-driven development, code review, and finishing a development branch\.
- Skills library includes testing, debugging, collaboration, and meta skills such as test\-driven\-development, systematic\-debugging, brainstorming, writing\-plans, executing\-plans, requesting\-code\-review, and writing\-skills\.
- Supports separate installation across many coding agent harnesses, including Claude Code, Codex App and CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code, and others\.
- Includes diagnosing\-superpowers for investigating session problems and packaging evidence for bug reports\.

## Use Cases

- Guiding a coding agent from initial idea through design, planning, implementation, review, and branch completion\.
- Running test\-driven development and subagent\-driven development workflows with review after each task\.
- Diagnosing a misbehaving agent session and producing evidence for a bug report\.
- Creating and testing new skills using the writing\-skills best practices\.

## Getting Started

- Installation differs by harness\. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one\.
- Claude Code: install from the official Claude plugin marketplace with /plugin install superpowers@claude\-plugins\-official\.
- Codex CLI: open the plugin search interface with /plugins, search for superpowers, and select Install Plugin\.
- Cursor: in Cursor Agent chat, install from the marketplace with /add\-plugin superpowers\.
- Devin CLI: install the plugin from this repository with devin plugins install obra/superpowers\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Superpowers must be installed separately for each coding agent harness in use\.
- Hermes users must restart active sessions after installing Superpowers\.
- Telemetry is enabled by default via a logo load that includes the Superpowers version\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Sure is a personal finance platform that brings tracking, transactions, budgeting, and an AI assistant into one place\. It is presented as open source and can be self\-hosted, with browser, macOS desktop, mobile app, API, and LLM\-agent access mentioned\.

## Key Features

- Link bank accounts, stocks, crypto, and other assets or debts in any currency, with manual and CSV import options also available\.
- Track, edit, filter, and automate transactions with custom categories, merchants, tags, and rules\.
- Set and customize category budgets, monitor balances and spending trends, and optimize allocations\.
- Ask an AI assistant questions about accounts, spending, net worth, and other financial topics\.
- Use charts to visualize assets and debts at a glance\.
- Self\-host with Docker and access the app through a browser, macOS desktop app, mobile app, API clients, and LLM agents\.

## Use Cases

- Consolidating bank, credit card, investment, and crypto accounts to view cash flow and net worth in one place\.
- Organizing and automating transaction categorization for monthly budgeting\.
- Monitoring category budgets and spending trends to adjust allocations\.
- Self\-hosting a personal finance app to keep account data under your control\.

## Getting Started

- For self\-hosting, follow the Docker hosting guide\.
- For local development, copy \.env\.local\.example to \.env\.local, run bin/setup and bin/dev, then visit http://localhost:3000\.
- Optionally load demo data with rake demo\_data:default; if loaded, log in with user@example\.com and Password1\!\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker is supported for self\-hosting the app\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is a community\-maintained fork of the abandoned Maybe Finance project\.
- Data\-heavy usage can surface performance issues, and the project provides a public dashboard for problematic requests\.
- Some AI deployment options rely on an external OpenAI token\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Survival LLM is a free AI assistant and emergency library that runs entirely on the user's computer\. It searches an offline library of medical, emergency, how\-to, repair, and encyclopedia articles, answers from what it finds, and shows the exact passages and articles used\. It is designed for blackout, first\-aid, water, food\-safety, and other emergency questions, and it can also search a user's own PDFs, Word documents, ebooks, web pages, and text files\.

## Key Features

- Works with no internet: the AI model and library live on the computer, and questions do not leave it\.
- Shows sources: every answer lists the articles read, and users can open an article with the exact passage highlighted\.
- Provides an emergency and reference library spanning medical references, FEMA and CDC guidance, survival manuals, how\-to guides, repair guides, and about 930,000 Wikipedia articles\.
- Selects an AI model based on computer memory, with more memory allowing a smarter model\.
- Searches personal files such as PDFs, Word documents, EPUB ebooks, web pages, and text files alongside the library\.
- Includes memory notes and reasoning controls so users can adjust how the assistant responds\.

## Use Cases

- Answering emergency questions about food safety in a blackout, burn treatment, water purification, generators, carbon monoxide, hypothermia, bleeding, and other first\-aid topics\.
- Checking official emergency and medical guidance from sources such as Ready\.gov, CDC, MedlinePlus, WikEM, and U\.S\. military manuals with cited passages\.
- Searching a generator manual, medicine list, family emergency plan, or other personal documents together with the built\-in library\.
- Using the assistant offline after initial setup when internet access is unavailable\.

## Getting Started

- Download the Mac or Windows build and unzip it\.
- Open Survival LLM; on Windows, open the extracted folder and double\-click Survival LLM\.bat\.
- During setup, pick a library and an AI model, then click Download; setup can resume if the internet drops or the app is quit\.
- Complete setup while online; after that the app needs no internet\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or newer) with macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, and on 64\-bit Windows 10 or 11\.
- Requires internet during initial setup; after setup it works with the internet off\.
- Free disk space must cover the chosen AI model plus 5 GB, plus extra space while the library installs\.
- Model downloads range from 6 GB to 80 GB depending on the computer's memory and platform; the Essentials library is about 1\.3 GB and the full library about 9 GB\.
- On Windows, the app downloads the Ollama AI engine (1\.6 GB) during setup; the Mac app has it built in\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- AI models can make mistakes, especially smaller models; the app exposes the articles used so answers can be checked\.
- The first launch may trigger an operating\-system warning because the app is not distributed through an app store\.

projects.descriptionZh: Surya 是 Datalab 推出的 689M 参数 OCR 模型，面向文档智能，支持 90 多种语言的 OCR、版面分析、阅读顺序与表格识别。
projects.content:
## Overview

Surya is a 689M\-parameter OCR model from Datalab that performs text recognition, layout analysis, reading order, and table recognition\. It supports 90\+ languages and is designed for document intelligence workloads across varied document types\.

## Key Features

- 689M\-parameter OCR model with text recognition and line\-level text detection\.
- Layout analysis for tables, images, headers, and other document elements, with reading order\.
- Table output as HTML, including merged cells as colspan and rowspan\.
- Multilingual support, scoring 74\.9% on an internal benchmark set of 91 languages\.
- Throughput of 4\.5 pages/s on one H100 at 192 DPI and 1\.7x Surya 2 with MTP\.

## Use Cases

- OCR of images, PDFs, or folders of images and PDFs into JSON with detected text and bounding boxes\.
- Layout analysis and reading\-order extraction for complex pages such as newspapers, forms, and academic papers\.
- Table recognition and HTML table output for documents with merged cells\.
- Multilingual document processing across 90\+ languages\.

## Getting Started

- Install with pip install surya\-ocr\.
- For NVIDIA GPU inference, install Docker and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit; for CPU or Apple Silicon, install the llama\-server binary from llama\.cpp\.
- Run surya\_ocr DATA\_PATH to write JSON with detected text and bounding boxes; DATA\_PATH can be an image, PDF, or folder of images or PDFs\.
- Optionally install streamlit and pdftext, then run surya\_gui for an interactive app\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- NVIDIA GPU inference requires Docker plus the NVIDIA Container Toolkit\.
- CPU or Apple Silicon inference requires the llama\-server binary from llama\.cpp\.
- Surya auto\-spawns the inference server on first use and can also point at an existing server via SURYA\_INFERENCE\_URL=http://host:port/v1\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- CPU or Apple Silicon inference involves llama\.cpp\.
- By default each command starts and stops the VLM server, so repeated commands incur startup and, on GPU, model\-load costs\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Surya 是 Datalab 推出的 689M 参数 OCR 模型，用于文档智能中的文本识别、版面分析、阅读顺序与表格识别，支持 90 多种语言，适用于多种文档类型。

## 核心功能

- 689M 参数 OCR 模型，支持文本识别与行级文本检测；提供表格、图像、页眉等版面元素分析，并给出阅读顺序；表格以 HTML 输出，合并单元格以 colspan 与 rowspan 表示；支持多语言，在 91 种语言的内部基准集上得分 74\.9%；在单张 H100、192 DPI 下吞吐量为 4\.5 页/秒，采用 MTP 时较 Surya 2 提升 1\.7 倍。

## 适用场景

- 将图片、PDF 或图片与 PDF 文件夹中的文档 OCR 为带检测文本和边界框的 JSON；对报纸、表单、学术论文等复杂页面进行版面分析与阅读顺序提取；对含合并单元格的文档进行表格识别并输出 HTML 表格；处理 90 多种语言的多语言文档。

## 快速开始

- 使用 pip install surya\-ocr 安装；NVIDIA GPU 推理需安装 Docker 与 NVIDIA Container Toolkit，CPU 或 Apple Silicon 需安装 llama\.cpp 的 llama\-server；运行 surya\_ocr DATA\_PATH 可将图片、PDF 或图片与 PDF 文件夹中的检测文本和边界框写入 JSON；可选安装 streamlit 与 pdftext 后运行 surya\_gui 启动交互式应用。

## 部署与要求

- NVIDIA GPU 推理需要 Docker 与 NVIDIA Container Toolkit；CPU 或 Apple Silicon 推理需要 llama\.cpp 的 llama\-server 二进制；Surya 首次使用时会自动启动推理服务器，也可通过 SURYA\_INFERENCE\_URL 指向已有服务器。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：Apache\-2\.0。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

SWE\-agent enables your language model of choice to autonomously use tools to fix issues in real GitHub repositories, find cybersecurity vulnerabilities, or perform any custom task\. It is built and maintained by researchers from Princeton University and Stanford University\.

## Key Features

- State of the art on SWE\-bench among open\-source projects
- Free\-flowing and generalizable: leaves maximal agency to the language model
- Configurable and fully documented: governed by a single YAML file
- Made for research: simple and hackable by design
- Supports multimodal input for processing images from GitHub issues with vision\-capable models

## Use Cases

- Fixing issues in real GitHub repositories
- Finding cybersecurity vulnerabilities (offensive cybersecurity / CTF challenges)
- Performing custom coding tasks and competitive coding challenges

## Getting Started

- Install from source or try it in your browser via GitHub Codespaces\. See the documentation for installation and hello world tutorials\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires a language model API key (e\.g\., GPT\-4o or Claude Sonnet 4) and a Python environment\. Configuration is done via a single YAML file\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- SWE\-agent has been superseded by mini\-swe\-agent and is now in maintenance\-only mode\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Switch AI is a self\-hostable platform for managing an agentic workforce\. It brings AI agents from any vendor into shared rooms with people, using the chat tools teams already use, and adds safety checks, cost and return visibility, and improvement recommendations\.

## Key Features

- Each chat channel can become a shared room where people and agents work from the same conversation, decisions, and documents in Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, or Mattermost\.
- Supports any agent, model, or provider that speaks the protocol, so teams can keep tools such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or LangChain agents\.
- Agents can be given roles, instructions, and tools such as Google Workspace, Jira, and GitHub, with access limited to the rooms they belong to\.
- Self\-hosting keeps team context with the company and lets teams change agents, models, or vendors without losing that context\.
- Switch Trust scans, tests, and guards agents, while Switch ROI shows what each agent costs and delivers and recommends improvements\.
- Permissions let teams decide who can talk to which agent and in which rooms\.

## Use Cases

- Cross\-timezone engineering collaboration, where an agent can open a pull request and a human reviews and merges it\.
- Incident response, where agents open an incident channel, pull error rates, identify the deploy, and chart data\.
- Customer onboarding and support, using shared rooms and runbooks that agents can answer from and correct when needed\.
- Vendor review and finance or operations work, with room\-level cost visibility through Switch ROI\.

## Getting Started

- Install Switch Console, the desktop app, for macOS, Windows, or Linux\.
- Open Switch Console and talk to switch\-buddy, which creates the first agents and channels, helps connect the team's chat app, and answers questions about Switch\.
- Use the getting\-started documentation to go from the first agent to the first channel, and the hosting documentation to deploy Switch for a team\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-host Switch on your own servers so team context stays with the company\.
- Switch Console desktop builds are available for macOS, Windows, and Linux x64 and ARM64\.
- Bring existing agent harnesses and models; Switch does not ship agents or models\.
- Connect the chat platform the team uses: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, or Mattermost\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Switch does not provide agents or models; teams must supply and operate their own agent harnesses and models\.
- The project states that there is still significant work to shape\.

projects.content:
## Overview

T3 Code is an open\-source control plane for coding agents\. It orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cursor, and Grok from one surface, with desktop, web, and mobile apps\. Bring your own subscription and fork the whole thing\.

## Key Features

- Orchestrates multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity) from one surface\.
- Bring your own subscription \- no token reselling, no quota caps\.
- One\-button PR creation with auto\-generated titles, bodies, and changelog, including draft and stack PRs\.
- Fully open source (MIT) and forkable \- customize UI, add agents, self\-host\.
- Available on desktop (Electron), web, and mobile (iOS/Android) with remote access\.

## Use Cases

- Remote development from mobile or another machine\.
- Unified control of multiple coding agents with existing subscriptions\.
- Streamlined PR workflow with auto\-generated PRs\.
- Customizing and forking the control plane for personal or team use\.

## Getting Started

- Install via the command line installer or package manager (winget, Homebrew, \.deb, AUR)\. After installation, authenticate at least one supported provider\. Run \`t3\` to start the server and open the local web app\. For desktop, download from GitHub Releases\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires at least one supported coding agent provider (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, or Antigravity) installed and authenticated on the machine\. Can be run as a background service\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Project is at an early stage and may contain bugs\.
- Contributions are mostly not accepted yet; only small fixes may be considered\.
